sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: Which mental and physical driving abilities does marijuana impair, and what does that do to crash risk?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: Marijuana affects both thinking skills, such as judging and planning, and physical skills, such as coordination, reaction time and tracking, so driving while impaired by it raises the risk of death or injury.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: Which four factors control how strongly marijuana impairs a person?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: How impaired marijuana makes you depends on the dose, the time since use, the individual, and the way it was consumed.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: How reliably does a measured THC reading in blood, breath, or saliva reflect actual driving impairment?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: Unlike alcohol, the amount of THC measured in blood, breath or saliva does not track how impaired a person actually is.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: Why does observed driving behavior carry extra weight in marijuana cases compared with alcohol BAC cases?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: For alcohol, BAC roughly reflects impairment, but for marijuana the measured THC level does not, which is why behavior evidence matters so much.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: What blood THC concentration lets a Colorado jury or court draw a permissible inference of DUI?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: Colorado law allows a permissible inference of DUI when a driver has five nanograms of THC per milliliter of blood.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: Does DWAI have a blood THC inference number, and how are most marijuana-impaired drivers convicted?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: There is no THC inference level for DWAI, and most marijuana-impaired drivers are convicted on their behavior together with blood THC results.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: Between DUI and DWAI, where does Colorado's five-nanogram blood THC inference apply and where does it not?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: The THC inference of five nanograms per milliliter of blood applies to DUI only; DWAI has no THC inference level at all.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: What does polydrug impairment mean, and why is combining substances before driving especially dangerous?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: Polydrug impairment means using two or more drugs at once, in any mix of alcohol, marijuana, prescription, over-the-counter or other drugs, and the mix can strengthen the effects.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: How do illegal drugs like LSD, methamphetamine, and heroin distort a driver's reflexes, confidence, or alertness?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: Illegal drugs such as LSD, methamphetamine and heroin harm reflexes, judgment and alertness, and can either create false confidence or leave you too drowsy to react.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: Can a driver escape conviction because a specific drug was unusual or showed only a tiny amount in fluids?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: Officers are trained to recognize and testify about impaired driving from any cause, and drivers are convicted regardless of which drug was involved or how much was found in blood or saliva.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: Which three major consequences can follow any alcohol or drug driving offense in Colorado?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: Penalties for alcohol or drug driving offenses are severe and can include jail, fines and loss of driving privileges.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: What is Colorado's rule on plea bargaining an alcohol or drug driving charge down, and what is your only sure safeguard?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: Colorado does not allow plea bargaining an alcohol or drug driving offense down, so the only sure protection is never driving after using alcohol or drugs.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: Under Colorado's Express Consent Law, what agreement do you make automatically whenever you drive in the state?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: Under the Express Consent Law (C.R.S. forty-two-four-one thousand three hundred one point one), driving in Colorado means you have agreed to a chemical test for alcohol or drugs.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: Which four body-fluid or breath samples can an officer require when impaired driving is suspected?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: When an officer suspects impaired driving, you can be required to give a blood, breath, saliva or urine sample for testing.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: Why is it a mistake to think Colorado's Express Consent Law applies only to breathalyzers?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: Express consent covers blood, breath, saliva and urine tests, not only a breath test.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: What license revocation and ignition-interlock requirements hit if you refuse or fail to cooperate with testing?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: Refusing or failing to cooperate with the chemical test leads to a one-year license revocation plus a two-year requirement to use an ignition interlock on any vehicle you drive.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: When does an ignition interlock demand breath samples, and how does it respond to elevated alcohol?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: An ignition interlock requires a breath sample before the engine starts and repeat samples while driving, and the vehicle will not start if it detects elevated alcohol.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: How are other suspensions or revocations from the same stop scheduled alongside a test-refusal revocation?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: Any other suspension or revocation from the same incident is added after the refusal revocation ends, served consecutively.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: Keep straight which refusal sanction lasts one year and which lasts two years?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: Refusing a chemical test brings two different time periods: one year of revocation and two years of ignition interlock use.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: Do extra suspensions from the same incident run concurrently with a refusal revocation or tack onto the end?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: Penalties from the same incident do not run at the same time as the refusal revocation; they are added onto its end.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: Which five personal qualities and sensory habits does safe driving require before you turn the key?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: Safe driving requires clear vision, being rested, being sober and drug-free, general good health, and mental and emotional fitness, while using all your senses to notice danger.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: Why is sharp eyesight central to driving, and how often should a specialist check your vision?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: Good vision is essential because you drive on what you see; have your eyes checked by a specialist every year or two.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: What must you wear on every single trip if your driver license lists a corrective lens restriction?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: If your license carries a corrective lens restriction, you must wear your glasses or contacts whenever you drive.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: How should you break up long road trips, and what should you do whenever drowsiness creeps in?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: Fatigue slows reactions and decisions, so split long drives into two-hour segments and pull off the road to rest if you get drowsy.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: Separate the number two in Colorado's eye-specialist advice from its long-drive fatigue rule?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: The eye exam advice is every year or two, while the fatigue advice is to break long drives into two-hour segments; do not swap these intervals.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: Why can even a driver with healthy ears miss sirens or horns outside the car?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: Being able to hear does not guarantee you will notice outside sounds, since music, talking passengers or a well-insulated car can mute them, and hearing can decline slowly with age or noise.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: How does Colorado define the earphones you are barred from wearing while driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: You may not drive wearing earphones, meaning any device that covers all or part of both ears.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: Which five medical, helmet, or single-ear devices do not count as prohibited earphones?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: Hearing aids, cochlear implants, assistive listening devices, speakers built into protective headgear, and a single-ear wireless device do not count as earphones.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: Why does a wireless earpiece in one ear stay legal under Colorado's earphone ban?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: The earphone ban covers devices on both ears, so a single-ear wireless device and hearing aids remain legal.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: How can everyday aches or chronic medical conditions affect your driving, and whom should you ask when unsure?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: Even minor health problems such as a cold, stiff neck, cough or sore leg can hurt your driving, and conditions like epilepsy, diabetes or heart trouble can make driving unsafe, so ask your doctor if unsure.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: Which strong emotions can degrade your driving judgment, and what aggressive reaction must you never give in to?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: Strong emotions such as worry, excitement, fear or anger can degrade your driving, and you should never give in to road rage.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: What is the number-one cause of driver error, and how does the Colorado handbook define it?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: Distraction is the leading cause of driver error, defined as anything that pulls your attention from driving, even for a moment.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: Which four sources of distraction does the handbook warn against—including rubbernecking—and how do you handle urgent tasks?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: Avoid distraction from your phone, passengers, children or rubbernecking, which means staring at something of interest, and pull over safely to handle anything urgent.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: Who bears legal responsibility for vehicle upkeep, and what four consequences can poor maintenance bring?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: Drivers are responsible for keeping their vehicle safe; a poorly maintained car costs more, can break down or crash, and can earn you a citation.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: What should you do immediately if your brakes feel off, and which four exterior light groups must work?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: If the brakes seem wrong, have a mechanic check them right away, and make sure turn signals, brake lights, tail lights and headlights all work.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: Which four maintenance habits keep your windshield, wipers, washer tank, and side glass ready for clear vision?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Replace a damaged windshield and worn wiper blades, keep the glass clean inside and out with the washer tank full, and clear snow, ice or frost from every window.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: Which four driving hazards come from running worn or bald tires?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: Worn or bald tires lengthen stopping distance, make turning harder, invite hydroplaning on wet roads and raise the chance of a flat.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: How do underinflated or unbalanced tires hurt your car, and which three warning signs call for a tire shop?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: Low tire pressure and unbalanced wheels wear tires faster, cut fuel economy and make steering and stopping harder; a bouncing car, shaking wheel or pull to one side means get the tires checked.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: What symptom calls for a mechanic to inspect your steering versus your suspension?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: Have a mechanic look at the steering if the car is hard to turn, and at the suspension if it bounces too much or keeps bouncing after a bump or a stop.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: How do you tell whether a bouncing car needs a tire check or a suspension check?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: A bouncing car points to two possible checks: tires when it bounces with a shaking wheel or pull, suspension when it keeps bouncing after a bump or stop.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: Why must you never idle an engine inside a garage or sit in a running parked car with closed windows?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: Exhaust fumes from a leak can kill very quickly, so never run the engine in a garage or sit in a running car without a window open.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: Which five problems can an out-of-tune engine cause, and what warning device needs regular testing?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: A poorly tuned engine may lose power, fail to start, waste fuel, pollute and stall in traffic; the horn should also be checked regularly.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: What adjustments, cabin cleanup, and buckle checks belong before shifting out of Park?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: Before you set off, adjust your seat, mirrors, radio and temperature, secure loose items, and make sure everyone, especially children, is in an age-appropriate restraint.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: Where do you lean your head—and what should barely show—when aiming the driver-side mirror?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: Set the driver-side mirror with your head against the left window so the side of the car is barely visible at the left edge of the mirror.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: Where do you position your head when aiming the passenger-side mirror?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: Set the passenger-side mirror with your head centered under the inside rearview mirror, or just above the center console, so the side of the car just shows at the right edge.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: How does your head lean change between setting the left side mirror and the right side mirror?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: Mirror setup differs by side: for the left mirror your head touches the left window, for the right mirror your head is centered under the inside mirror.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: Why must you clear loose items off the rear shelf, back seat, and driver floorboard?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: Remove loose objects from the rear shelf and back seat that could hurt someone in a sudden stop, and from the floor where they could roll under the pedals.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: How close should your seat's head restraint sit behind your head?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: Adjust the head restraint so it touches the back of your head.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: Regardless of vehicle make or model, where does your right foot belong when starting the engine, and what do you scan next?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: Whatever the make or model, keep your right foot on the brake when starting the vehicle, then check the indicator lights and gauges for maintenance warnings.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: What check-and-signal sequence precedes pulling out, and which parts of your foot work the gas?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: To pull away, find a safe path, check for traffic and pedestrians to the sides and rear, signal, then press the accelerator gently with the ball of your foot while your heel rests on the floor.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: How does your right foot's placement differ between starting the car and pressing the gas?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: When pressing the accelerator, the ball of the foot works the pedal while the heel stays on the floor; when starting the engine, the right foot is on the brake.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: What three-step sequence brings your vehicle to a smooth, safe stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: To stop, check your mirrors for traffic behind, move your foot from the accelerator to the brake, and press with steady pressure until the vehicle stops.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: Which way do you turn the steering wheel to guide your car—forward or in reverse?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: Always turn the steering wheel toward the direction you want the vehicle to go, whether moving forward or backing up.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: Does backing up invert which direction you turn the steering wheel?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: Steering in reverse follows the same rule as forward driving: turn the wheel toward where you want the vehicle to go.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: Which two clock-face hand placements on the outside of the wheel give optimal control in Colorado?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: For best control, hold the outside of the wheel on opposite sides at the three and nine o'clock or the four and eight o'clock positions.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: Why shouldn't you pick ten-and-two o'clock on a Colorado permit question about steering hand placement?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: The two approved hand positions are three and nine o'clock or four and eight o'clock; the classic ten-and-two answer is not what this handbook gives.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: How should your fingers and thumbs rest on the steering wheel, and what rim grip must you avoid?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: Grip the wheel firmly but gently with your fingers rather than your palms, keep your thumbs up along the face of the wheel, and never hold the inside of the rim while turning.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: Before climbing into the driver seat to back out, what outside check should you make and why?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Before you get in to back up, look behind the vehicle, because small children and small objects cannot be seen from the driver seat.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: Where do your brake foot, left hand, right arm, and eyes belong when backing straight back?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: To reverse, keep a foot on the brake while shifting, grip the top of the wheel, the twelve o'clock spot, with your left hand, rest your right arm on the passenger seat back and look over your shoulder out the rear window.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: Why shouldn't a rearview camera replace mirrors and turning your head when reversing?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: Mirrors do not show the space right behind the car, so a rear-view camera, if you have one, is used together with mirrors and an over-the-shoulder look, never instead of them.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: How fast should you reverse, where do you glance during a backing turn, and how long do you keep looking back?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: Back up slowly and smoothly, steering a little toward where the rear should go; when turning in reverse, glance quickly to the front and sides and keep looking back until fully stopped.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: Beyond lights, posts, and paint, which three people on the street legally direct traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: Traffic is controlled by signals, signs and pavement markings, and also by police, highway workers and school crossing guards, whose directions you are required to follow.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: From top to bottom, how are standard three-lens traffic lights arranged?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: Signal lights are normally arranged with red at the top, yellow in the middle and green at the bottom, though some places use a single red, yellow or green light.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: How must every driver treat an intersection whose traffic lights have gone dark or malfunctioned?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: If a traffic signal is dark or not working properly, handle the intersection as a four-way stop.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: When storm outages knock out a signal, does the wider multi-lane arterial keep priority over the side street?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: A dark or broken signal is handled as a four-way stop, not as a green light for the busier road.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: What must you do at a steady red light, and what conditions allow turning right on red?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: At a steady red light, stop and wait for green; after stopping and yielding to pedestrians and traffic, a right turn on red is allowed unless a sign forbids it.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: Under what exact street layout—and after what steps—is turning left on a steady red light legal in Colorado?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: Turning left on red is legal only when both streets are one-way, going from one onto the other, after you stop and yield, and only if no sign prohibits it.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: Why is turning right on red common while turning left on red applies to far fewer corners?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: Right on red is allowed at most intersections after a full stop, but left on red works only when turning from one one-way street into a second one.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: What does a steady round yellow light warn, and what action does it call for?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: A steady yellow light warns that red is coming next, so stop unless you are already inside the intersection.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: Before moving straight or turning on a steady green light, whom must you yield to?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: On a steady green you may go straight or turn either way unless a sign bans the turn, but first yield to any vehicle or pedestrian already in the intersection or the crosswalk next to it.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: May you stop and make a turn in the direction of a lit steady red arrow?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: A lit red arrow means stop, and you may not turn in the direction it points.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: What happens to your turn privilege when a green arrow clicks off while the round green ball stays lit?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: A green arrow, shown alone or with another light, lets you turn the way it points; if the arrow goes dark while the round green stays on, you may still turn after yielding to through traffic and pedestrians unless a sign or red arrow forbids it.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: How does a green arrow turning off alongside a green ball differ from a red arrow lighting up?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: If the green arrow goes out but the round green remains, the turn is still allowed, now only after yielding; a red arrow means no turn that way at all.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: What is about to appear after a steady yellow arrow, and what should you do?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: A steady yellow arrow warns that a red arrow is about to appear, so stop unless you are already in the intersection.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: What does a flashing yellow left-turn arrow allow, and what two phases follow it?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: A flashing yellow arrow lets a left-turning driver go carefully only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians; it then turns solid yellow, meaning do not enter if you can stop safely, and finally red, meaning stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: Which everyday roadside control matches the exact rule for a flashing red signal light?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: Treat a flashing red light exactly like a stop sign: come to a stop, then move on once pedestrians and other traffic have been given the right of way.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: After coming to a full stop, how does a steady red light differ from a flashing red light?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: Steady red means stop and wait for green, while flashing red means stop and then proceed when clear, just as at a stop sign.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: How should you respond when approaching a plain flashing yellow light?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard ahead, so slow down and continue with caution.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: What separates the meaning of a plain flashing yellow light from a flashing yellow arrow?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: Flashing yellow light and flashing yellow arrow differ: the plain flashing light warns of a hazard, while the flashing arrow permits a left turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and walkers.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: What does HAWK stand for, and what triggers its yellow-and-red sequence?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: A HAWK signal, short for High Intensity Activated Crosswalk, helps pedestrians cross by flashing a yellow and red sequence that tells drivers someone needs to cross.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: Which five kinds of travel info do road signs convey, and why do their shapes and colors matter?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: Signs tell you rules, hazards, where you are, directions and nearby services, and a sign's shape and color show what kind of message it carries.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: What colors mark regulatory signs, what do they communicate, and what happens if you ignore one?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: Regulatory signs state the law at a location, use black or red on a white background, and disobeying one is a traffic violation.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: What two speed bounds can speed-limit panels post, and when is driving at the posted maximum too fast?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: Speed limit signs give the highest or lowest speed allowed; the highest limit assumes ideal conditions, so you must slow down when conditions demand it.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: At what exact spot do you stop at a stop post when there is a stop line, only a crosswalk, or neither?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: At a stop sign, stop completely at the marked stop line; with no line, stop before the near-side crosswalk; with neither, stop at the point closest to the cross road where you can see approaching traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: What is the one-two-three fallback order for picking your stopping point at a stop post?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: The stopping point at a stop sign follows an order: the stop line first, then the near-side crosswalk, then the spot nearest the cross road with a view of traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: What two speed actions can a yield post require, and who goes first?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: A yield sign means slow down, or stop if needed, to let every pedestrian and any vehicle that has the right of way go first.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: What critical mistake do Do Not Enter and Wrong Way panels catch, and what is the rule?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: Do Not Enter and Wrong Way signs warn and turn back drivers heading the wrong way on a street or freeway ramp; never drive past one.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: What rule does a One Way arrow panel set for every lane on that roadway?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: A One Way sign means you may travel only in the direction its arrow points.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: How does the job of a One Way panel differ from Do Not Enter and Wrong Way panels?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: A One Way sign tells you which single direction a street allows, while Do Not Enter and Wrong Way signs tell a driver already facing the wrong direction to go no further.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: Where are lane control panels mounted, and what do their curved or straight arrows dictate?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: Lane control signs, placed beside or above the road and often using arrows, show where you may turn; similar arrows are sometimes painted on the pavement.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: What do prohibited-action panels communicate to drivers approaching an intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: Prohibited signs show an action you may not take, such as making a U-turn or a left turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: Which two background colors mark warning panels, and what kinds of upcoming hazards do they preview?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: Warning signs are yellow or fluorescent green with black symbols and alert you to things like school zones, curves, slippery pavement, merging traffic or busy pedestrian areas; a merge sign, for example, warns of cars joining from a side street.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.front: What does a yellow advisory speed plaque tell you approaching a curve, corner, or exit ramp?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.expected_back: Advisory speed signs are cautionary signs giving the safe speed for curves, corners and off-ramps under ideal conditions.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.front: Which three rules—about racing, far-side space, and shifting gears—apply at every railroad crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.expected_back: Railroad crossing signs come in several shapes; never race a train, never start across until there is room for your whole vehicle beyond the far side, and do not shift gears on the tracks in case the engine stalls.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.front: What two critical pieces of information appear on the blue Emergency Notification System plaque at every rail crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.expected_back: Blue railroad emergency notification system signs at every highway-rail grade crossing list a phone number for reporting problems, and the Department of Transportation number printed below it identifies that exact crossing.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.front: What color combination marks work-zone panels, and what do they team up with to protect road crews?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.expected_back: Work zone signs are orange with black letters or symbols and are used with other devices or flaggers to steer traffic through work areas and protect road workers.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.front: What background color marks guide panels, and what two travel details do they display?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.expected_back: Guide signs have a green background and give directions and mileage to particular destinations.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.front: How do blue roadside panels differ in purpose from brown roadside panels?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.expected_back: Blue signs direct you to service facilities, while brown signs mark recreational, historic or cultural areas.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: How do five background colors—yellow or fluorescent green, orange, green, blue, and brown—pair with their message types?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: Warning signs are yellow or fluorescent green, work zone signs are orange, guide signs are green, service signs are blue and recreation signs are brown.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: Which four highway systems can you tell apart just from the outline shape of a route marker?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: The shape of a route sign or marker tells you what kind of road you are on: Interstate, U.S., State or County highway.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: What colors appear on combined bicycle-and-pedestrian crossing panels, and what spot do they mark?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: Bicycle and pedestrian crossing signs are black symbols on yellow and mark places, such as a shared use path meeting a road, where both bicyclists and walkers may cross.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: How much clearance must you give when passing any bicyclist in Colorado, and does a reminder panel need to be posted?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: When passing or overtaking a bicyclist on any road, a driver must leave at least three feet of clearance, whether or not a white Pass three feet min sign is posted.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: Why does a white Bicycle May Use Full Lane panel remind drivers that cyclists sometimes ride mid-lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.memory_hook: Hazards or sight make right unsafe
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: A white Bicycle May Use Full Lane sign reminds drivers that a bicyclist may ride in the middle of the lane when hazards or poor visibility would make riding on the right side unsafe.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: What design speed does a reflective orange triangle on the rear of a vehicle indicate?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle marks it as built to travel slower than twenty-five miles per hour.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: Which vehicles are legally allowed to use stalls marked with disabled parking posts and pavement symbols?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: Disabled parking signs, and markings painted in the space, reserve those spots for vehicles showing a disabled parking permit.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: What is the painted crosshatched zone beside a disabled parking stall used for, and when may someone park on it?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: The crosshatched area next to a disabled space is for van access only, and no one may park there at any time.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: Does hanging a valid disabled placard on your mirror allow parking on the striped van-access crosshatch?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: A van-access crosshatch beside a disabled space is never a parking spot, even for a vehicle with a placard.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: When driving a car that has a disabled placard or plate, what must be true for you to park in an accessible stall?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: You may park in a disabled space only when the person who holds the placard is getting into or out of the vehicle.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: What charge, fine range, and extra penalties hit if you park in a disabled stall without a placard or plate?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: Parking in a disabled space without a placard or plate can be charged as a misdemeanor, with a three hundred fifty dollars to five thousand dollars fine on conviction, plus possible jail, loss of driving privileges or impoundment of the car.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: What four penalties apply in Colorado if you use someone else's disabled placard or plate to park?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: Using somebody else's placard or plate to park in a disabled space brings jail time, loss of driving privileges, towing and fines twice the normal amounts.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: How does Colorado punish parking with a borrowed placard compared with parking with no placard at all?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: A borrowed placard is punished more heavily than having none: fines double plus jail, loss of privileges and towing.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: Which five traffic-guiding jobs do painted lines and symbols handle on the pavement?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: Pavement lines and symbols divide lanes, show where passing and lane changes are allowed, mark turn lanes and pedestrian walkways, and show where to stop for signals or signs.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: What traffic flows do yellow lines divide, and what does a single broken yellow line permit?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: Yellow lines divide traffic going in opposite directions; a broken yellow line means passing is allowed.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: What does a single or double solid yellow line prohibit, and what special overtaking exception applies?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: A solid yellow line, or a pair of solid yellow lines, means no passing, except that you may pass a bicyclist with at least three feet of room when the oncoming lane is clear.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: When a solid yellow stripe runs beside a broken yellow stripe, when may you pass and when must you finish?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: With a solid and a broken yellow line side by side, you may not pass if the solid line is on your side, but may pass safely if the broken line is on your side, returning to your lane before the broken line becomes solid.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: In a mixed pair of center yellow stripes, which of the two lines governs your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: In a mixed yellow pair only the line nearest you counts: solid on your side means no passing, broken on your side means passing is allowed when safe.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: Which two everyday maneuvers legally let you cross a solid yellow centerline when oncoming traffic is clear?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: Crossing a solid yellow line is allowed, when safe, for a left turn into a driveway, alley or private road, or to get around a bicyclist with three or more feet of room.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: Why isn't 'never cross solid yellow for any reason' a true statement under Colorado rules?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Solid yellow still has two exceptions when safe: turning left into a driveway, alley or private road, and getting around a bicyclist with three or more feet of room.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: Which traffic direction do white lines divide, and how does broken white differ from solid white?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: White lines separate lanes moving the same way: a broken white line allows a safe lane change, and a solid white line means stay in your lane and also marks the road shoulder.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: How does glancing at lane-line color tell you immediately which way adjacent traffic is moving?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: Line color answers who is beside you: yellow separates opposite directions, white separates lanes going your way.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: What does bright green pavement paint designate on a city street?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: Green paint marks a lane or area set aside for bicyclists and makes riders more visible.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: What do painted sharrows warn drivers about lane width, and where may cyclists ride there?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: Sharrows, or shared lane markings, warn that a lane may be too narrow for a car and a bicycle side by side, and bicyclists may ride in the center of such a lane or whenever they must avoid obstacles or be seen.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: Who holds the right-of-way inside painted or unpainted crosswalks, and what must approaching drivers do?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: A crosswalk, marked or unmarked, is where pedestrians have the right-of-way, and drivers must slow down or stop as needed for people crossing in it.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: When a car ahead stops at a crosswalk, what is prohibited and where must you stop on a multi-lane street?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: If a vehicle ahead is stopped at a crosswalk, you may not pass it; stop behind it, or behind the crosswalk in the next lane on a multi-lane road.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: What do broken lines called conflict zones along a bike lane or bus lane warn about?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: Conflict zones are broken lines in a bike or bus lane warning drivers and bicyclists that their paths will cross there.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: Which side of the roadway—and how many lanes—should your vehicle occupy in normal driving?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: As a general rule, drive on the right half of the road and keep to a single lane without straddling two.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: How do you position your car and handle turns or passes on an unmarked roadway with zero lane stripes?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.expected_back: On a road with no lane signs or markings, drive just right of the center, stay off the shoulder, and follow the same passing and turning rules as on marked roads.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: What are restricted lanes, and what common painted pavement emblem marks them?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: Restricted lanes, such as transit or bicycle lanes, are reserved for a special use shown by signs or markings, often a white diamond painted in the lane or a roadside sign.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: Who holds the right-of-way inside a bike lane, and which four car actions are banned there?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: Bike lanes are only for bicyclists and other authorized users, who have the right-of-way there; drivers may not drive, idle, park in or otherwise block a bike lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: When bike-lane stripes pause across the middle of an intersection, does the bike lane end there?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: A bike lane continues through an intersection even where no paint joins the two sides.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: Which vehicles are transit lanes primarily built for, and can regular cars ever touch them?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: Transit lanes are parts of the street marked by signs and markings for buses or light rail, sometimes with limited use by other vehicles allowed.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: How are High Occupancy Vehicle lanes marked on pavement, and how do you know if your car qualifies?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: High Occupancy Vehicle lanes carry a painted white diamond, and signs state which vehicles may use them and how many occupants each needs.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: Why must you read the accompanying roadside panel whenever you spot a white diamond painted in a lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: A white diamond can mark an HOV lane or another restricted lane, so read the sign to learn who may use it.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: What is a two-way center left-turn lane strictly used for, and what two misuses are illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: A two-way left-turn lane, or center turn lane, is only for drivers turning left from either direction; you may wait in it until the turn is safe but may not use it to pass or travel.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: On a street equipped with a shared center turn lane, from which lane must every left turn be made?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: If a street has a shared center turn lane, every left turn must be made from that lane and not from any other.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: What two strict rules govern a shared center left-turn lane—both inside it and beside it?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.memory_hook: Never cruise inside, always turn from
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: A center turn lane is for waiting to turn left, not for passing or driving along, and it also removes the option of turning left from other lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.front: How do reversible lanes work across the day, and what yellow line pattern sets them apart?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.expected_back: Reversible lanes carry traffic one way at some times and the other way at other times, and are set apart by a barrier or double broken yellow lines, sometimes with signs or special lights.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: How do double broken yellow lines differ in meaning from a shared center left-turn lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: Double broken yellow lines signal a reversible lane, which differs from a center turn lane used only for left turns.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.front: How does a diverging diamond interchange move traffic onto freeway ramps without left-turn conflicts?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.expected_back: A diverging diamond interchange shifts traffic to the opposite side of the road across the interchange so vehicles can move onto freeway ramps without interruption.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.front: Which side of the center island do you pass on in a roundabout, and who yields at the entrance?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.expected_back: In a roundabout, traffic circles to the right around a center island, and drivers entering yield to traffic already circulating.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.front: Which four large vehicles get special statutory yield priority in Colorado roundabouts, and what happens when two meet?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.expected_back: Colorado law requires you to yield to a truck, bus, emergency vehicle or recreational vehicle entering, leaving or driving in a roundabout, and when two such large vehicles meet there, the one on the right yields to the one on the left.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.front: When no large trucks or buses are around, whom do you yield to entering a roundabout and when do you stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.expected_back: Approaching a roundabout with no large trucks present, yield to traffic coming from the left, and do not stop fully unless traffic keeps you from merging.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.front: Whom must you yield to when entering or leaving a roundabout, and when do you use turn signals?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.expected_back: Each time you enter or exit a roundabout, give way to anyone walking or riding in a crosswalk and to vehicles already circling, and use turn signals to change lanes and to exit.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: What are the three priority layers to watch every time you use a Colorado roundabout?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: Roundabout yielding has layers: large vehicles first, then circulating traffic on the left, and crosswalk users whenever you enter or leave.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: What do right-of-way rules settle when drivers or walkers meet without traffic lights or posts?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: Right-of-way rules decide who goes first and who waits when drivers or pedestrians meet where no sign or signal controls traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: Does Colorado law ever grant someone automatic right-of-way—even when facing a green light?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: The law only says who must yield; it never grants anyone the right-of-way, not even a driver facing a green light.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: Whom must you let clear first whenever you roll up toward an intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: You must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and drivers who are already inside an intersection you are approaching.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: Why must you hold back on a brand-new green light if someone is still crossing the box?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: A green light lets you go but does not give you the right-of-way; anyone already in the intersection still goes first.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: Regardless of who broke a yielding rule, who stays responsible for preventing a collision?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: No matter who has the right-of-way, every driver is still responsible for avoiding a crash.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: Where do walkers hold priority over cars, and what braking action must you take for them?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians, who have the right-of-way at every intersection and crosswalk; come to a full stop and let them pass safely.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: Which three pedestrian groups need extra patience, and what dangerous assumption must you avoid?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: Take extra care around children, seniors and people with disabilities, and never assume a pedestrian can see or hear your vehicle or a crossing signal.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: What two visual cues usually show that a pedestrian is blind or deaf-blind?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: A white cane or a guide dog is the usual sign that a pedestrian is blind or deaf-blind.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: How do a cyclist's legal rights and duties shift between riding on asphalt versus using a sidewalk or crosswalk?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: On the road a bicycle counts as a vehicle with many of the rights and duties of a motor vehicle, but a bicyclist on a sidewalk or in a crosswalk has the rights and duties of a pedestrian.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: Where does Colorado law treat someone on a bicycle like a pedestrian rather than a vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: A bicyclist on the roadway is treated as a vehicle, but the same rider in a crosswalk or on a sidewalk is treated as a pedestrian.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: What is your yielding duty whenever you merge into or turn across a marked bike lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: When you merge with or cross a designated bike lane to make a turn, you must yield to bicyclists in that lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: Who moves first at a four-way stop, and how do two simultaneous arrivals break the tie?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: At a four-way stop the first vehicle to arrive goes first; if vehicles arrive together, the one on the left yields to the one on the right.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: What defines an uncontrolled intersection, and which car goes first when two reach it together?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: An uncontrolled intersection has no stop signs or lights; when vehicles reach it at the same moment, the vehicle on the left lets the vehicle on the right go first.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: What exact tie-breaker rule connects four-way stops and uncontrolled intersections?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: Four-way stop and uncontrolled intersection share the same tie-break: when two arrive together, the driver on the left waits for the driver on the right.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: Besides crosswalk walkers, which slim oncoming riders need careful speed-and-distance checks before a left turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: Before turning left, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to smaller oncoming road users like bicyclists and motorcyclists, judging their speed and distance carefully.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: In what sole two intersection situations does a left-turning driver not yield to oncoming traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: A left-turning driver yields to all oncoming traffic unless holding a green arrow or having arrived first at a four-way stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: How does a diverging diamond interchange make highway ramp turns safer?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: A diverging diamond interchange removes the troublesome left-turn movements of a standard interchange, which leaves fewer conflict points with other vehicles.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: Whom must you yield to when changing lanes or passing, and what brake test tells you the gap is too tight?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: When changing lanes or passing, yield to vehicles already in the lane you want, and do not move over if another driver would have to slow for you.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: Who holds priority when you merge onto a roadway, and when must you hold off merging?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: When merging, yield to every vehicle on the road you are joining, and do not merge if it would force someone to slow down.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: Which vehicles hold priority over you whenever your car is moving in reverse?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: When backing up, yield to all vehicles near enough to be a hazard.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: When two vehicles meet on a steep Colorado road too narrow to pass, which driver normally backs or yields, and when does that flip?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: On a steep road too narrow for two vehicles, the downhill driver yields by backing to a wider spot or stopping to leave room, unless it is more practical for the uphill driver to return to a turnout.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: Between an uphill car and a downhill car on a single-lane mountain grade, who normally gives way?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: On a narrow mountain road the downhill vehicle is the one that normally yields, not the uphill one, unless the uphill vehicle can more practically reach a turnout.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: What warning sounds or four strobe colors require pulling right and stopping for an approaching emergency vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: Yield to any emergency vehicle using a siren, air horn or flashing red, blue, white or yellow lights by pulling to the right edge and stopping where possible.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: If sirens and flashing lights close in while your car is already inside an intersection, what must you do?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are inside an intersection, continue through the intersection first and then pull over.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: What is your first choice—and your backup move—when passing a stopped emergency vehicle along the shoulder?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: Passing an emergency vehicle stopped beside the road, try to leave at least one empty lane between you, or slow to a safe speed and use care if you cannot change lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: How does your legal duty change between an emergency vehicle closing from behind versus one parked on the shoulder?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: For an approaching emergency vehicle you pull right and stop, but for one already stopped at the roadside you leave a lane open or slow down as you pass.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: When traffic blocks you from vacating the lane beside a stopped responder, what exact speed drops apply at forty-five and below versus above forty-five?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: Unless emergency personnel direct otherwise or conditions prevent a lane change, slow to twenty-five miles per hour when the posted limit is forty-five miles per hour or less, or to twenty miles per hour below the limit when it is above forty-five miles per hour

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: How does the forty-five-mile-per-hour posted limit split Colorado's move-over slowdown numbers?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: Move-over speed depends on the posted limit: at forty-five miles per hour or below slow to twenty-five miles per hour, and above forty-five miles per hour slow to twenty miles per hour under the limit.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: What two flashing light colors mark working service and maintenance trucks, and how must you treat them?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: Yield to service and maintenance vehicles that are working and showing flashing yellow and blue lights, and take extra care when approaching or passing them.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: How does the light bar on a maintenance truck differ from the lights and sound on an emergency vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: Maintenance vehicles use flashing yellow and blue lights, while emergency vehicles may use red, blue, white or yellow lights with a siren or air horn.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: Why are working snowplows tough to see, and what passing move around diagonal plow formations is illegal?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: Snow plows can be hidden by the blowing snow they throw up, and passing working plows that are staggered diagonally in formation is illegal.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.front: What two adjustments protect road crews and fellow drivers inside a construction zone?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.expected_back: In a work or construction zone, protect crews and other road users by shifting your lane position away from workers and slowing down for obstacles.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.front: At least how many feet away must you halt for a school bus flashing red lights, and when may you move?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.expected_back: Stop at least twenty feet away from a school bus that has stopped with red lights flashing, and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.front: Which approaching directions must stop for a flashing red school bus, and what sole roadway feature excuses opposite lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.expected_back: The school bus stop rule applies on your side of the road, the opposite side or at an intersection ahead, unless a median or other physical barrier separates you from the bus.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: When a school bus flashes red across a multi-lane road, what is the sole separator that lets oncoming cars keep moving?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: The school bus stop applies in both directions; only a median or other physical barrier between you and the bus excuses you from stopping.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.front: Once a school bus switches off its flashing red lights, what check comes before touching the gas?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.expected_back: After a school bus turns off its lights, look carefully for children near the bus and crossing the road before you move.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.front: When does Colorado law require yielding to a public transit bus pulling back out from the curb?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.expected_back: Yield to a transit bus that is signaling to pull into a traffic lane when the yield sign on its rear is lit.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: How should you pace your vehicle and focus your attention inside a construction zone?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: In work zones, move with the flow of traffic carefully and stay ready for sudden, unexpected events.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: What happens to posted speed limits and speeding ticket amounts inside Colorado work zones?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Speed limits may be lowered in work or construction zones and will be clearly posted; speeding there can bring double fines.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: What single factor drives crash severity more than any other on Colorado highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: Speed is the biggest factor in how severe a crash is, and many deadly Colorado highway crashes involve drivers going too fast.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: What weather do posted speed caps assume, and when does driving below a posted freeway minimum draw a ticket?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Posted speed limits are the most you may drive in ideal conditions; some roads like freeways also post a minimum, and going below it is a violation unless road or weather conditions require it.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: Under what condition is driving slower than a posted minimum speed limit illegal versus legal?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: Driving too slowly can also be wrong: going below a posted minimum is a violation unless conditions require it.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: Around what six hazards must you drop speed, and why is creeping way below normal flow dangerous?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Slow down in poor weather and near railroad tracks, pedestrians, bicyclists, animals and school buses, but crawling far below the limit in normal conditions disrupts traffic flow and can be unsafe.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: Even inside a marked reduced-speed zone, can safe driving require going slower than the sign?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: Signs mark reduced speed zones, and you may need to go slower than any posted limit to keep everyone safe.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: When no speed post appears, what is Colorado's default limit on blind curves and narrow, winding mountain highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: Unless signs say otherwise, blind curves and winding, narrow mountain highways carry a twenty miles per hour Colorado limit.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: With no sign posted, what default Colorado limits govern open mountain highways and commercial trash-hauling trucks?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: Unless signs say otherwise, the Colorado limit is forty miles per hour on open mountain highways and forty-five miles per hour for vehicles in the trash-hauling business.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: How do Colorado's two unposted mountain highway speed limits split between tight switchbacks and open stretches?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: Mountain roads carry two different defaults: twenty miles per hour on narrow, winding mountain highways and blind curves, but forty miles per hour on open mountain highways.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: When unposted, what default speed limits apply in Colorado business districts versus residential neighborhoods?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Unless signs say otherwise, the Colorado limit is twenty-five miles per hour in a business district and thirty miles per hour in a residence district.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: Many states set residential streets slower, so how do Colorado's twenty-five and thirty default limits pair up?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: The two lowest default limits are easy to mix up: twenty-five miles per hour belongs to business districts and thirty miles per hour to residence districts.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: What default limits apply on Colorado urban highways versus designated rural interstates, and who can lower local limits?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: Unless signs say otherwise, the Colorado limit is fifty-five miles per hour on urban interstates and highways and sixty-five to seventy-five miles per hour on designated rural interstates and highways; cities and towns may set lower limits by ordinance.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: How is total stopping distance defined, and which four factors add together to determine it?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Stopping distance is how far you travel from the moment you realize you must stop until the vehicle stops, and it depends on speed, recognition time, reaction time and braking time.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: How does keeping generous space behind traffic ahead make slowing or stopping safer?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: Leaving space behind other vehicles lets you see stops coming, so slowing or changing lanes may avoid a stop or make it gradual and safer.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: What two driver mistakes cause most sudden stops, and what three bad outcomes follow hard panic braking?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: Sudden stops usually come from inattention or following too closely, and braking too hard can cause a skid, loss of control or a rear-end crash from the driver behind.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: Under ideal conditions, roughly how many feet does a light passenger car need to stop from fifty-five miles per hour?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: The National Safety Council says a light passenger car at fifty-five miles per hour can stop in roughly two hundred feet under ideal conditions, while other vehicles need different distances.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: What four steps from early blinker to exit throttle make up a textbook proper turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: A proper turn means signaling early enough, scanning for hazards and crossing road users, turning from and into the correct lane on the correct path, then accelerating up to the limit or traffic flow.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: Is skipping your turn signal an actual traffic violation, and before which four maneuvers must it flash?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: Not signaling is a traffic violation; signal before every turn, lane change, turn into a parking lot or pull-out from a parked spot so others know your intentions.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: How many continuous feet must your blinker run in urban zones versus four-lane highways posted above forty?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: Before turning or changing lanes, keep signaling without a break for one hundred feet in urban areas, or for two hundred feet on four-lane highways posted above forty miles per hour

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: Since judging exact footage on asphalt is tough, what everyday seconds rule guides pre-move signaling?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: A common rule of thumb is to signal for at least three seconds before turning or changing lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: How do Colorado's urban footage, fast four-lane footage, and time rule of thumb fit together for signaling?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: Signal distance depends on the road: one hundred feet in urban areas, two hundred feet on four-lane highways posted above forty miles per hour, with three seconds as a general rule of thumb.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: What must you use if your electric blinkers burn out, and what do you do right before turning the wheel?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: If your turn signals fail you must use hand signals, ending the signal before the turn so both hands are on the wheel.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: Where inside your lane do you set up for a right turn versus a left turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: For a right turn, start from the rightmost lane and turn from the right part of your lane as close to the curb as possible; for a left turn, keep to the left side of your lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: How can you tell when turning from more than one parallel lane is legal at a busy junction?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: Where turns from more than one lane are allowed, signs, signals or lane markings will show the correct turn lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: In which lane of the cross street should your car finish a standard turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: End each turn centered in the proper lane of the road you enter, which is usually the closest lane on your side.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: What painted guides steer multi-lane turns, and what four steering mistakes must you avoid?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: In intersections with several turn lanes, follow the white lines to find your path, and avoid cutting corners, swinging wide, turning late or straddling lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: In Colorado, where exact spot should you hold while waiting for a safe oncoming gap to turn left?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: Left turns are a frequent crash point; wait at the stop line or crosswalk until oncoming traffic leaves a gap big enough to finish the turn safely.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: What three hazards arise if you creep out into the middle of the intersection while waiting to turn left?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: Creeping into the intersection while waiting to turn left blocks emergency vehicles, cuts visibility for oncoming drivers and exposes you to red-light runners if the signal changes.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: Why must your front tires stay pointed straight ahead while waiting to turn left?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: Keep your front wheels pointed straight while waiting to turn left, because if you are hit from behind, turned wheels would push you into oncoming traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: What two habits combine for the safest possible left-turn wait in Colorado?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: While waiting to turn left, stay behind the stop line or crosswalk and keep the wheels straight, rather than edging into the intersection with wheels turned.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: Where are U-turns illegal, and what safer alternative should you pick instead?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: A U-turn reverses your direction on the same road; it is banned where No U-turn signs are posted and anywhere it would endanger others, so go on to the next street or turnaround instead.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: What off-street spaces let you perform a two-point turnabout when circling the block will not work?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: A two-point turnabout uses a street, alley or driveway to reverse direction when driving around the block is not practical or possible.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: Why is backing into a right-side driveway first—then signaling left forward—the preferred reverse two-point sequence?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: In a reverse two-point turnabout, signal right, check traffic, back until the rear bumper reaches the driveway edge, steer quickly full right while backing slowly, straighten once centered, then signal and turn left into the proper lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.front: How do you execute a forward two-point turnabout using a left-side driveway and backing right?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.expected_back: In a forward two-point turnabout, signal left, pull in near the right side of the driveway or alley, stop once the rear clears the curb, signal right, reverse slowly with the wheel turned full right, straighten in the nearest lane, then drive forward.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.front: Under what strict road and routing conditions is a three-point turnabout justified?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.expected_back: A three-point turnabout is only for a two-lane road too narrow for a U-turn when there is no way around the block and no two-point option.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.front: How do you stop, signal early, check blind spots, and cut across to begin a three-point turnabout?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.expected_back: For a three-point turnabout, pull over and stop on the right, then signal left at least two hundred feet or three seconds ahead, check traffic and blind spots, and turn hard left to stop at the far side.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.front: How do you reverse across, pull forward into your new lane, and check your stalk to finish a three-point turnabout?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.expected_back: To finish a three-point turnabout, check both sides, reverse with the wheel turned sharply right across the road and stop, then in drive signal left, turn sharply left into the right lane of the new direction and check the signal has canceled.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: What goal unites U-turns, two-point turnabouts, and three-point turnabouts, and which one sits last in priority?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: A U-turn, a two-point turnabout and a three-point turnabout all reverse direction; the three-point version is only for narrow two-lane roads with no other option.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.front: What gear, brake, and key habits secure automatic and manual vehicles when parked on uphill or downhill slopes?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.expected_back: When parking, leave an automatic in park; leave a manual in low gear facing uphill and in reverse facing downhill, set the emergency brake and take the key.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: How does securing a manual transmission uphill versus downhill differ from parking an automatic?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: A manual transmission is left in low gear facing uphill but in reverse facing downhill, while an automatic simply stays in park.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.front: Including runaway truck ramps, bridges, tunnels, tracks, and bike lanes, where is parking flatly prohibited?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.expected_back: Never park on a crosswalk, sidewalk, bridge, elevated structure, railroad tracks, controlled access highway, in an intersection, tunnel, runaway truck ramp, on or off ramp, in a bike lane, or across a driveway.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.front: How many feet of clear curb must you leave near a stop post, signal, or rail crossing versus a fire hydrant?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.expected_back: Parking is banned closer than thirty feet to a stop sign, traffic signal or railroad crossing, and closer than fifteen feet to a fire hydrant.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: How do Colorado's thirty-foot and fifteen-foot no-parking buffers divide up roadside fixtures?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: No-parking distances differ by object: thirty feet from signals, stop signs and railroad crossings, but fifteen feet from a fire hydrant.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.front: What three steering cuts move you from beside the front car into the middle of a parallel parking space?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.expected_back: To parallel park, stop beside the car ahead, back slowly with the wheel sharp right, turn sharp left once clear of that car, then turn right to pull toward the curb in the middle of the space.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.front: What three-step safety check is required before pulling out of a parallel parking spot into live traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.expected_back: To leave a parallel space, signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and pull out only when it is safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: Within how many inches of the curb—or where on curbless shoulders—must you parallel park?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Where parallel parking is allowed, park within twelve inches of the curb, or as near as possible to the outer edge of the shoulder, so traffic is not blocked or slowed.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: Which way do your front wheels point when parked downhill beside a curb, and how do you set the tire?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Parked facing downhill beside a curb, turn the front wheels toward the curb and let the car roll gently until the front tire rests against it.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: Which way do your front wheels point when parked uphill beside a curb, and how does the tire catch?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: Parked facing uphill beside a curb, point the front wheels away from it and ease backward until the rear of the front tire is blocked by the curb.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: With no curb present, which way must your front wheels turn whether facing uphill or downhill, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: With no curb, turn the front wheels to the right whether facing uphill or downhill, so a rolling car would leave the highway instead of entering traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: How do the three hill-parking wheel directions line up across downhill curb, uphill curb, and no curb?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: With a curb, downhill means wheels toward the curb and uphill means wheels away from it; without a curb, the wheels go right either way.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: What makes freeways inherently hazardous, and what mental habit must stay active there?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: Freeways are dangerous because of the high speeds involved, so stay aware of everything around you at all times.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: What two traffic advantages are controlled-access freeways engineered to deliver over surface streets?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: Freeways are built to carry more traffic at higher speeds than ordinary streets or highways.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: What is your main throttle job along a freeway acceleration ramp?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: On an acceleration ramp, build up speed to match freeway traffic before you merge.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: What four-step routine blends you cleanly from a side entrance ramp onto the freeway?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: To enter from a side entrance ramp, signal, look for a gap, speed up to the traffic speed and merge only when it is safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: What painted ramp line must end before you merge, why avoid stopping, and who holds priority?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: Do not merge until the solid white line ends, avoid stopping in the acceleration lane unless truly necessary, and remember that freeway traffic has the right-of-way.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: How do you handle an entrance ramp controlled by an active ramp-metering signal?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: On a metered entrance ramp, stop at the signal and enter the freeway only when released by a green light.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: Why is stopping on a normal acceleration lane a last resort, yet mandatory on a metered ramp?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: When entering a freeway you match its speed and yield to it; stopping in the acceleration lane is a last resort, except on a metered ramp where you stop for the signal.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: Which freeway lane belongs to you whenever you are traveling slower than surrounding traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: Use the rightmost lane when you are going slower than normal traffic speed.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: For what three specific uses is the leftmost freeway lane reserved?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: The leftmost passing lane is for passing, left turns, and times when heavy traffic leaves no room to merge into the other lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: How do the rightmost and leftmost freeway lanes split duties by speed and maneuver?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: The rightmost freeway lane is for slower drivers, while the leftmost lane is reserved for passing, left turns and heavy-traffic situations.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: When cruising in the right freeway lane toward an upcoming on-ramp, what courteous move helps incoming drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: Approaching a merge area, move over when it is safe to give entering vehicles room.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: What directions, hidden zones, and overhead aids should guide your awareness while cruising a freeway?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: On the freeway, watch traffic ahead, beside and behind you, stay aware of vehicles in your blind spots, and plan ahead with directional and guide signs.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: What blinker distance, weaving restraint, and median rule govern freeway lane changes?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: On the freeway, signal at least two hundred feet before a lane change, avoid changing lanes often, and never drive across, over or inside a median or island.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: How early do you signal for an exit lane, and at what exact point do you start braking?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: To exit, use the deceleration lane: signal two hundred feet before it begins, hold your speed until you are in it, then slow to the advised exit ramp speed.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: Why must your braking wait until you have entered the deceleration lane rather than starting on the mainline?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: On the exit you keep your speed until inside the deceleration lane and slow down there, not on the freeway itself.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: What three mistakes must you avoid when leaving a freeway onto an exit ramp?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: When leaving a freeway, keep pace with traffic until the exit, do not exit at the last second, and do not exceed the posted ramp limit.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: Which four everyday maneuvers count legally as a lane change and demand full three-way checks?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: A lane change includes moving between lanes, passing, merging from an entrance ramp and pulling onto the road from a curb or shoulder, and each requires checking ahead, beside and behind.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: Where exact spot around your car sits a blind spot, and why do mirrors miss it?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: A blind spot is an area slightly to the side and rear of your vehicle that neither the rearview nor side mirrors show.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: Why is glancing at inside and outside mirrors never sufficient by itself before moving laterally?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: Mirrors are not enough for a lane change, because the blind spot just behind and beside you needs an over-the-shoulder look.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: What five-step sequence takes you safely from signaling to sliding into an adjacent lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: To change lanes, signal for at least three seconds or two hundred feet, check ahead, check the mirrors, look over your shoulder at the blind spot, then move over when safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: Once centered in your new lane, what mirror check and exact blinker cutoff finish the move?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: Once centered in the new lane, glance at the mirror for traffic behind you, and switch the signal off no more than three seconds after the change is complete.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: How do the pre-move blinker minimum and post-move blinker shutoff frame every lane change?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: The lane-change signal runs at least three seconds or two hundred feet before you move, and goes off within three seconds after you finish.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: What roadway cues govern passing zones, and on which side does normal overtaking happen?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: Signs and markings show where passing is and is not allowed, and passing is normally done on the left.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: On which two multi-lane road layouts is passing on the right legal, and what shoulder move is banned?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: Passing on the right is allowed only on one-way streets and on roads with two or more lanes each way, and passing by driving off the pavement or on the shoulder is never allowed.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: How does Colorado separate legal right-side overtaking from illegal shoulder bypassing?
