sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: Passing on the right is allowed on one-way streets and roads with two or more lanes each way, but passing on the shoulder or off the pavement never is.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: Before overtaking any road user—including a cyclist—what must you evaluate ahead, beside, and behind?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: Before passing anyone, bicyclists included, judge from traffic ahead, beside and behind whether you have enough time and room to do it safely.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: How many vehicles should you commit to overtaking in a single passing move?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: Pass only one vehicle at a time rather than counting on passing several at once.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: While completing a pass, what exact image in your inside rearview mirror signals safe clearance to return right?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: To pass, change lanes properly, speed up past the vehicle, and return to your lane once both of its headlights appear in your rearview mirror.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: At least how far from any oncoming vehicle—or oncoming cyclist—must you be tucked back into your right lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: Never start a pass unless you can be back on the right side while still more than two hundred feet from any oncoming vehicle, counting a bicyclist on the oncoming lane or shoulder.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: How does a solid yellow stripe starting ahead restrict starting a two-lane pass?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: Do not pass if you cannot get back to the right side before a solid yellow line begins.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: What rear-mirror sight and forward-paint boundary together mark a textbook completed pass?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: Return to your lane after passing when you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in the rearview mirror, and finish before a solid yellow line begins.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: What minimum side clearance must separate a cyclist from the widest sticking-out part of your rig?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: When passing a bicyclist, keep at least three feet between the rider and the outermost part of your vehicle, including mirrors or a trailer.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: When does Colorado law allow briefly crossing a solid yellow center line to give a cyclist room?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: To pass a bicyclist you may briefly cross a solid yellow line when no traffic is oncoming and your view ahead is clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: Under what three road, vehicle, or weather conditions should you widen your buffer beyond three feet around cyclists?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: Give bicyclists extra room on rural roads, in a large vehicle or in wind, because a wind blast can knock a rider over.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: Where do blind hills, curves, crossings, and structures make passing illegal in Colorado?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Do not pass on a hill or curve that blocks your view, within one hundred feet of an intersection or railroad crossing, or within one hundred feet of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel when your view is blocked.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: Within what distance of an intersection or railroad crossing—and on which sight-limited features—is passing illegal?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Passing is illegal closer than one hundred feet to an intersection or a railroad crossing, and on a bridge, curve or hill that limits what you can see.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: What single distance links Colorado's no-passing rule at intersections and rail crossings with sight-blocked bridges, viaducts, and tunnels?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: The no-passing distance near intersections and railroad crossings is one hundred feet, the same figure used for bridges, viaducts and tunnels with a blocked view.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: What side clearance—including mirrors—must you keep when passing a bicyclist, and when may you touch a solid yellow line?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Do not pass a bicyclist unless you can keep a buffer of at least three feet, counting mirrors and other projections; a brief crossing of a solid yellow line to do so is allowed when no one is oncoming and the view ahead is clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: Even on an open road, which two passing actions break Colorado law every time?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: It is illegal to pass in a marked no-passing zone or to go over the posted speed limit while passing.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: May you ever pass a school bus displaying flashing red lights and an extended stop arm?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: It is illegal to pass a school bus whose red lights are flashing and whose stop arm is out.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: Why must you stay ready to stop at sight-blocking hills and curves even on routes you drive daily?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: Hills and curves can hide hazards even on roads you know, so be ready to stop when one blocks your view of the road.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: How should you manage your speed when approaching a hilltop you cannot see beyond?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: If you cannot see past the top of a hill, slow to a suitable speed until you crest it and can see the road again.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: Why must you reduce speed before entering a curve, and at what point may you begin accelerating?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: Slow down before you enter a curve, because taking it too fast lets the tires lose grip and skid; start speeding up only after the middle of the curve.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: Contrast your pedal timing at curve entry versus past the midpoint of the curve?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: In a curve you slow down before entry and accelerate only after the middle, never while entering.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: Which three visibility and lighting factors can make dawn and dusk riskier than midday driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: Dawn and dusk can be riskier than daytime because of poor visibility, the small area your headlights light up and glare from headlights combined with fog lights.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: When does Colorado law mandate headlights, and what daytime lighting habit lowers crash risk?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Colorado law requires headlights from sunset to sunrise and whenever you cannot see one thousand feet ahead; keeping low beams or daytime running lights on all the time lowers risk.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: When must a roadside-parked vehicle display parking lights, and what driving use is forbidden?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: A vehicle parked beside the road, attended or not, must show parking lights from sunset to sunrise or when visibility is under one thousand feet, but never drive on parking lights alone.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: Contrast the legal purpose of parking lights at night against rolling down the street with only parking lights lit?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Parking lights are required on a vehicle parked at the roadside at night, but driving with only parking lights on is not allowed.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: Under which two conditions—lighting and route familiarity—should you stretch out your following distance?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: Leave more following distance at night and on roads you do not know.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: What unlit users, dark-zone movers, and single-lamp clues should you scan for after dark?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: At night watch for vehicles and bicyclists without lights, slow down in dark areas where people or animals may be moving, and look for the single headlight of a bicycle or motorcycle.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: On which types of roadways should you use your high-beam headlights?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: Use high beams in rural areas and on open highways away from cities.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: Before reaching what distance from an approaching vehicle must you dim high beams or low-plus-fog lights?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: Dim high beams, or low beams used with fog lights, before you come within five hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle so its driver is not blinded.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: Within what distance behind another vehicle must you switch to low beams and shut off fog lights?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: When you are within two hundred feet behind another vehicle, you must use low beams with fog lights turned off.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: Match Colorado's three key headlight distances—one thousand, five hundred, and two hundred feet—to each situation?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: Headlight distances differ by purpose: lights on when visibility is under one thousand feet, dim for oncoming traffic within five hundred feet, low beams when following within two hundred feet.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: Where should you aim your eyes to stay centered when oncoming headlights glare toward you?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: Do not stare into oncoming headlights; lower your eyes below the glare and steer by the painted edge line until the vehicle passes, then look up again.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: Which lights work best in nighttime fog, and why do high beams make visibility worse?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: In fog at night use low beams or fog lights, because high beams reflect back at you as if shining on a mirror.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: Contrast the driving setting where high beams shine against the weather condition where they backfire?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: High beams help on dark open highways but backfire in fog, where low beams or fog lights work better.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: Regardless of drivetrain, which two driving adjustments are essential in rain, fog, ice, high wind, or blowing dust?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: Bad weather affects every vehicle, whether front, rear, four-wheel or all-wheel drive, and the two key responses to rain, fog, ice, high wind or dust are slowing down and leaving more following distance.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: Does driving a four-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive SUV let you skip slowing down and widening gaps in storms?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: Four-wheel or all-wheel drive does not exempt you from slowing down and adding following distance in bad weather.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: How should you set your headlights in poor storm visibility and your cruise control on wet or icy pavement?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: In bad weather turn on headlights when visibility is poor, and never use cruise control on a wet or icy highway.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: How should you respond to large pools of standing water or a flooded roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: Do not drive through large pools of standing water; if the road is flooded, take another route.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: How does the Colorado handbook rate the hazard level of snow, packed snow, and ice on roadways?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: Roads covered with snow, packed snow or ice are extremely hazardous.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: What happens beneath your tires during hydroplaning, and what tire condition raises the danger?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on a film of water on the pavement, which can wipe out traction and steering; worn tires raise the risk, so check tread depth regularly.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: Which pedal and steering inputs bring your vehicle back under control if hydroplaning begins?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: If you start to hydroplane, lift your foot off the gas and steer slowly in the direction the car is sliding until control returns, which helps line the tires up with the vehicle.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: Which abrupt steering or pedal reactions must you avoid while hydroplaning, and why?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: During a hydroplane, never jerk the wheel, since overcorrecting can flip the car, and do not brake or turn until the tires grip again.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: During a hydroplane, contrast the right steering direction and foot move against the wrong instincts?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: In a hydroplane you steer gently toward the direction of the slide, not away from it, and you ease off the gas instead of braking.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: At what stage are snow and ice slickest, and how do slippery surfaces change tire grip and stopping?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Snow and ice are at their most dangerous as they begin to melt, and slippery roads reduce tire grip and lengthen stopping distance.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: Which four roadway locations can stay icy even when surrounding lanes look dry and clear?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: Overpasses, bridges, shaded spots and snow-packed stretches can be icy even when the rest of the pavement is clear.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: Why shouldn't clear, dry-looking winter pavement trick you into letting your guard down?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: Bridges, overpasses and shaded spots can stay icy when the surrounding pavement is not, so a clear road can still hold icy patches.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: What winter benefit does four-wheel drive deliver, and how does its stopping distance compare with a regular car's?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: Four-wheel drive improves traction but does not let a vehicle stop any sooner than an ordinary car.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: Separate what four-wheel drive adds on winter roads from the physics it cannot improve?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: Four-wheel drive adds traction but not stopping power; it cannot stop any sooner than an ordinary car.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: Which winter tire setups help or may be mandated on Colorado highways, and can they still slip?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: Keep good tire tread; in winter, chains, snow tires or other traction devices are better and may be required on highways, though even these can slip on slick pavement.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: How must your vehicle's braking system be maintained and adjusted ahead of slick driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: Keep brakes in good repair and adjusted so every wheel brakes evenly.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: When traction breaks into a skid, what is the baseline pedal and steering response?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: When traction is lost or a skid begins, lift off the gas and the brake together, then steer the front wheels toward your intended path.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: In a vehicle equipped with anti-lock brakes, how do you respond if a skid starts?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: With anti-lock brakes, if you begin to skid, ease off the gas, press the brake and steer the front wheels the way you want to go.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: Which braking technique applies on slippery roads or skids when your car lacks anti-lock brakes?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: Without anti-lock brakes, use threshold braking when skidding or on slippery roads, pressing the brake to just short of locking the wheels.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: Between threshold braking and anti-lock braking technique, which works in every car and which requires ABS?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: Threshold braking works on cars with or without anti-lock brakes, but anti-lock braking technique cannot be used on a car without ABS.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: Contrast your brake-pedal action during a skid in an ABS-equipped car versus a car without ABS?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: The two skid instructions differ by brakes: with anti-lock brakes you ease off the gas and push on the brake while steering, without them you use threshold braking just short of lockup.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: How does the handbook's general skid rule differ on the pedals from its anti-lock skid rule, and what stays identical?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: A generic skid starts with both feet off the pedals, while an anti-lock skid adds pushing on the brake; in both, steer where you want to go.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: Before even a quick winter errand, how must you prep your glass and clear sudden cabin fogging?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: Keep defrosters and wipers working, scrape off all ice, snow and frost even for a short trip, and clear inside fogging quickly by opening a window.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: Which two warning-light colors identify snowplows and sanding trucks, and how should you approach them?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: Snow plows and sanding trucks flash yellow and blue warning lights, so be extremely careful as you come up behind or go around them.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: When does Colorado law make passing a snowplow strictly illegal?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: Use extra care near snowplows clearing snow with flashing yellow lights; passing a government-operated plow working in tandem with other plows while its yellow lights flash is illegal.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: How should you adjust speed, following gap, and side clearance around pedestrians and cyclists in snow and ice?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: In snow and ice keep an extra large gap behind the vehicle ahead, slow down, and give pedestrians and bicyclists extra room to get around snow and ice.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: What hazards come with Colorado mountain driving, and how should you control speed down steep grades?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: Mountain driving brings steep grades, changing weather, bicyclists, wildlife and rocks on the road; shift to a lower gear to control speed going down steep grades.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: Where on mountain two-lane roads is crossing into the oncoming lane to pass illegal?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: Using the oncoming lane to pass is illegal near the crest of a hill, on a curve or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is blocked.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: Beyond steep grades and fast weather shifts, what hidden road junctions and roadside movers appear in the mountains?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: In the mountains expect intersections hidden by trees, brush or crops, and animals on or beside the road.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: What should you do if your vehicle loses pace climbing a steep grade, and who holds mountain right-of-way?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: If your vehicle struggles up a steep road, pull off at the first safe spot or keep right so others can pass; uphill vehicles have the right-of-way over downhill ones.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: Pair who gets right-of-way on a narrow mountain grade with the courtesy duty of a slow climbing vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: On a mountain grade the uphill driver has the right-of-way, and a slow uphill vehicle should keep right or pull off to let others by.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: Which roadway category carries the highest fatality rate per mile driven across the United States?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: Rural highways are the most dangerous roads, with the highest U.S. death rate per mile driven of any road type.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: Which design features—from curves and hills to lane width and edges—make rural roads extra risky?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: Rural roads may have sharp or blind curves, steep hills and dips, poor or hidden guide signs, narrow lanes that make passing hard, and no shoulders or guard rails.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: What hidden entrances, unmarked tracks, debris, and slow traffic must you anticipate on rural roads?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: On rural roads expect blind driveways, T-intersections and side streets hidden by plants, plus rocks, debris, animals, crossing farm vehicles, unmarked railroad crossings and slow or small vehicles like bicycles.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.front: How do unpaved dirt or gravel rural surfaces—and washboard ripples—affect vehicle control?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.expected_back: Rural pavement is often rough or unpaved dirt and gravel with less traction, and washboarding on gravel roads can upset steering and control.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.front: How can striking potholes upset your vehicle's grip on the road?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.expected_back: Potholes can make the vehicle bounce or jolt and cause the tires to lose traction.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.front: Why do many bicyclist fatalities happen on rural roads, and how should you adjust speed and buffer when passing?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.expected_back: Many bicyclist deaths happen on rural roads because of higher speeds, so slow down and give more than the required three feet when passing riders there, since dangerous wind blasts can lead to riders being struck.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.front: Why can yesterday's path through a construction zone look different today, and what guides you ahead?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.expected_back: Work zones contain equipment and workers and may change routes daily, and signs, cones and other devices placed ahead warn of the changes.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.front: Which three core driving habits keep you out of trouble inside any construction zone?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.expected_back: In a work zone stay alert, be ready to stop suddenly and never tailgate.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.front: What traffic controls appear on major construction projects, and why are speed limits reduced there?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.expected_back: Large projects may use flaggers, portable concrete barriers, complex signs and reduced speed limits, and those lower limits give drivers more time to read and react.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.front: Why must construction workers stay constantly on guard beside active travel lanes?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.expected_back: Work-zone crews cannot be fully separated from traffic and must watch constantly for drivers who drift into the work area.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.front: How do police presence and ticket fines change in Colorado work zones, and which other zone matches?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.expected_back: Police enforcement is often added in work zones, and fines are doubled there as they are in school zones.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.front: Which crash type dominates construction zones, what causes it, and whom must you obey?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.expected_back: In a work zone, obey work-zone speed signs and flaggers, and watch the vehicle ahead, because most work-zone crashes are rear-end collisions caused by inattention.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: Pair the two special zones that double traffic fines with the number-one collision inside work zones?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: Work-zone and school-zone fines are both doubled, and most work-zone crashes are rear-end collisions.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.front: Why is calm, defensive driving necessary even when you follow every traffic rule yourself?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.expected_back: You cannot count on others obeying every rule, so drive calmly, ignore aggressive drivers and practice defensive driving.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.front: Who inside your vehicle needs to wear a fastened seat belt?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.expected_back: Make sure every person in the vehicle wears a seat belt.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.front: Which three exceptions allow using a mobile device while driving under Colorado law?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.expected_back: Colorado law bars using a mobile device while driving except to contact police or fire services, in an emergency, or with a hands-free accessory.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.front: When is texting while driving permitted in Colorado, and does a hands-free accessory excuse texting?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.expected_back: Colorado law bars texting while driving except to contact police or fire services or in an emergency; the listed texting exceptions do not include a hands-free accessory.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: How do Colorado's exceptions for general mobile-device use differ from its exceptions for texting?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: Hand-held phone use has a hands-free exception, but texting does not; both allow contacting police or fire and emergencies.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.front: Which clock positions and turning techniques belong on the steering wheel, and which two habits are unsafe?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.expected_back: Keep both hands on the wheel at eight and four or nine and three o'clock, turn with the hand-over-hand or push-pull-slide method, and never palm the wheel or let it slide through your fingers after a turn.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.front: Which directions should you scan continuously, and what head-check pattern applies at intersections?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.expected_back: Scan ahead, to the sides and behind, and always look left, right and left again when turning at, crossing or entering an intersection, watching for pedestrians, bicyclists and motorcyclists.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.front: How many seconds ahead should you aim your gaze, and what distance is that in town versus open highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.expected_back: Look at least ten seconds down the road, about one block in the city or half a mile on the open road, to avoid last-second braking or swerving.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.front: How frequently should you glance at your rearview mirror, and which maneuvers call for extra checks?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.expected_back: Check your rearview mirror every five to eight seconds, more often in heavy traffic, and especially when changing lanes, slowing, backing, leaving an intersection or going down a long or steep hill.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.front: How do you measure safe normal-weather following distance using a roadside fixed point?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.expected_back: Under normal conditions use the three-second rule: when the car ahead passes a fixed point, count three seconds, and if you reach the point first you are following too closely.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: Match ten seconds, five to eight seconds, and three seconds to forward gaze, mirrors, and following space?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: Three different times guide your eyes and spacing: look ten seconds ahead, check the mirror every five to eight seconds, and leave three seconds behind the car ahead.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: Which four driving environment factors can dramatically lengthen the distance you need to stop?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: Weather, road conditions, traffic volume and time of day can greatly increase the stopping distance you need.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: Why should you stay within posted limits while matching surrounding flow instead of driving much faster or slower?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: Keep to posted limits and the pace of traffic; much faster means constant passing, and much slower causes back-ups and unpredictability.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: Where two lanes narrow into one, how does a proper Colorado zipper merge work?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: At a zipper merge where two lanes become one, use both lanes equally until just before the closure, then take turns into the open lane; drivers who wait until the lane ends are doing it right.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: In a zipper merge, is riding the closing lane all the way to the taper rude cutting-in?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: In a zipper merge, using the closing lane up to the merge point is correct, not cutting in.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: Which eight busy locations or choke points count as slow zones needing lower speed and heightened focus?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: Slow zones calling for lower speed and extra attention include shopping centers, schools, parks and playgrounds, residential streets, rush hour, narrow bridges, toll plazas and rail crossings.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: What legal threshold allows law enforcement officers to initiate a traffic stop?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: Officers make traffic stops on reasonable suspicion of a traffic or criminal violation.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: How should you respond when police lights or a siren activate right behind your car?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: When you see emergency lights or hear a siren behind you, stay calm, signal and pull off or to the right as soon as it is safe; the officer may ask you to move farther from traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: Once parked for a traffic stop, which five cabin actions set up a safe roadside interaction?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: Once stopped, shut off the engine and audio, stay inside unless told otherwise, use interior lights at night, keep hands visible and follow instructions.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: Which window do you lower at a stop, and how do you handle weapons or reaching for paperwork?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: The officer may come to either side; lower that window, mention any weapon in the vehicle at first contact without reaching for it, and wait for instructions before reaching for documents.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: What happens with identification when an officer making a stop is not wearing a uniform?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: An officer not in uniform will normally show credentials, and you may ask to see them if they do not.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: Which three documents do officers typically request, and how should you retrieve them if stored out of reach?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: The officer will usually explain the stop and ask for your license, proof of insurance and registration; if those are out of reach, say where they are and wait for an okay before getting them.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: How should you behave if asked out of the vehicle, and what three stop outcomes can occur?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: If asked to step out, keep your hands visible and stand where directed; the officer may give a warning, a ticket that may carry a fine, or make an arrest, and you may ask what action is being taken.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: Where do ticket disputes belong instead of the shoulder, and how do you address improper officer conduct?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: Do not argue at the roadside; contest a decision in court instead, and ask for a supervisor soon after the stop if you think the officer acted improperly.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: What does your signature on a traffic ticket mean legally, and what happens if you refuse to sign?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: Signing a traffic ticket does not admit guilt, but refusing to sign it can lead to arrest.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: Separate signing a citation, refusing to sign it, and disputing the charge?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: Signing a ticket is not admitting guilt, but refusing to sign can get you arrested; disagreements go to court, not the roadside.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: What shared rights, legal duties, and handling differences define sharing the road in Colorado?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: Sharing the road means everyone has the right to use it and the duty to obey traffic laws and watch out for one another, keeping in mind that bicycles, motorcycles, buses and trucks handle differently.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: Under what traffic-state, space, and speed conditions may a two-wheeled motorcycle lane-filter in Colorado?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: Lane filtering lets a two-wheeled motorcycle pass stopped vehicles in its lane when traffic in neighboring lanes is also stopped, there is room, and it goes no faster than fifteen miles per hour.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: Which motorcycle type, surrounding traffic state, and top speed cap limit legal Colorado lane filtering?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: Lane filtering is limited to two-wheeled motorcycles passing stopped traffic at no more than fifteen miles per hour, not moving traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.front: Which driver maneuver causes most motorist-at-fault bicycle and motorcycle wrecks, and how do you prevent it?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.expected_back: Most motorist-caused crashes with bicycles or motorcycles involve a driver turning left in front of the oncoming rider, so look for riders at the right of the lane or on the shoulder, look again and judge their speed first.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.front: What legal status, full-lane and one-way street rights, and horn etiquette apply around bicyclists?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.expected_back: Bicycles are vehicles under state law with the same duty to obey rules, signs and markings; at normal traffic speed they may use the full lane, on a multi-lane one-way street they may ride on either side, and you should not honk to startle them.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: What makes the No Zones around large trucks and buses so hazardous to nearby cars?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: No Zones are blind areas around trucks and buses where cars vanish from view or sit so close the driver cannot stop or maneuver safely, which greatly raises crash risk.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: Why must you never duck past or stop right behind a truck or bus preparing to back up?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: Never pass or stop close behind a truck or bus that is backing or about to back, because the trailer hides objects in its No Zone.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: Which two visibility losses happen simultaneously when you tailgate a truck or bus?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: Do not tailgate a truck or bus: its driver cannot see you behind it, and it blocks your own view of traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: How do the side blind spots of trucks and buses compare with passenger cars, and what risk follows?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: Trucks and buses have much larger side blind spots than cars, so a sudden lane change or emergency move by the driver could hit you there.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: Why is stopping behind white intersection stop bars especially helpful around turning trucks and buses?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: Trucks and buses need more room to turn and change lanes, so stay behind white stop bars at signs and signals, which are often placed to leave trucks turning room.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: On which side should you overtake a truck, and what mirror cue tells you it is safe to merge back?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: Pass trucks quickly and on the left when you can, and do not cut back in front until both of its headlights show in your rearview mirror, since trucks need longer to slow down.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: What visual mirror benchmark governs pulling back ahead of a semi-truck just like any regular pass?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: Returning in front of a truck after passing uses the same test as any pass: wait until both of its headlights appear in your rearview mirror.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: Why do trucks and buses swing leftward before turning right, and where must you never squeeze?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: Trucks and buses often swing into the left lane to turn right, so never squeeze between one and the curb or shoulder.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: What is a right-signaling truck or bus doing when it shifts left approaching a corner?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: A truck or bus moving into the left lane before a right turn is setting up a wide turn; do not slip between it and the curb or shoulder.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: What emergency role do mountain runaway truck ramps serve, and which three stops are illegal there?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: Runaway truck ramps stop vehicles whose brakes fail; chaining up, changing a tire or parking on a ramp or its entrance is illegal and unsafe.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: What visual sign warns of a runaway truck or bus, and where must you move immediately?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: Smoke from the brakes is one sign of a runaway truck or bus, so get out of its way and never get in front of it.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: Why must you stay extra alert behind transit buses and cautious when passing a stopped one?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: Buses stop often, so stay alert behind them, and take care passing a stopped bus because it may pull into your lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: Who holds right-of-way when a bus pulls back into traffic from a drop-off zone, and whom should you watch for?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: A bus pulling out of a drop-off spot into traffic has the right-of-way, and you should watch for riders waiting, getting off or loading bikes in front of it.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: In which two everyday settings must you use heightened caution around school buses and crossing students?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: Take extra care near school buses in neighborhoods and school zones, where students board, leave and cross the road.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: What do overhead yellow warning lights on a school bus announce, and what triggers the switch to red?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: Overhead yellow warning lights mean a school bus is about to stop for children and stay on until the door opens, when the red STOP lights and STOP arm come on.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: Contrast the meaning of overhead yellow school-bus lights against red lights paired with the STOP arm?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: School bus lights come in two stages: yellow means the bus is about to stop, red with the STOP arm means the door is open and you must stop.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: How far from a stopped school bus's front or rear bumper must you halt, and when may you move?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: Stay stopped at least twenty feet from the front or rear bumper of a school bus until the driver pulls in the STOP arm and turns off the red lights; failing to stop is illegal.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.front: How must you respond to alternating flashing red lights on either end of a school bus?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.expected_back: When a school bus shows alternating flashing red lights from front or rear, stop at least twenty feet before it and go on carefully only after the lights stop.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.front: Compare which directions stop for a school bus on a four-plus-lane median-divided highway versus an undivided two- or four-lane road?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.expected_back: On a divided highway of four or more lanes with a median, only traffic behind the school bus must stop; on a two-lane road, or a four-lane road with no median, traffic both ways must stop.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.front: Who must stop for a school bus on a highway with five or more lanes including a shared center turn lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.expected_back: Where a highway has a shared center turn lane and five or more lanes, the duty to stop falls only on the lanes behind the bus, not on oncoming traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: Across Colorado road layouts, sort where oncoming traffic stops for a school bus versus where oncoming keeps moving?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: Whether oncoming traffic stops for a school bus depends on the road: yes on two-lane roads and four-lane roads without a median, no on divided highways with a median or roads of five or more lanes with a center turn lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.front: How heavy can a light rail car be, and what rule governs turning across light rail tracks?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.expected_back: A light rail vehicle can weigh up to forty tons and cannot stop quickly, so never turn in front of one and check every direction before turning across light rail tracks.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.front: What foot traffic and sightline traps require extra alertness around light rail corridors?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.expected_back: In light rail areas watch for riders boarding and leaving, and stay alert because buildings and plants can hide the trains.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.front: What do light-rail signals and gates command, and why must you never drive around a lowered gate after one train clears?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.expected_back: Traffic lights, warning lights and gates at light rail crossings all mean stop and do not cross; never drive around a gate, even right after a train passes, since another may come from the other way.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.front: How high do standard light-rail overhead wires hang, and how must you handle a downed wire or broken crossing gear?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.expected_back: Light rail overhead wires hang at a standard eighteen feet, six inches above the track center; treat any hanging wire as live, never touch it, and report it or faulty safety devices to RTD.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.front: Which standard traffic control does a railroad crossbuck match, and what does a numbered plaque underneath indicate?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.expected_back: Treat a railroad crossbuck like a yield sign, and a sign below it shows how many tracks the crossing has when there is more than one.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: Contrast your legal duty at a passive railroad crossbuck versus active flashing lights or crossing gates?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: A crossbuck is treated like a yield sign, while flashing lights or gates at a light rail crossing mean stop and do not cross.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.front: Which two large vehicle types must stop at most railroad crossings, and how should following drivers prepare?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.expected_back: Commercial buses and hazardous-materials trucks must stop at most railroad crossings, so be ready to stop when following one.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: What non-driving financial court order can cost you your Colorado driving privilege if left unpaid?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: Failing to pay court-ordered child support is another way to lose your Colorado driving privilege.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: What document must you carry whenever you drive, and what do you risk if you cannot show an officer?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive, and failing to show valid evidence of insurance when an officer asks can cost you your license.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: How can a conviction for buying or holding alcohol under age twenty-one affect your driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: A conviction for buying or possessing alcohol while under twenty-one can also lead to losing your driving privilege.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: In vehicles equipped with built-in belts, which three groups must wear a fastened seat belt on Colorado public roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.memory_hook: Driver, front riders, kids under sixteen
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: On public roads, Colorado requires a fastened seat belt in every vehicle with factory-installed belts for the driver, every front-seat passenger, and every child under sixteen.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: Which five occupational, vehicle, or medical situations are exempt from Colorado's mandatory seat belt rule?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: The only seat belt exceptions are emergency personnel, passenger and school buses, farm equipment, delivery-van drivers while working, and anyone carrying a physician statement saying they cannot wear a belt for physical or psychological reasons.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: When does a delivery-van driver qualify for the seat belt exemption versus have to buckle up like everyone else?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: Seat belts are required for the driver, front-seat passengers and children under sixteen, but delivery-van drivers are exempt only while on the job.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: How do Colorado's seat-belt and passenger-count rules tighten whenever the driver is younger than eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: When the driver is under eighteen, every passenger must be belted or properly restrained, and the passenger count may never be more than the number of seat belts.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: When a child's parent is not riding in the car, who is legally responsible for securing that child properly?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: When no parent is in the vehicle, the driver is responsible for making sure each child is properly secured in the correct child restraint.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: How and where must a child younger than two weighing under forty pounds ride?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: A child younger than two who weighs less than forty pounds must ride in a rear-facing child restraint in the back seat.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: What restraint options apply to a child younger than two who already weighs forty pounds or more?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: A child younger than two who weighs forty pounds or more may ride in either a rear-facing or a forward-facing child restraint.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: For children younger than two, what exact weight threshold separates rear-facing-only from facing either direction?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: The rear-facing rule for a child under two turns on weight: under forty pounds means rear-facing in the back seat, while forty pounds or more allows rear-facing or forward-facing.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: How must a child aged two to under four weighing at least twenty pounds be restrained and seated?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: A child aged two to under four who weighs at least twenty pounds must ride in a rear-facing or forward-facing child restraint, in the back seat when one is available.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: What restraint and seating rule covers a child aged four to under nine weighing forty pounds or more?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: A child aged four to under nine who weighs at least forty pounds must use a child restraint or booster seat in the back seat when the vehicle has one.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: Match the twenty-pound weight floor and the forty-pound booster floor to their exact Colorado child age bands?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: The twenty-pound minimum belongs to the age two to under four band, while the forty-pound minimum belongs to the age four to under nine band that allows a booster seat.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: How must youths from age nine up to eighteen be secured inside a vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: Children from nine to eighteen must be restrained by a seat belt or a child restraint used as the manufacturer directs.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: Where does impairment from alcohol, drugs, or combined substances rank among traffic hazards?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: Impaired driving by alcohol, drugs or a mix of them is among the leading causes of crashes and deaths on the road.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: What drug classification does alcohol belong to, and how does it alter your brain, reflexes, and driving choices?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: Alcohol is a depressant: it slows brain function, reflexes and reaction time, harms thinking and coordination, and makes risky moves such as speeding or abrupt turns more likely.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: Which two open substances are banned inside the passenger area of a vehicle on public roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: It is illegal to have an open container of alcohol or of marijuana in the passenger area of a vehicle on a public road.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: Which five personal and drinking factors explain why two people having the same drinks hit different BAC readings?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: BAC depends on how much you drank, your body weight, how fast you drank, how long since the last drink, and your sex, so two people drinking the same amount can differ.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: Which serving sizes of beer, wine, and distilled spirits pack roughly the same amount of pure alcohol?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.memory_hook: Twelve beer, five wine, one-five spirits
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: Beer, wine and liquor are equally intoxicating per standard drink: twelve ounces of beer, five ounces of wine and one point five ounces of distilled spirits each hold about the same alcohol.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: Why doesn't sticking to beer or wine instead of liquor make driving any safer?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: A standard drink is the same alcohol whether it is twelve ounces of beer, five ounces of wine or one point five ounces of spirits, so switching drink types does not make you safer.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: What is the sole cure for blood alcohol, and how fast does average BAC drop each hour?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: Only time sobers you up, and on average BAC falls by about zero point zero one five percent per hour.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: Why do black coffee, fresh air, or cold showers fail to lower your blood alcohol concentration?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: BAC drops only with time, at about zero point zero one five percent per hour on average; nothing else speeds it up.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: How does Colorado's definition of DWAI differ in impairment degree from DUI?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: DWAI, Driving While Ability Impaired, means impairment to even the slightest degree, while DUI, Driving Under the Influence, means being substantially incapable of driving safely.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: At what blood alcohol reading can a driver be convicted of DUI per se?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: A driver can be convicted of DUI per se when BAC is greater than zero point zero eight percent.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: Separate DWAI, standard DUI, and DUI per se in one clean comparison?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: DWAI and DUI are different charges: DWAI means impaired even slightly, DUI means substantially unable to drive safely, and DUI per se is based on BAC above zero point zero eight percent.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: Besides a chemical BAC reading, which three types of roadside evidence can convict an impaired driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: An impaired driving conviction does not rest on BAC alone; it can be proven by driving behavior, the officer observations during the stop, and performance on Standardized Field Sobriety Tests.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: Alongside test refusal, which three BAC cutoffs for adults, under-twenty-one drivers, and CDL holders trigger license revocation?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: Your license may be revoked for refusing a chemical test, for a BAC over point zero eight, for a BAC over point zero two if you are under twenty-one, or over point zero four if you are a CDL driver.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: Match the revocation BAC thresholds of point zero two, point zero four, and point zero eight to each driver group?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: The revocation BAC level depends on the driver: over point zero eight for most adults, over point zero two for drivers under twenty-one, and over point zero four for CDL drivers.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: For a driver twenty-one or older, what BAC benchmark, points, fine, jail, and service attach to a first DWAI?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: A first DWAI conviction for a driver twenty-one or older is tied to a zero point zero five percent BAC level and carries eight points, a fine of two hundred dollars to five hundred dollars, two to one hundred eighty days in jail and twenty-four to forty-eight hours of public service.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: For a driver twenty-one or older, what BAC benchmark, revocation length, fine, jail, and service follow a first DUI?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: A first DUI for a driver twenty-one or older is tied to zero point zero eight percent BAC and brings a nine-month revocation, a fine of six hundred dollars to one thousand dollars, five to three hundred sixty-five days in jail and forty-eight to ninety-six hours of public service.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: How does the license hit on a first adult DWAI differ fundamentally from a first adult DUI?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: The first DWAI is the only listed impaired-driving conviction measured in points, eight of them, while a first DUI brings a nine-month revocation instead.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: What revocation length, fine range, jail range, and public-service hours hit on a second DWAI or DUI?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: A second DWAI or DUI brings a one-year revocation, a fine of six hundred dollars to one thousand five hundred dollars, ten to three hundred sixty-five days in jail and forty-eight to one hundred twenty hours of public service.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: What revocation length, fine range, jail floor, and public service hit on a third or later DWAI or DUI?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: A third or later DWAI or DUI brings a two-year revocation, a fine of six hundred dollars to one thousand five hundred dollars, sixty to three hundred sixty-five days in jail and forty-eight to one hundred twenty hours of public service.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: Trace how license revocation length climbs across a first DUI, a second offense, and a third or later offense?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: Revocation length climbs with repeat convictions: nine months for a first DUI, one year for a second DWAI or DUI, and two years for a third or later.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: When does a driver under twenty-one face revocation on a first DUI or DWAI versus on a second or third?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: A driver under twenty-one convicted of DUI or DWAI faces revocation on a first conviction if they do not finish the court-ordered evaluation or program, and a second or third conviction means mandatory revocation.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: Does an under-twenty-one alcohol purchase or possession conviction require a car to revoke your license?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: Anyone under twenty-one convicted of buying or possessing alcohol can have their driving privilege revoked even when no driving was involved.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: Contrast how revocation works on a first under-twenty-one DUI or DWAI against a repeat conviction?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: For drivers under twenty-one, a first DUI or DWAI leads to revocation only if the court-ordered evaluation or program is not completed, but a second or third is always revoked.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: How do Colorado's penalties for driving impaired by cannabis, prescriptions, or cold medicine compare with alcohol?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: Driving impaired by any drug, whether illegal drugs, marijuana, prescription or over-the-counter medicine, is illegal and carries the same penalties as alcohol-impaired driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: Does holding a medical prescription or using medical marijuana shield you from a DUI or DWAI charge?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: Using marijuana or another drug for medical reasons is no defense to a DUI or DWAI charge.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.front: Summarize why legal over-the-counter, prescription, and medical cannabis use can still trigger alcohol-style penalties?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.expected_back: Legal or medical use of a drug does not excuse impaired driving; prescription, over-the-counter and medical marijuana impairment are all penalized like alcohol.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: What determines how strongly a drug impairs someone, and which three everyday medication types can impair driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: Drug impairment depends on the dose and the person; tranquilizers, pain killers and allergy or cold remedies can all impair driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: What two steps should you take before driving on any medication, especially when warning print is missing or unclear?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: Read medication labels for warnings before you drive, and ask your doctor or pharmacist when a label is missing or unclear.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: When a five-plus-lane Colorado road includes a shared center turn lane, which directions stop for a school bus?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: On a highway of five or more lanes with a shared center turn lane, vehicles in the lanes behind a stopped school bus must stop fully, while opposite-direction traffic is not legally required to.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: What kind of legal exposure follows from violating Colorado's school bus traffic laws?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: Breaking school bus traffic laws carries serious legal consequences.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: Because trains run on unscheduled clocks day and night, how must you approach every railroad crossing?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: A train can reach a crossing at any hour, so approach with caution and obey every warning device, light, gate and sign.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: How does a train's massive bulk distort your speed sense, and what stopping distance does a fifty-five-mile-per-hour freight train need?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: A train's large size makes it look slower than it really is, and an average freight train at fifty-five miles per hour needs about one mile to stop.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: Why is trying to eyeball whether you can beat an approaching fifty-five-mile-per-hour freight train so risky?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: A train looks slower than it is, and a freight train at fifty-five miles per hour needs about a mile to stop, so judge its speed and distance carefully.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: When you reach railroad tracks lacking flashing lights or gates, what precaution applies before crossing?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: At a crossing without flashing lights or gates, stop beforehand if needed to check for trains.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: What clearance must exist before entering railroad tracks, and what hidden danger lurks at multi-track crossings?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: It is illegal and very dangerous to stop on the tracks; enter a crossing only once you know the rails are clear and your car fits fully past them, and with several tracks watch for a second train.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: Which sole traffic sign uses a circular outline, and why is it placed well ahead of the tracks?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: The round advance warning sign, the only round traffic sign, tells you a railroad crossing is ahead early enough for you to stop if needed.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: What letters mark railroad pavement approaches, where must you wait without a painted line, and how far do trains overhang?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: Railroad pavement markings show an R X R and a stop line; wait behind the line for a passing train, or at least ten feet from the tracks if no line shows, because trains overhang the rails by three feet.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: Where no white stop line is painted before railroad tracks, what minimum setback protects you from train overhang?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: With no stop line painted, keep at least ten feet from the rails, because a train overhangs the tracks by three feet.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: How do you identify a designated railroad quiet zone, and what warns you instead of locomotive horns?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: In a designated quiet zone a No Train Horn sign hangs below the advance warning sign, horns do not sound, and the flashing lights and gates are your warning.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: Which standard sign does a railroad crossbuck mirror, what plaque sits beneath multi-track posts, and when does it turn regulatory?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: Treat a crossbuck like a yield sign; a sign beneath it gives the number of tracks when there is more than one, and the crossbuck is normally a caution sign that becomes regulatory when a train approaches.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: Why must you leave stopping margin behind commercial buses or hazardous-materials trucks nearing railroad tracks?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: Commercial buses and hazardous-materials trucks must stop at most crossings, so be ready to stop when following one.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: When red railroad crossing lights start flashing, what must you do and how long must you hold?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: Always stop when crossing lights flash and do not cross until they stop flashing.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: What is the legal status of the roadway while crossing gates sit lowered, and when may you proceed?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.memory_hook: Road closed until gates, lights clear
sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: Where gates are used with flashing lights, the road is closed while the gates are down; wait until the gates rise and the lights stop flashing.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: Contrast your legal duty at a lone crossbuck against your duty at flashing red lights or lowered gates?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: A crossbuck is a yield-type sign that becomes regulatory as a train approaches, while flashing lights and lowered gates always mean stop.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: How does the job of the round advance railroad sign differ from the job of the crossbuck at the tracks?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: The round advance warning sign only tells you a crossing is ahead in time to stop, while the crossbuck carries a yield duty.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: If your engine dies straddling railroad tracks, what happens first even with empty rails, and whom do you call?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: If your car stalls on the rails, have all occupants leave and move well away right away, train or no train in view, then phone the number on the blue Emergency Notification sign or local law enforcement.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: Where is the blue Emergency Notification System sign mounted at public rail crossings, and when is its line answered?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: Every public highway-rail grade crossing has a blue Emergency Notification System sign, usually on the post below the crossbuck, with a phone number answered at all hours.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: Which emergencies belong on the ENS hotline, and what code on the blue sign lets dispatchers stop the right train?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: The ENS number is for emergencies that would require stopping a train, and giving the DOT crossing number on the sign lets the dispatcher pinpoint the crossing and warn trains.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: Why must phoning the ENS hotline or police always come second when a vehicle stalls on railroad tracks?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: A stalled car on the tracks calls for getting everyone out and away first and phoning the ENS number or police second.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: Which directions can RTD light rail run along Denver-area streets, and what road rules apply to its operators?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: RTD runs light rail vehicles in the Denver metro area, sometimes in the same direction as traffic and sometimes against it, and on streets they obey all signals and signs with the same rights and duties as other motorists.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: How heavy can a single light rail car be, and what check is vital before turning across its tracks?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: A light rail car can weigh up to forty tons and cannot stop quickly, so never turn in front of one or across its tracks without checking every direction.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: What pedestrian and sightline hazards cluster around RTD light rail stops and urban corridors?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: Watch for riders getting on and off a stopped light rail vehicle, and stay alert because buildings and plants can hide light rail vehicles.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.front: Which three types of control devices guard light rail crossings, and what single command do they share?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.expected_back: Light rail crossings may use regular traffic lights, warning lights or gates with arms, and all of them mean stop and do not cross the tracks.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.front: Why must you never weave around light rail gates even the moment one train clears the crossing?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.expected_back: Never drive around light rail gates, even right after a train passes, because another may be coming from the other direction.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.front: At what standard height do light rail overhead wires hang, and how must you treat any sagging or downed line?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.expected_back: Light rail overhead wires sit at a standard eighteen feet, six inches above the track center, so know your vehicle height, assume any hanging wire is live and never touch it or anything touching it.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.front: Whom should you contact immediately upon spotting a low-hanging light rail wire or broken crossing signal?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.expected_back: Report a hanging overhead wire or faulty light rail safety device by calling nine one one or RTD.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.front: How does Colorado roadway law classify bicycles, and what general rules govern riders?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.expected_back: Bicycles are vehicles on the roadway, and their riders generally follow the same rules of the road with many of the same rights and duties as motorists.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.front: How can city or town ordinances modify where bicyclists ride and which rights apply on sidewalks and crosswalks?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.expected_back: Some local ordinances treat bicyclists differently, for example letting them ride on sidewalks and in crosswalks with pedestrian rights and duties.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.front: Does one uniform Colorado statute decide whether bicycles may use sidewalks in every town?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.expected_back: Whether bicyclists may ride on sidewalks depends on local ordinance, not one statewide rule.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.front: What size, protection, and rider-experience factors demand active visual scanning around bicyclists?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.expected_back: Bicyclists are smaller and more vulnerable than people in vehicles and vary in skill, and some are children, so look for them actively and use caution when approaching or passing.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.front: Where do cyclists normally position themselves, and what five conditions let them legally ride down the lane center?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.memory_hook: Right edge unless hazards require center
sec13-card-sec13-F27.expected_back: Bicyclists should ride as far right as they judge safe, but they may take the center of the lane for visibility, on narrow roads, or to avoid car door zones, broken glass or drainage grates.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.front: Under what traffic condition may two cyclists ride side by side in Colorado, and how can that help passing?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.expected_back: Bicyclists may ride side by side when they are not blocking normal, reasonable traffic flow, which can make them more visible and quicker to pass.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: Why shouldn't a motorist assume a cyclist mid-lane or riding two abreast is breaking Colorado law?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: A bicyclist in the center of the lane or riding side by side may be within the law, for visibility or hazard avoidance, as long as normal traffic is not impeded.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.front: From what point on your rig is Colorado's three-foot bicycle pass measured, does it apply beside bike lanes, and what if space is tight?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.expected_back: When passing a bicyclist, even one in a bike lane, give at least three feet from the outermost part of your vehicle or attachments; if you cannot, slow down and stay behind until it is safe.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.front: When does Colorado law allow crossing a solid double yellow centerline to pass a bicyclist?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.expected_back: Crossing a double yellow line with no oncoming traffic is legal when needed to give a bicyclist the three-foot passing gap.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: How do Colorado's double-yellow exception and tight-lane rule work together when overtaking a cyclist?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: The three-foot bicyclist gap allows briefly crossing a double yellow line when nothing is oncoming; if three feet is impossible, stay behind the rider.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.front: How must motorists yield to bicyclists inside intersections?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.expected_back: Yield to bicyclists in intersections as you would to pedestrians and other vehicles.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.front: Who owns priority inside a bike lane, even across unpainted intersection gaps, and what three car actions are banned there?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.expected_back: Bicyclists have the right-of-way in a bike lane, the lane continues through intersections even without paint, and drivers may not stop, park or drive in a bike lane or path.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.front: Before turning left across opposing lanes, where can oncoming cyclists hide and what must you judge?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.expected_back: To avoid the common left-turn crash with an oncoming cyclist, look for riders on the shoulder, at the lane edge or behind other vehicles and judge their speed and distance before turning.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.front: What two-stage sequence prevents stop-sign and traffic-signal collisions with cyclists?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.expected_back: To avoid stop-sign and signal crashes, stop first, then enter the intersection only after looking for and yielding to others.

sec13-card-sec13-F35.front: Before swinging your street-side car door open, what rear check and hand switch help spot passing cyclists?
sec13-card-sec13-F35.expected_back: Before opening a door into the roadway, check behind for passing riders or vehicles, and try opening it with the hand farther from the door.

sec13-card-sec13-F36.front: How should you position and time a right turn when a cyclist is riding straight toward the same corner?
sec13-card-sec13-F36.expected_back: When turning right, yield and let a cyclist going straight clear the intersection first, and turn from close to the curb so no rider can pass unsafely on your right.

sec13-card-sec13-F37.front: Which three paths and directions must you scan before nosing out of a driveway?
sec13-card-sec13-F37.expected_back: When pulling out of a driveway, check both directions and past the curb or driveway for riders on the road, sidewalk or bike path.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: Why is parking or stopping inside a bike lane dangerous, and when is crossing one legal?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: Blocking a bike lane pushes bicyclists into the main travel lane and can endanger them; you may cross a bike lane only when turning or entering or leaving a road, driveway or alley.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: Contrast crossing across a bike lane for an alley or turn against stopping inside it?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: You may cross a bike lane to turn or to enter or leave a road, driveway or alley, but you may not block it.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: Are cyclists required to stay inside a marked bike lane, and which sides work on a one-way multi-lane street?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.memory_hook: May leave lane; either one-way side
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: People on bikes are allowed to ride outside a bike lane, and on a multi-lane one-way street they may ride on either the right or the left side.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: Under Colorado's two-thousand-twenty-two law, how may riders fifteen and older treat clear stop signs and red lights?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.memory_hook: Stop as yield; red as stop
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: Under a law passed in two thousand twenty-two, bicyclists aged fifteen and older who already have the right-of-way at a clear intersection may treat stop signs as yield signs and red stop lights as stop signs.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: Which age cutoff and two intersection conditions limit Colorado's stop-as-yield bicycle rule?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: The stop-as-yield rule covers bicyclists aged fifteen and up only, and only when the intersection is clear and they already have the right-of-way.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: Which direction does Colorado law require cyclists to travel, and why should drivers still scan every angle?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: Bicyclists must ride in the same direction as traffic, but look for them anywhere on the roadway anyway.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: When must your turn signal be blinking, and what must you verify when driving straight?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: Always signal before turning and keep the signal off while going straight.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: How should you position your vehicle for a right turn, including where a green or dashed Conflict Zone is marked?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: Turn right hugging the curb, using a Conflict Zone where one is marked, so riders approaching from behind are not tempted to pass you on the right.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: As you set up for a right turn and spot a bicyclist riding alongside you, who goes first?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: When a bicyclist is beside you as you prepare to turn right, slow down, yield and let the rider clear the intersection first.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: After stopping completely for a legal right turn on red, which three bicycle paths must you check?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: Before a legal right turn on red, stop completely and look for bicyclists behind or beside you, turning left from across the street, or riding in the lane you will join.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: Before backing, changing lanes, or turning, especially turning left, where must you look for cyclists?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: Check your path and blind spots for bicyclists before backing, changing lanes or turning, and before a left turn look for riders on the right side or shoulder and judge their speed.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: How does Colorado law classify deliberately crowding or forcing a bicyclist off the roadway?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: Forcing a bicyclist off the road counts as aggressive driving and carries legal consequences.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: What dual mindset should guide motorists whenever sharing lanes with bicyclists?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: Treat bicyclists as drivers with a right to the road who are also more vulnerable, look for them actively and judge their speed and distance carefully.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: Which three vehicle, road, or weather situations call for giving a cyclist wider room than three feet?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: Give a bicyclist more than three feet of room when you drive a bigger vehicle, are on a rural road or face wind, because wind blasts are dangerous.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: Why must you never cut in and brake hard or turn sharply right ahead of a moving bicyclist?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: Never turn sharply, slow down or stop suddenly in front of a bicyclist, because car brakes are stronger than bicycle brakes and a crash could follow.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: Why do wet asphalt, gravel, and road debris call for extra patience around bicyclists?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: Wet roads and debris affect bicyclists far more than drivers, so take extra care around riders in those conditions.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: Under what sole circumstance should you sound your horn near a bicyclist?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: Do not honk near bicyclists unless a crash is about to happen, because the noise can startle them into crashing.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: What street-parking exit habit is called the Dutch Reach, and which hand opens the latch?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: Before opening a door when parked on the street, check sides and rear for bicyclists and open it with the hand nearer the center of the vehicle, a habit called the Dutch Reach.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: Why might a cyclist keep both hands gripping the bars instead of signaling, and what clues tip you off?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: Bicyclists must hand-signal turns and stops, yet skill level or road or traffic conditions may require both hands on the handlebars, so watch for head turns or shoulder glances.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: How does a cyclist hand-signal a right turn, a left turn, and slowing or stopping?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.memory_hook: Right out-or-up; left out; down stop
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: A bicyclist signals a right turn with the right arm straight out or the left arm bent upward at a right angle, a left turn with the left arm straight out, and slowing or stopping with the left arm bent downward.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: When a cyclist ahead bends their left arm ninety degrees upward, which turn are they signaling?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: A bicyclist has two valid right-turn signals, right arm straight out or left arm bent up, so a raised left arm means right, not left.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: Contrast a cyclist holding their left arm straight out horizontally against bending that left arm downward?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: A left arm bent downward means the rider is slowing or stopping, while a left arm held straight out means a left turn.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: How do a motorcyclist's legal road rights compare with their physical protection in a crash?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: Motorcyclists have the same rights and duties as other drivers but little crash protection, so a hit from a larger vehicle can injure or kill them.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: How much lane width belongs to a motorcycle, why do riders weave inside it, and what can gusts do?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane width and often shift within it to see, be seen and avoid hazards, and strong wind can push one out of its lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: Under what traffic state, space check, and speed cap may a two-wheeled motorcycle lane filter in Colorado?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: A two-wheeled motorcycle may lane filter past a stopped vehicle in its lane only when neighboring lanes are also stopped, there is room, and it moves no faster than fifteen miles per hour.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: Does Colorado's lane-filtering rule allow weaving between moving highway traffic or using three-wheeled trikes?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: Lane filtering is passing stopped traffic within a lane at low speed, and the rule is written for two-wheeled motorcycles.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: Which visibility, braking, and road-surface traits call for leaving a longer following gap behind motorcycles?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: Motorcycles are small and hard to see, can speed up and stop faster than expected, and are endangered by road defects and debris, so use extra caution and a longer following distance.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.front: Which turning mistake ranks among top bicycle crashes, and where must your eyes sweep first?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.expected_back: Common bicycle collisions include a driver turning left in front of an oncoming rider, so look for riders on the shoulder or lane edge before turning.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.front: Beyond left turns, which four everyday mistakes commonly cause car-bicycle collisions?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.expected_back: Other common bicycle collisions come from running stop signs or signals, opening a door without looking back, riders going the wrong way against traffic, and drivers pulling out of driveways without looking.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.front: Is sharing the road with bikes, motorcycles, and walkers merely polite advice or a legal mandate?
