sec14-card-sec14-F31.expected_back: Sharing the road is required by law, not just a safety habit.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.front: Who falls under Colorado's pedestrian definition across public and private pavement, and who bears watch duty?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.expected_back: Pedestrians, meaning people standing, walking, running or using mobility aids on public roads or private property, are the most vulnerable road users, and watching out for them is the driver's duty.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.front: Why must you sometimes slow below the posted limit near foot traffic, especially around kids or wheelchair users?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.expected_back: Obey the speed limit or go slower when needed to spot and react to pedestrians, and remember that children and wheelchair users sit lower and are harder to see.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.front: At which intersections and crosswalks do pedestrians hold right-of-way, and what must drivers do?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.memory_hook: Every intersection crosswalk, painted or not
sec14-card-sec14-F27.expected_back: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at every intersection and crosswalk, painted or not, and drivers must yield or stop completely to let them cross safely.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: Does missing crosswalk paint strip a pedestrian of right-of-way at a street intersection?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at intersections and crosswalks even where no lines are painted.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.front: Before edging forward to check vehicle gaps for a turn on red, what lane, stop, and walker steps come first?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.expected_back: When turning on red, be in the correct lane, stop completely and check for pedestrians in all directions before creeping forward to look for traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: Put stopping for pedestrians and creeping forward for cross-traffic sightlines in the right order on a red turn?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.expected_back: When turning on red, the checks come in order: stop and check for pedestrians in every direction first, then edge forward to look for vehicles.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.front: Why must you never stop across a crosswalk or whip around another car paused beside one?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.expected_back: Never stop with any part of your vehicle over the crosswalk, and never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk, since its driver may be waiting for a pedestrian you cannot see.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.front: Around parked cars, busy gathering spots, and backing maneuvers, what pedestrian habits protect lives?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.expected_back: Watch for people getting in or out of parked cars, drive very carefully near schools, parks, parking lots, bus stops and events, and check mirrors and blind spots when backing out.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.front: Which three driver faculties can a distraction pull away, and how do mental distractions compare with physical ones?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.expected_back: A distraction is anything that takes your eyes, hands or mind off driving, and mental distractions are just as dangerous as physical ones; even tuning the radio is risky in bad weather or heavy traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.front: Which seven everyday eating, grooming, smoking, or audio habits does Colorado tell drivers to skip while moving?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.expected_back: Do not eat, drink, read, smoke, vape, apply makeup or adjust music while driving.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.front: Why does a minor cabin distraction turn far deadlier when alcohol, cannabis, or drugs are involved?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.expected_back: Alcohol, marijuana and many other drugs reduce the ability to handle several tasks, so a distraction that is merely hazardous for a sober driver can be deadly for an impaired one.

sec14-card-sec14-F35.front: When may adult Colorado drivers use a mobile electronic device, and what penalties follow careless manual texting?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.expected_back: Drivers may not use a mobile electronic device unless hands-free or in an emergency; careless driving caused by texting or other manual device use can bring a fine or a misdemeanor charge, so pull off the road to use a phone.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: What legal trouble can manual phone use or texting trigger if it makes your driving careless?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: Hands-free use is allowed for mobile devices, but careless driving from texting or any manual device use can still bring a fine or misdemeanor charge.

sec14-card-sec14-F36.front: How should you handle kids, pets, audio presets, cabin controls, and navigation before shifting into drive?
sec14-card-sec14-F36.expected_back: To prevent distraction, skip phone use and emotional conversations, restrain children properly, put pets in a carrier or kennel, learn your controls, preset radio stations and playlists, and plan your route before driving.

sec14-card-sec14-F37.front: What makes dangerous behavior behind the wheel count as aggressive driving in Colorado?
sec14-card-sec14-F37.expected_back: Aggressive driving is any willful behavior behind the wheel that endangers people or property without regard for safety.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.front: How does Colorado define reckless driving, and must a driver intend harm to commit it?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.expected_back: Reckless driving means operating a vehicle in a way that endangers people or property, whether or not it is intentional.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.front: When can a Colorado officer cite you for reckless driving, and how many record points can follow conviction?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.expected_back: If an officer sees your driving as endangering a person or property, including another vehicle, you can be charged under the reckless driving statute and face up to eight points on your record if convicted.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.front: When do tailgating, shoulder passing, red-light running, or angry combinations count as aggressive driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.expected_back: Tailgating, passing on the shoulder or running a red light can be treated as aggressive when an officer believes it was willful and endangered others, and so can a mix of speeding, cutting off, swerving, honking, flashing lights, yelling and rude gestures.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.front: What mental state separates aggressive driving from reckless driving under Colorado's handbook?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.expected_back: Reckless driving needs no intent, only danger to people or property, while aggressive driving turns on willful acts that put others in danger.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.front: Which three hostile acts toward another motorist escalate past traffic tickets into criminal charges?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.expected_back: Showing a weapon to another motorist, bumping or ramming a vehicle, or chasing a vehicle at high speed can bring criminal charges beyond reckless driving.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.front: What four non-engagement habits protect you when an aggressive driver targets your lane?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.expected_back: To protect yourself from an aggressive driver, do not engage: avoid eye contact, do not respond in kind, back off and let the driver go.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.front: Which cabin behaviors, from muttering insults and blocking merges to confronting someone, warn of aggressive driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.expected_back: Anyone can become an aggressive driver; warning signs include insulting other drivers, blocking merges or passing, tailgating to push someone, angry speeding, running controls out of anger, honking or yelling, gestures, pursuing or ramming, getting out to confront, or thinking about attacking.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.front: Answering yes to how many aggressive-driving self-check questions signals real personal risk?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.expected_back: Answering yes to even a couple of the self-check questions means you may be at risk of becoming an aggressive driver.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.front: Which five pre-trip and on-road mindset choices prevent you from turning into an aggressive driver?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.expected_back: To avoid becoming aggressive, leave early, expect others to make mistakes, stay calm, keep anger from elsewhere out of your driving and let people merge even if they were rude.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.front: When a crash suddenly looks likely ahead, why is freezing in panic the worst response?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.expected_back: When a crash seems likely, many drivers panic, yet there is almost always something you can do to avoid it or lessen its results.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.front: What are the three fundamental maneuvers for avoiding an impending collision?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.expected_back: The three ways to avoid a collision are to slow down or stop, to turn, or to speed up.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.front: Between stopping dead and steering around a sudden obstacle, which works faster and how do you hold the wheel?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.expected_back: You can usually turn a vehicle faster than you can stop it, so steer around a hazard if that will not cause another crash, gripping the wheel with both hands and staying ready to control the car afterward.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.front: If an oncoming car drifts into your lane, how does leaving the roadway compare with taking a head-on hit?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.expected_back: Leaving the road is generally a better outcome than a head-on collision with another vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.front: In what crash-threat scenario is pressing the gas, followed by easing back down, your safest escape?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.expected_back: Accelerating out of danger can be the answer when another vehicle is about to strike your side or rear and the road ahead is open; slow back down afterward.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.front: Where and during what daily window do roughly ninety percent of Colorado deer and elk crashes happen?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.expected_back: Watch for animals especially in rural and mountain areas and between dusk and dawn, when about ninety percent of deer and elk crashes happen, and slow down and look on entering a marked animal crossing.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.front: Why can holding your lane and striking a deer or elk be safer than jerking the wheel sharply?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.expected_back: A drastic swerve to miss a large animal can cause loss of control and a worse crash, so hitting the animal may be the safest choice; focus on keeping control before, during and after impact.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.front: Pair Colorado's two counter-intuitive survival choices for large animals on the road versus oncoming head-on threats?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.expected_back: Swerving hard to miss a large animal can be more dangerous than hitting it, and running off the road beats a head-on crash.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.front: How do you brake for a panic stop with anti-lock brakes, even when the pedal vibrates or pushes back?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.expected_back: To stop fast with anti-lock brakes, press hard and firmly and keep the pedal down even if it pushes back, since ABS works only while the pedal is pressed.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.front: Without anti-lock brakes, how hard should you press the pedal, and how do you recover if wheels lock?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.expected_back: To stop fast without anti-lock brakes, brake as hard as you can without locking the wheels; if they lock and you skid, ease off slightly, then brake again once the skid stops, repeating until stopped.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.front: Contrast your footwork during an emergency stop in an ABS car versus a car without ABS?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.expected_back: Emergency braking is opposite by brake type: with ABS keep firm pressure and never let up, without ABS brake just short of lockup and ease off if you skid.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.front: What steering advantage do anti-lock brakes preserve during hard emergency braking?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.expected_back: Anti-lock brakes let you steer while braking without skidding, which helps when you must turn and slow at once.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.front: How do you execute an emergency turn in a vehicle without anti-lock brakes so it does not plow straight?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.expected_back: Without anti-lock brakes, brake to slow somewhat, then release the brake before the evasive turn, and do not lock the front wheels or turn so sharply that the car only plows ahead.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.front: Put slowing, releasing the brake pedal, and steering away in exact sequence for a non-ABS evasive turn?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.expected_back: Without ABS, an emergency turn is done in sequence: brake to slow, release the brake, then steer away, never locking the front wheels.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.front: What simple ownership habit sharply cuts the odds of mechanical failure on the road?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.expected_back: Following the maintenance schedule in the owner's manual greatly reduces the chance of a vehicle failure.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.front: Walk through the step-by-step recovery if your service brakes fail, and may you keep driving afterward?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.expected_back: If the brakes fail, lift off the gas and pump the pedal; if that fails, apply the parking brake slowly, ready to release it if you skid, then shift to lower gears, find a safe spot off the road and do not drive on without brakes.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.front: If your gas pedal sticks down at speed, what gear move comes before pulling off and shutting down?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.expected_back: If the gas pedal jams, keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral quickly, pull off when safe and turn off the engine.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.front: Contrast your immediate mechanical response to failed brakes against a jammed gas pedal?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.memory_hook: Failed brakes pump; stuck gas neutral
sec15-card-sec15-R04.expected_back: Brake failure starts with pumping the pedal, then the parking brake applied slowly, then lower gears; a jammed gas pedal calls for shifting to neutral.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.front: When a tire blows out at speed, how should you handle steering, gas, and brakes until off the road?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.memory_hook: Grip straight, lift gas, light brake
sec15-card-sec15-F23.expected_back: In a tire blowout, grip the wheel tightly, keep going straight, take your foot off the gas, brake lightly and slow gradually, then pull off the road somewhere safe.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.front: Why must you resist slamming the brakes or stopping right in a travel lane during a tire blowout?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.expected_back: A blowout calls for gentle braking while holding straight, not hard braking or an immediate stop on the road.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.front: If your engine stalls and power assist cuts out while rolling, do steering and brakes still work?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.expected_back: If power fails, hold the wheel firmly and pull off the road; steering will be hard but possible, and the brakes still work with much harder pressure.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.front: If your headlights suddenly go dark at night, what steps help you see and get off the road?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.expected_back: If headlights fail, pull off as soon as possible, try the switch a few times, and if that does not work use the emergency flashers, turn signals or fog lights.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.front: Where must a driver involved in a Colorado crash present proof of insurance to law enforcement?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.expected_back: After a crash you must show proof of insurance to law enforcement, either at the scene or at the police station.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.front: When an injured driver is physically unable to report a crash, whose legal duty steps in?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.memory_hook: Passenger reports and stays if told
sec15-card-sec15-F28.expected_back: If the driver cannot physically report an injury crash, a passenger must report it and, if law enforcement directs, stay at the scene until officers arrive.

sec15-card-sec15-F29.front: What immediate stop, aid, reporting, and information-exchange duties apply after any traffic crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F29.expected_back: After a crash, stop at once and never leave, check for injuries and give reasonable help where practical, call law enforcement and emergency services, and exchange names, addresses, phone numbers, registration and insurance.

sec15-card-sec15-F31.front: If you bump an unattended parked car and cannot locate its owner, what two actions are required?
sec15-card-sec15-F31.expected_back: If you hit a parked car and cannot find its owner, call law enforcement and leave a note where the owner will find it.

sec15-card-sec15-F30.front: During severe-weather Accident Alert Status, how do sober, uninjured drivers with drivable cars handle a crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F30.expected_back: During Accident Alert Status, when severe weather keeps officers from answering all crashes, drivers in a crash with no alcohol, drugs or injuries and drivable vehicles exchange information and must file a report within twenty-four hours.

sec15-card-sec15-F32.front: After a minor divided-highway crash with drivable cars and zero injuries or impairment, what must drivers do?
sec15-card-sec15-F32.expected_back: Under the Move It Law, after a minor divided-highway crash with drivable vehicles and no injuries, drugs or alcohol, drivers must get the vehicles off the highway, and police and insurers will not penalize them for it.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.front: With drivable cars and zero injuries or impairment, how does the Move It Law differ from Accident Alert Status?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.memory_hook: Move It clears; Alert reports later
sec15-card-sec15-R06.expected_back: When vehicles are drivable and neither injuries nor drugs or alcohol are involved, the Move It Law requires clearing a minor divided-highway crash off the road, whereas Accident Alert Status requires exchanging details and reporting within twenty-four hours.

sec15-card-sec15-F33.front: When passing any stopped highway vehicle flashing its hazards, what lane change or speed drop does Colorado require?
sec15-card-sec15-F33.expected_back: The Move Over Law requires moving over one lane, when safe, for any stopped vehicle on a highway with hazards flashing; if that is unsafe or the road has one lane each way, slow to at least twenty miles per hour under the posted limit.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.front: Under Colorado's Move Over Law, when do you drop at least twenty miles per hour below the limit instead of changing lanes?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.expected_back: For any stationary highway vehicle flashing its hazards, the Move Over Law requires moving over one lane when safe, or slowing to at least twenty miles per hour below the posted speed limit if unsafe or on a road with one lane each way.

sec15-card-sec15-F34.front: What standard of care do Good Samaritan laws expect, and how do they shield everyday crash rescuers?
sec15-card-sec15-F34.expected_back: Good Samaritan laws encourage helping in emergencies and expect common sense and reasonable skill within your training; acting as a reasonable, prudent person generally protects a rescuer from being sued and held financially responsible.

sec15-card-sec15-F35.front: When may a bystander move an injured crash victim, and what consent, check, call, and care rules apply?
sec15-card-sec15-F35.memory_hook: Move for danger; ask, call, stay
sec15-card-sec15-F35.expected_back: A reasonable rescuer moves a victim only if life is in danger, asks a conscious victim before helping, checks for life-threatening problems first, calls for professional help and keeps giving care until trained help arrives.

sec15-card-sec15-F36.front: What card mark and registry enrollment happen when you say yes to organ, eye, and tissue donation at licensing?
sec15-card-sec15-F36.expected_back: When applying for or renewing a license, permit or ID you are asked whether to register as an organ, eye and tissue donor; a yes puts a heart with a Y on the card and adds you to the Donate Life Colorado registry until you change it.

sec15-card-sec15-F37.front: Whose names honor Colorado's voluntary licensing donation fund, and what does that money support?
sec15-card-sec15-F37.expected_back: You are also asked whether to make a voluntary gift to the organ and tissue donation awareness fund named for Emily Keyes and John W. Buckner, which pays for public outreach and education.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: What minimum age and credential do you need to operate a car, motor-driven cycle, or moped on Colorado public roads?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: Anyone driving a motor vehicle, motor-driven cycle or moped on public roads in Colorado has to be at least sixteen years old and carry a valid driver license.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: Which three examples involving business, living stretch, or employment make Colorado count you as a state resident?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: Colorado counts you as a resident if, for example, you own or run a business in the state, have lived there continuously for ninety days, or hold a job there.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: How many days after becoming a Colorado resident do you have to obtain a Colorado driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: Once you become a Colorado resident, you have thirty days to get a Colorado driver license.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: Which three groups living in Colorado are exempt from the thirty-day new-resident licensing deadline?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: The thirty-day licensing deadline does not apply to active-duty U.S. military members, their dependents, or people living in Colorado mainly to further their education.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: Within how many days must you notify the DMV after changing your name or home address?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: If your name or address changes, you must tell the Division of Motor Vehicles within thirty days.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: How do Colorado's thirty-day licensing and record-update deadlines contrast with the ninety-day continuous-living rule?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: Three different Colorado deadlines share the same length: getting a Colorado license after becoming a resident and reporting a name or address change are both thirty days, while the residency example is ninety days of continuous living in the state.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: Which handbook topics appear on the written knowledge exam, and where can you take official practice quizzes?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: The written knowledge test draws on the whole handbook, including road signs, driving under the influence, driving rules, safety rules and legal topics; practice quizzes are offered online and in the myColorado app.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: How long before scheduled closing do offices stop starting written knowledge exams?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: Offices stop giving written tests thirty minutes before their scheduled closing time, so arrive earlier than that.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: How does the number thirty work differently for the written-test office cutoff than for residency and address rules?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: The written test is not offered in the final thirty minutes before closing, which is a scheduling rule and is different from the thirty-day residency and address-change deadlines.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: What credential do you qualify for once you pass the written exam, and what does it grant?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: Passing a written test makes you eligible for an instruction permit, which gives a learner limited driving privileges.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: What age, license status, and seating position are required for your supervising driver while you use an instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: While driving on an instruction permit, you need a supervising driver aged twenty-one or older, holding a valid Colorado license, in the front passenger seat.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: How does Colorado's general minimum age to drive compare with the minimum age to supervise a permit holder?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: The general minimum age to drive in Colorado is sixteen, but a permit supervisor must be at least twenty-one; do not mix up the driver age with the supervisor age.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: Who administers most Colorado drive tests since state driver license offices do not currently schedule them?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: State driver license offices do not currently schedule drive tests; some county-run offices do, and most drive tests are given by certified commercial driving schools.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: Which vehicle parts and documents does the examiner verify before your road test can roll?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: Before a drive test the examiner checks the vehicle for safety, including brake lights, turn signals, seat belts, windshield and tires, and confirms the doors and windows open from inside; a vehicle you supply needs current insurance and registration.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: Who is allowed inside the vehicle during a drive test, and what items or electronics must be removed, cleared, or turned off?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: During the drive test only you and the examiner may be in the car: no interpreters, family, friends or pets; remove any weapons, switch off the radio, phone and other electronics, and clear the dashboard and rearview mirror.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: How soon may you take another shot at the drive test if you do not pass?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: If you fail the drive test, you cannot retake it until the next business day.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: What mandatory waiting rule applies to anyone who fails the driving skills test?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: Anyone who fails the driving skills test must wait until the next business day before taking the drive test again.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: Will an examiner ever trick you into breaking a traffic law, and when should you ask questions?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: The examiner will never ask you to break the law; ask your questions before the test starts, because you are scored the entire time and extra talking only interferes.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: Which three AAMVA skill categories does Colorado's drive test evaluate, and what does each cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: The drive test follows AAMVA guidelines and assesses three skill categories: perceptual (seeing gaps and hazards), motor (operating the controls) and attentional (focusing and shifting attention).

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: Which six everyday traffic maneuvers combine to build your Colorado drive-test score?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: Your drive test score comes from six maneuvers: left and right turns, stopping at intersections, driving through intersections, changing lanes in traffic, general driving behavior, and merging into and leaving traffic.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: At which three stages of driving does the examiner grade whether you picked the proper lane?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: Lane selection is graded: enter and leave traffic from the correct lane, approach intersections in the correct lane, and finish each maneuver in the correct lane.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: What lane-tracking and steering-wheel habits are graded under lane management during turns?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: Lane management is graded: stay entirely within the turning lane, keep both hands on the wheel, and steer with an approved method such as hand-over-hand or push-pull-slide.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: From which part of your lane should you initiate a right turn versus a left turn?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: When turning right, start from the right-most part of your lane; when turning left, start from the left-most part of your lane.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: Where in the receiving lane should your car settle after a turn, and what two contact errors must you avoid?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: After a turn, settle the car in the center of the proper lane and never cross lane markings or ride over curbs.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: Put together the exact starting edge and finishing lane position expected on right and left turns?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: Always turn right from the right-most portion of your lane and left from the left-most portion, then finish centered in the proper lane without crossing markings or curbs.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: For how many feet before turning or switching lanes must your blinker run in urban areas versus on four-lane highways?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.memory_hook: One hundred town, two hundred highway
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: Keep your turn signal on continuously for one hundred feet before turning or changing lanes in urban areas, and for two hundred feet before doing so on four-lane highways.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: Within how many seconds after completing a turn or lane change must you cancel your turn signal?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: Cancel your turn signal within three seconds after you finish the turn or lane change.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: Combine Colorado's urban and four-lane highway signal distances with the post-move cancellation timer?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.memory_hook: One hundred, two hundred, three seconds
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: The turn signal distance depends on the road: one hundred feet in urban areas versus two hundred feet on four-lane highways, and either way the signal is canceled within three seconds after the move.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: What three smooth habits demonstrate proper speed control when slowing, changing lanes, and entering turns?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.memory_hook: Smooth slowing, steady lanes, slow entry
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: Good speed control means slowing smoothly without holding up traffic, keeping a steady speed through a lane change, and reaching an intersection slowly enough to turn without braking mid-turn.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: What three checks define a proper stop regarding motion, pavement lines, and front-wheel angle?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.memory_hook: Full halt, behind lines, wheels straight
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: A correct stop has no forward motion, stays behind the stop line and crosswalk, and keeps the front wheels pointed straight until you begin the turn.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: What visual cue tells you that you stopped far enough behind the vehicle ahead in traffic?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: When stopped behind another vehicle, you are far enough back if you can see where its rear tires touch the pavement.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: Which six rough or sluggish mistakes must you avoid while accelerating on the drive test?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: Accelerate smoothly: do not jerk, lug the engine, coast, clash gears, stall, or hold up traffic.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: Which five scanning, mirror, shoulder, and intersection checks make up proper visual searching?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: Searching means scanning traffic, checking over your shoulder before a lane change, using mirrors, looking left, right, then left again before entering an intersection, and looking behind after every turn.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: How are backup cameras and blind-spot or lane alerts treated during the Colorado drive test?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.memory_hook: Driver aids allowed, head checks required
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: Back-up cameras and blind-spot or lane-departure warnings may be used during the drive test, but they never replace your own physical searching.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: Which form must applicants under eighteen submit, and which adults are eligible to sign it?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: Applicants under eighteen must include an Affidavit of Liability (form DR2460), signed by a parent, stepparent, grandparent with power of attorney, legal guardian, spouse over eighteen, or another responsible adult who accepts legal liability.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: In front of whom is the liability affidavit signed, what happens if the signer withdraws, and who may be exempt?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: The affidavit is signed before a driver license office employee or a notary; the signer becomes legally responsible for your driving and may withdraw, which cancels your permit or license; minors in foster care can be exempt under certain conditions.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: What age requirement lets a spouse sign a minor's Affidavit of Liability, and what does withdrawing that signature do?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: The Affidavit of Liability signer can be a spouse only if that spouse is older than eighteen, and withdrawing the signature cancels the minor permit or license.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.front: For how many months must a minor hold an instruction permit before applying for a Colorado driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.expected_back: A minor must hold an instruction permit for twelve months before applying for a driver license.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.front: How many total and nighttime driving hours must appear on a minor applicant's signed driving log?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.expected_back: A minor applicant must turn in a signed driving log showing fifty hours of driving, including ten hours at night.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: Do a minor's ten required night hours add on top of the fifty logged hours or count inside them?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: The minor log requires fifty total hours, of which ten must be at night; the night hours are part of the total, not added on top.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.front: Which minor age bracket owes six instructor-led driving hours before licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.expected_back: Applicants younger than sixteen and six months must also complete six hours of behind-the-wheel training with an approved driver education instructor.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.front: When may twelve extra supervised hours replace the six instructor hours, and what proof do you bring?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.expected_back: If no approved school within thirty miles of home offers at least twenty hours of behind-the-wheel training per week, twelve extra hours with a parent, guardian or alternate permit supervisor may replace the six instructor hours; bring a printed route map if the nearest commercial school is more than thirty miles away.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: Tie together who owes the six behind-the-wheel instructor hours and when the twelve-hour substitute applies?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: The six hours of behind-the-wheel instruction apply only to applicants younger than sixteen and six months, and the twelve extra supervised hours are a substitute only where no qualifying school is within thirty miles.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.front: During the first six months with a minor license, what is the rule on carrying passengers under twenty-one?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.expected_back: For the first six months after a driver under eighteen is licensed, no passengers under twenty-one are allowed unless a parent or another licensed adult driver is in the car.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.front: How do minor passenger rules open up from six months to one year, and then after one full year?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.expected_back: From six months to one year of licensure, a driver under eighteen may carry one passenger under twenty-one, with siblings and passengers in a medical emergency as exceptions; after one year, passengers may equal the number of seat belts.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: Walk through all three passenger stages across a minor driver's first year and beyond?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: Passenger limits step up with time licensed: none under twenty-one in the first six months without an adult driver, one under twenty-one after six months, and as many as there are seat belts after one year.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.front: Between which overnight hours is a first-year minor barred from solo driving, and which four exceptions apply?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.expected_back: During the first year of licensure, a minor may not drive between midnight and five a.m. unless accompanied by an instructor, parent or legal guardian; exceptions cover trips to school or work with a signed statement, medical emergencies and emancipated minors.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: During the midnight-to-five curfew in year one, what exact proof makes a school or work drive legal?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: The curfew window for first-year minors runs from midnight to five a.m., and a school or work trip is excused only with a signed statement from the school or employer.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.front: Which three point, impairment, or testing triggers can suspend, revoke, or cancel your driving privilege?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.expected_back: Your driving privilege can be suspended, revoked or canceled if you reach the point total for suspension, are convicted of driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs, or refuse an alcohol or drug test.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.front: Which two crash-scene or reporting failures can strip away your Colorado driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.expected_back: Leaving a crash scene without stopping, exchanging information and giving aid, or failing to report a crash to the DMV under the Financial Responsibility Law, can also cost you your license.

sec01-card-sec01-F40.front: Which five application, judgment, misuse, re-exam, or felony grounds can also cost your license?
sec01-card-sec01-F40.expected_back: Other grounds for losing your license include lying on your application, not settling a crash judgment, lending or misusing your license, skipping a DMV re-examination, and a vehicular homicide conviction.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.front: Why is it wrong to assume only points or impaired driving can cost your license after a collision?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.expected_back: Losing your license can come from conduct after a crash, such as leaving the scene or not reporting it under the Financial Responsibility Law, not only from driving under the influence or points.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: Which mental and physical driving abilities does marijuana impair, and what does that do to crash risk?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Safe driving demands both planning ahead and smooth hand-eye tracking, and cannabis degrades both at once.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: Which four factors control how strongly marijuana impairs a person?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Edibles, vapes, and smoking peak on totally different timelines, catching users off guard hours later.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: How reliably does a measured THC reading in blood, breath, or saliva reflect actual driving impairment?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Unlike alcohol, someone can feel heavily impaired with a low lab number or vary widely across body fluids.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: Why does observed driving behavior carry extra weight in marijuana cases compared with alcohol BAC cases?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: Because THC numbers do not mirror impairment like BAC does, lane weaving and roadside performance seal the case.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: What blood THC concentration lets a Colorado jury or court draw a permissible inference of DUI?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Five nanograms per milliliter is not an automatic pass below five, yet at five it supports inferring DUI.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: Does DWAI have a blood THC inference number, and how are most marijuana-impaired drivers convicted?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Waiting for a magic safe number fails when officers combine bad driving with any blood THC presence.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: Between DUI and DWAI, where does Colorado's five-nanogram blood THC inference apply and where does it not?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Exam questions love swapping the two charges, so tie five nanograms strictly to DUI and zero cutoff to DWAI.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: What does polydrug impairment mean, and why is combining substances before driving especially dangerous?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Combining even one drink with cannabis or allergy pills can amplify impairment far beyond either substance alone.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: How do illegal drugs like LSD, methamphetamine, and heroin distort a driver's reflexes, confidence, or alertness?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Stimulants trick you into feeling invincible during reckless moves while opioids make you nod off mid-lane.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: Can a driver escape conviction because a specific drug was unusual or showed only a tiny amount in fluids?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Trained officers document real-world impairment on the road, so neither the drug's name nor trace lab amounts save you.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: Which three major consequences can follow any alcohol or drug driving offense in Colorado?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Impaired convictions hit freedom, bank accounts, and mobility all at the same time.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: What is Colorado's rule on plea bargaining an alcohol or drug driving charge down, and what is your only sure safeguard?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Counting on a lawyer to plead a DUI down to a minor ticket fails in Colorado, leaving sobriety as the sole guarantee.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: Under Colorado's Express Consent Law, what agreement do you make automatically whenever you drive in the state?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Taking the wheel on Colorado pavement legally locks in your agreement to test for alcohol or drugs if suspected.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: Which four body-fluid or breath samples can an officer require when impaired driving is suspected?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Different substances show up in different samples, so Express Consent extends well beyond a roadside breath tube.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: Why is it a mistake to think Colorado's Express Consent Law applies only to breathalyzers?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Refusing blood, saliva, or urine when drug impairment is suspected triggers the exact same refusal fallout as refusing breath.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: What license revocation and ignition-interlock requirements hit if you refuse or fail to cooperate with testing?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Stonewalling a test costs a full year off the road followed by two years blowing into an interlock on every car.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: When does an ignition interlock demand breath samples, and how does it respond to elevated alcohol?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Requiring rolling retests while driving stops someone from having a sober friend blow once in the driveway.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: How are other suspensions or revocations from the same stop scheduled alongside a test-refusal revocation?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Serving penalties back-to-back instead of together means refusing a test stretches your total time unlicensed.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: Keep straight which refusal sanction lasts one year and which lasts two years?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: Test writers flip those two durations constantly, so put the one-year revocation first and two-year interlock second.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: Do extra suspensions from the same incident run concurrently with a refusal revocation or tack onto the end?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Nothing runs simultaneously here; clock two waits until the full one-year refusal revocation finishes.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: Which five personal qualities and sensory habits does safe driving require before you turn the key?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Anger, exhaustion, or illness can wreck your judgment on the road even when you are completely sober.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: Why is sharp eyesight central to driving, and how often should a specialist check your vision?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Eyesight shifts gradually enough that you rarely notice blurry distance signs without an exam every year or two.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: What must you wear on every single trip if your driver license lists a corrective lens restriction?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Even a two-minute daylight errand without required lenses violates your license restriction and blurs hazards.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: How should you break up long road trips, and what should you do whenever drowsiness creeps in?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Fatigue dulls reaction speed like alcohol, so planned two-hour breaks and prompt rest stops prevent highway drift.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: Separate the number two in Colorado's eye-specialist advice from its long-drive fatigue rule?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Keeping specialist checkups in years and highway segments in hours prevents mixing up two easy wellness questions.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: Why can even a driver with healthy ears miss sirens or horns outside the car?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Modern soundproofed cabins plus loud playlists or gradual age-related hearing loss easily drown out emergency sirens.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: How does Colorado define the earphones you are barred from wearing while driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Any headset or pair of buds covering all or part of both ears cuts off directional horn and siren awareness.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: Which five medical, helmet, or single-ear devices do not count as prohibited earphones?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Medical hearing devices, helmet speakers, and a one-ear wireless bud leave your hearing open to traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: Why does a wireless earpiece in one ear stay legal under Colorado's earphone ban?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Leaving one ear uncovered preserves outside traffic sound, putting single-ear buds alongside legal hearing aids.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: How can everyday aches or chronic medical conditions affect your driving, and whom should you ask when unsure?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: A stiff neck blocks shoulder checks while conditions like diabetes or epilepsy risk sudden blackouts behind the wheel.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: Which strong emotions can degrade your driving judgment, and what aggressive reaction must you never give in to?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Worry, fear, excitement, and anger tunnel your attention onto feelings instead of brake lights and crosswalks.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: What is the number-one cause of driver error, and how does the Colorado handbook define it?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: Even a one-second mental or visual detour off the road counts as distraction and sets up preventable mistakes.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: Which four sources of distraction does the handbook warn against—including rubbernecking—and how do you handle urgent tasks?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: Gawking at roadside scenes, juggling phones, or tending kids steals forward focus—park off-road first whenever something cannot wait.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: Who bears legal responsibility for vehicle upkeep, and what four consequences can poor maintenance bring?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: Neglecting basic upkeep inflates repair bills while risking roadside breakdowns, collisions, and equipment citations.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: What should you do immediately if your brakes feel off, and which four exterior light groups must work?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Spongy or grinding brakes never heal themselves, and dead brake, tail, turn, or head lamps leave other drivers guessing.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: Which four maintenance habits keep your windshield, wipers, washer tank, and side glass ready for clear vision?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Cracked glass, empty washer fluid, interior haze, or frosted side windows blind you when sun glare or snow hits.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: Which four driving hazards come from running worn or bald tires?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Shallow tread stretches braking distances, slips in corners, surfs atop rain puddles, and punctures far more easily.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: How do underinflated or unbalanced tires hurt your car, and which three warning signs call for a tire shop?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: Soft or out-of-balance wheels burn extra gas, chew tread fast, and telegraph trouble through vibrations or sideways tugs.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: What symptom calls for a mechanic to inspect your steering versus your suspension?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Stiff steering points to linkage or assist trouble, whereas repeated bobbing after bumps or stops signals worn shocks.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: How do you tell whether a bouncing car needs a tire check or a suspension check?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Pair wheel shimmy or sideways pulling with tire balance, and lingering porpoising after bumps or stops with suspension.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.question_text: Why must you never idle an engine inside a garage or sit in a running parked car with closed windows?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.teaching_text: Odorless carbon monoxide from a tiny exhaust leak builds lethal cabin concentrations within minutes in still air.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: Which five problems can an out-of-tune engine cause, and what warning device needs regular testing?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: An engine stalling mid-intersection leaves you stranded in cross traffic, and a dead horn robs your emergency voice.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: What adjustments, cabin cleanup, and buckle checks belong before shifting out of Park?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: Dialing in seat, mirrors, climate, and child restraints while parked keeps your eyes up once wheels roll.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: Where do you lean your head—and what should barely show—when aiming the driver-side mirror?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: Fanning the left mirror outward from the window glass erases huge blind spots that overlap your inside mirror.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: Where do you position your head when aiming the passenger-side mirror?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: Leaning above the center console until the right quarter panel barely shows sweeps wide right-lane blind zones clear.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: How does your head lean change between setting the left side mirror and the right side mirror?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Both setups push mirror aim outward past duplicate rear views—left from the door glass, right from cabin center.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: Why must you clear loose items off the rear shelf, back seat, and driver floorboard?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: Hard braking hurls back-shelf gear forward at highway speed while rolling bottles can wedge underneath your brake pedal.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.question_text: How close should your seat's head restraint sit behind your head?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.teaching_text: Eliminating the gap behind your skull catches your head early in a rear-end hit to prevent whiplash.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.question_text: Regardless of vehicle make or model, where does your right foot belong when starting the engine, and what do you scan next?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.teaching_text: Holding the brake prevents unexpected lurches on startup while checking dash lights catches oil or brake warnings early.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.question_text: What check-and-signal sequence precedes pulling out, and which parts of your foot work the gas?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.teaching_text: Pivoting on a planted heel lets the ball of your foot meter smooth, jerk-free acceleration into clear traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: How does your right foot's placement differ between starting the car and pressing the gas?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Keep your right foot anchored on the brake for ignition, then pivot from a floor-planted heel onto the gas.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.question_text: What three-step sequence brings your vehicle to a smooth, safe stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.teaching_text: Glancing in the mirror first spots close tailgaters so you can apply smooth, steady brake pressure.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.question_text: Which way do you turn the steering wheel to guide your car—forward or in reverse?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.teaching_text: Whether nosing into a spot or backing out a driveway, turning the wheel right moves the car right.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: Does backing up invert which direction you turn the steering wheel?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: Beginners often overthink reverse—want the rear bumper to swing left, turn the top of the wheel left.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.question_text: Which two clock-face hand placements on the outside of the wheel give optimal control in Colorado?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.teaching_text: Lower side grips stabilize your shoulders and keep your forearms clear of an inflating steering-wheel airbag.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: Why shouldn't you pick ten-and-two o'clock on a Colorado permit question about steering hand placement?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Modern airbag steering wheels retired old ten-and-two advice in favor of three-and-nine or four-and-eight.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.question_text: How should your fingers and thumbs rest on the steering wheel, and what rim grip must you avoid?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.teaching_text: Hooking thumbs or grabbing inside the rim risks broken wrists if a pothole or airbag snaps the spokes.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: Before climbing into the driver seat to back out, what outside check should you make and why?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Toddlers, pets, and low toys sit completely below rear window height where driver-seat sightlines miss them.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: Where do your brake foot, left hand, right arm, and eyes belong when backing straight back?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Bracing your right arm across the passenger backrest twists your torso cleanly to see directly out the rear glass.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: Why shouldn't a rearview camera replace mirrors and turning your head when reversing?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Dashboard screens miss cross-traffic cars and walkers approaching from rear corners outside the wide-angle lens.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: How fast should you reverse, where do you glance during a backing turn, and how long do you keep looking back?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Front fenders swing wide during reverse turns, needing quick side glances while keeping eyes rearward until wheels halt.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: Beyond lights, posts, and paint, which three people on the street legally direct traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Live instructions from an officer, work-zone flagger, or school crossing guard override normal signal cycles.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: From top to bottom, how are standard three-lens traffic lights arranged?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Consistent top-to-bottom placement lets color-blind drivers and snow-glare squinters read signal state instantly by position.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: How must every driver treat an intersection whose traffic lights have gone dark or malfunctioned?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Taking turns after a full stop at every leg prevents high-speed T-bone crashes during storm blackouts.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: When storm outages knock out a signal, does the wider multi-lane arterial keep priority over the side street?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Blowing through a dead signal just because your avenue is bigger is a classic crash and exam trap.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: What must you do at a steady red light, and what conditions allow turning right on red?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Rolling through without a complete stop first earns red-light citations and clips crosswalk walkers.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: Under what exact street layout—and after what steps—is turning left on a steady red light legal in Colorado?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Only turning from one one-way street into another avoids crossing opposing lanes on red—provided nothing bans it.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: Why is turning right on red common while turning left on red applies to far fewer corners?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Right turns hug the near curb anywhere unposted, whereas left on red demands two intersecting one-way streets.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: What does a steady round yellow light warn, and what action does it call for?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Yellow clears the box rather than inviting gas-pedal sprints—stop safely unless your car already entered.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: Before moving straight or turning on a steady green light, whom must you yield to?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: A fresh green never gives permission to hit pedestrians in adjacent crosswalks or cars finishing left turns.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: May you stop and make a turn in the direction of a lit steady red arrow?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Unlike a round red ball at unposted right turns, a red arrow bans turning in its pointed direction completely.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: What happens to your turn privilege when a green arrow clicks off while the round green ball stays lit?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Once protected arrow time ends without a red arrow or prohibition post, oncoming traffic and walkers gain priority.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: How does a green arrow turning off alongside a green ball differ from a red arrow lighting up?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: A dark arrow drops you to yield-and-turn mode on round green, whereas a red arrow locks the turn shut.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: What is about to appear after a steady yellow arrow, and what should you do?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Protected turn time is ending—brake before the line unless your front wheels are already inside the intersection.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: What does a flashing yellow left-turn arrow allow, and what two phases follow it?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Yield to oncoming cars and crosswalk walkers while flashing, then stop once solid yellow transitions into solid red.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: Which everyday roadside control matches the exact rule for a flashing red signal light?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Come to a complete halt, yield to walkers and cross traffic with priority, then proceed without waiting for green.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: After coming to a full stop, how does a steady red light differ from a flashing red light?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Waiting forever at a midnight blinking red backs up traffic because no green phase is coming.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: How should you respond when approaching a plain flashing yellow light?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Blinking amber beacons mark tricky curves, firehouse aprons, or busy crossings where lower speed buys reaction room.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: What separates the meaning of a plain flashing yellow light from a flashing yellow arrow?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Keep shape in mind—the round blinking beacon warns through traffic of hazards while the arrow governs permissive left turns.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: What does HAWK stand for, and what triggers its yellow-and-red sequence?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: High Intensity Activated Crosswalk beacons stay dark until a pedestrian pushes the button to halt roadway traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: Which five kinds of travel info do road signs convey, and why do their shapes and colors matter?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Even through snow crust or long distance, an octagon, pennant, or orange diamond reveals rules or hazards immediately.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: What colors mark regulatory signs, what do they communicate, and what happens if you ignore one?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Regulatory panels post enforceable statutes for speed, turns, and lanes—ignoring them earns traffic citations.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: What two speed bounds can speed-limit panels post, and when is driving at the posted maximum too fast?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Snow, glare, heavy traffic, or rain requires dropping below the white maximum panel to keep safe control.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: At what exact spot do you stop at a stop post when there is a stop line, only a crosswalk, or neither?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Halting before painted bars or crosswalks keeps pedestrians safe before you creep out if buildings block sight.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: What is the one-two-three fallback order for picking your stopping point at a stop post?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Never roll past a painted stop bar to stop at the curb—always honor whichever marker appears first.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: What two speed actions can a yield post require, and who goes first?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Approach ready to halt completely whenever pedestrians or cross-street vehicles hold the right-of-way.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: What critical mistake do Do Not Enter and Wrong Way panels catch, and what is the rule?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Entering an exit ramp or one-way street backward puts you nose-to-nose against fast oncoming traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: What rule does a One Way arrow panel set for every lane on that roadway?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Checking black-and-white One Way arrows before turning keeps you from turning against every lane of traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: How does the job of a One Way panel differ from Do Not Enter and Wrong Way panels?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: One Way arrows show cross-street drivers which way to turn, while red Wrong Way warnings stop head-on mistakes.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: Where are lane control panels mounted, and what do their curved or straight arrows dictate?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Matching overhead or curbside arrow panels—and matching asphalt paint—keeps straight-through cars out of turn-only pockets.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: What do prohibited-action panels communicate to drivers approaching an intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Spotting a crossed-out left turn or U-turn early lets you route around the next block legally.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: Which two background colors mark warning panels, and what kinds of upcoming hazards do they preview?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: Yellow diamonds preview curves, merges, and slick spots while bright fluorescent green highlights schools and pedestrian crossings.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: What does a yellow advisory speed plaque tell you approaching a curve, corner, or exit ramp?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: Exit ramps curl sharper than they look from freeway pace, and wet or icy asphalt demands slowing even lower.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: Which three rules—about racing, far-side space, and shifting gears—apply at every railroad crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: Shifting manual gears mid-crossing risks stalling right on the rails, and tight traffic ahead can trap your rear bumper.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.question_text: What two critical pieces of information appear on the blue Emergency Notification System plaque at every rail crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.teaching_text: Reading the exact DOT crossing number to the railroad dispatcher lets them halt approaching trains on the right line.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.question_text: What color combination marks work-zone panels, and what do they team up with to protect road crews?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.teaching_text: Orange panels pair with cones, barrels, and flaggers to guide cars safely past exposed highway crews.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.question_text: What background color marks guide panels, and what two travel details do they display?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.teaching_text: Green overhead and roadside boards tell you how many miles remain and which exit leads to your town.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.question_text: How do blue roadside panels differ in purpose from brown roadside panels?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.teaching_text: Blue points toward fuel, food, lodging, or hospitals, while brown marks campgrounds, trails, and historic landmarks.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: How do five background colors—yellow or fluorescent green, orange, green, blue, and brown—pair with their message types?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Memorizing all five color families turns every background-color question on the Colorado permit exam into free points.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: Which four highway systems can you tell apart just from the outline shape of a route marker?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Distinct shield, crest, and pentagon shapes tell you instantly what class of highway you are following.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: What colors appear on combined bicycle-and-pedestrian crossing panels, and what spot do they mark?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Shared multi-use paths send both fast cyclists and walkers across roadways at mid-block trail intersections.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: How much clearance must you give when passing any bicyclist in Colorado, and does a reminder panel need to be posted?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Colorado's three-foot passing buffer applies statewide on every road whether or not a white reminder panel stands nearby.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: Why does a white Bicycle May Use Full Lane panel remind drivers that cyclists sometimes ride mid-lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Broken pavement, car doors, or blind curves can make hugging the right gutter dangerous for two thin wheels.
sec06-card-sec06-F04.must_match_memory_hook: Hazards or sight make right unsafe

visual_sync.text_span: Hazards or sight make right unsafe

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: What design speed does a reflective orange triangle on the rear of a vehicle indicate?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Tractors and construction rigs wearing that glowing orange triangle top out under twenty-five miles per hour.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: Which vehicles are legally allowed to use stalls marked with disabled parking posts and pavement symbols?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Accessible stalls keep wide, close building entry open strictly for vehicles displaying a valid permit.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: What is the painted crosshatched zone beside a disabled parking stall used for, and when may someone park on it?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Side-lift wheelchair vans need every inch of those diagonal stripes clear to deploy ramps and load safely.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: Does hanging a valid disabled placard on your mirror allow parking on the striped van-access crosshatch?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Blocking the striped aisle traps the neighboring wheelchair van's lift shut even when both cars hold valid placards.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: When driving a car that has a disabled placard or plate, what must be true for you to park in an accessible stall?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: A placard belongs to the person rather than the car—running solo errands while the holder stays home is illegal.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: What charge, fine range, and extra penalties hit if you park in a disabled stall without a placard or plate?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Colorado treats accessible-stall abuse as a criminal misdemeanor carrying steep fines plus possible jail, license loss, or impoundment.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: What four penalties apply in Colorado if you use someone else's disabled placard or plate to park?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Misusing another person's permit triggers twice the standard fine ceiling alongside towing, jail exposure, and lost privileges.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: How does Colorado punish parking with a borrowed placard compared with parking with no placard at all?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Deliberately misusing someone else's credential draws harsher punishment—doubling the financial hit plus towing, jail, and license loss.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: Which five traffic-guiding jobs do painted lines and symbols handle on the pavement?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Asphalt paint works nonstop beside signs to separate lanes, govern passing, mark turns and crosswalks, and show stop bars.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: What traffic flows do yellow lines divide, and what does a single broken yellow line permit?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Dashed yellow paint marks a two-way road with enough sightline to pass when the oncoming lane is clear.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: What does a single or double solid yellow line prohibit, and what special overtaking exception applies?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Colorado explicitly allows crossing solid yellow paint to give a bicyclist three feet once oncoming lanes are completely clear.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: When a solid yellow stripe runs beside a broken yellow stripe, when may you pass and when must you finish?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Only drivers with dashes on their side may overtake, tucking back right before their dashed line turns solid.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: In a mixed pair of center yellow stripes, which of the two lines governs your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Ignore the far stripe meant for opposing cars—dashes next to your left tire allow safe passing, solid forbids it.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: Which two everyday maneuvers legally let you cross a solid yellow centerline when oncoming traffic is clear?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Solid yellow bans overtaking faster cars without trapping you out of driveways, alleys, private roads, or wide bike passes.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: Why isn't 'never cross solid yellow for any reason' a true statement under Colorado rules?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Watch out for absolute-sounding wrong answers—turning into private drives or giving cyclists three feet is legal when safe.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: Which traffic direction do white lines divide, and how does broken white differ from solid white?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Broken white dashes welcome safe lane changes, while solid white bars lane weaving and marks the right shoulder edge.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: How does glancing at lane-line color tell you immediately which way adjacent traffic is moving?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Even on unfamiliar downtown streets, white to your left confirms a one-way flow while yellow warns of oncoming headlights.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: What does bright green pavement paint designate on a city street?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Green lane blocks highlight bike-only zones at busy merges and corners so turning motorists spot riders early.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: What do painted sharrows warn drivers about lane width, and where may cyclists ride there?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Shared-lane bike-and-chevron stencils show cars cannot squeeze beside a rider safely inside that single narrow lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way inside painted or unpainted crosswalks, and what must approaching drivers do?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Unmarked corner extensions carry the exact same legal duty to slow or stop for crossing walkers as zebra stripes.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: When a car ahead stops at a crosswalk, what is prohibited and where must you stop on a multi-lane street?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Passing a stopped adjacent car blindsides pedestrians stepping out from in front of its hood.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: What do broken lines called conflict zones along a bike lane or bus lane warn about?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Solid restricted stripes switch to dashes right where turning cars and straight-through cyclists or buses intersect.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: Which side of the roadway—and how many lanes—should your vehicle occupy in normal driving?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Staying on the right half inside one lane prevents sideswipes and head-on conflicts.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: How do you position your car and handle turns or passes on an unmarked roadway with zero lane stripes?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: Treat the imaginary middle like a centerline—stay off soft shoulders and follow normal passing and turn laws.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: What are restricted lanes, and what common painted pavement emblem marks them?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: White diamonds and roadside panels set lanes aside for buses, carpools, or bicycles during posted hours.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way inside a bike lane, and which four car actions are banned there?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Pulling into a bike lane 'just for a minute' forces unprotected cyclists out into fast motor traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: When bike-lane stripes pause across the middle of an intersection, does the bike lane end there?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Turning motorists must still yield to through cyclists even where cross-street asphalt lacks connecting bike lines.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: Which vehicles are transit lanes primarily built for, and can regular cars ever touch them?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Dedicated bus and rail lanes keep mass transit on schedule, allowing regular cars only where markings allow right turns.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: How are High Occupancy Vehicle lanes marked on pavement, and how do you know if your car qualifies?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Posted HOV panels specify exact passenger headcounts, hours, and eligible low-emission or toll vehicles.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: Why must you read the accompanying roadside panel whenever you spot a white diamond painted in a lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: A white diamond could mean two-plus carpools, three-plus carpools, buses only, or bicycles—only the panel clarifies.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: What is a two-way center left-turn lane strictly used for, and what two misuses are illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Using the shared center lane as a passing strip or merge runway risks head-on collisions with opposing left turners.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: On a street equipped with a shared center turn lane, from which lane must every left turn be made?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Stopping inside a through lane to turn left beside an empty center turn pocket is illegal and invites rear-end hits.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: What two strict rules govern a shared center left-turn lane—both inside it and beside it?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: You cannot drive along or pass inside it, and you cannot skip it to turn left from regular through lanes.
sec06-card-sec06-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Never cruise inside, always turn from

visual_sync.text_span: Never cruise inside, always turn from

sec06-card-sec06-F35.question_text: How do reversible lanes work across the day, and what yellow line pattern sets them apart?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.teaching_text: Inbound morning lanes switch outbound for evening commutes, bordered by barriers or double dashed yellow lines and overhead lights.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: How do double broken yellow lines differ in meaning from a shared center left-turn lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Exam questions love mixing these two center lanes—solid-outside broken-inside marks left turns, whereas double broken marks reversible flow.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.question_text: How does a diverging diamond interchange move traffic onto freeway ramps without left-turn conflicts?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.teaching_text: Temporarily crossing traffic to the opposite side across the bridge lets left-bound ramp drivers peel off uninterrupted.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.question_text: Which side of the center island do you pass on in a roundabout, and who yields at the entrance?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.teaching_text: Keeping right of the central island sends traffic counterclockwise while entering cars wait for vehicles already circling.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.question_text: Which four large vehicles get special statutory yield priority in Colorado roundabouts, and what happens when two meet?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.teaching_text: Colorado law gives trucks, buses, emergency units, and RVs space to straddle lanes—and between two giants, right yields left.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.question_text: When no large trucks or buses are around, whom do you yield to entering a roundabout and when do you stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.teaching_text: Scanning left lets you roll smoothly into open gaps without unnecessary full stops that surprise trailing cars.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.question_text: Whom must you yield to when entering or leaving a roundabout, and when do you use turn signals?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.teaching_text: Splitter-island crosswalks guard both entry and exit legs, and signaling lane changes or exits keeps flow predictable.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: What are the three priority layers to watch every time you use a Colorado roundabout?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Put Colorado's big-vehicle statute on top, circulating left cars second, and crosswalk walkers or cyclists at every leg.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: What do right-of-way rules settle when drivers or walkers meet without traffic lights or posts?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Shared priority rules stop hesitation standoffs and simultaneous pull-outs at quiet neighborhood corners.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: Does Colorado law ever grant someone automatic right-of-way—even when facing a green light?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Permit questions love testing that statutes only name who must yield and never hand anyone a license to collide.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: Whom must you let clear first whenever you roll up toward an intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Charging into a box before slower walkers, cyclists, or turning cars finish clearing causes preventable side impacts.
