sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: Why must you hold back on a brand-new green light if someone is still crossing the box?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Anyone already inside the intersection holds priority to clear before stopped green-phase traffic accelerates.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: Regardless of who broke a yielding rule, who stays responsible for preventing a collision?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Insisting on your turn instead of tapping the brakes turns someone else's mistake into a wreck you could have dodged.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: Where do walkers hold priority over cars, and what braking action must you take for them?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Swerving around a pedestrian instead of halting completely hides them from cars in the next lane over.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: Which three pedestrian groups need extra patience, and what dangerous assumption must you avoid?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Quiet electric drivetrains, earbuds, or vision limits mean kids, seniors, and disabled walkers may never detect your approach.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: What two visual cues usually show that a pedestrian is blind or deaf-blind?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Honking or waving hand gestures at a traveler with a white cane or harness dog can startle or disorient them.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: How do a cyclist's legal rights and duties shift between riding on asphalt versus using a sidewalk or crosswalk?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Knowing riders switch from vehicle rules in traffic lanes to pedestrian protections on crosswalks clarifies every corner yield.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: Where does Colorado law treat someone on a bicycle like a pedestrian rather than a vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Turning drivers must scan sidewalks far back because a rolling rider enters a crosswalk much faster than someone walking.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: What is your yielding duty whenever you merge into or turn across a marked bike lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Whipping right across a bike lane without a right-shoulder check causes classic right-hook crashes with straight-moving cyclists.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: Who moves first at a four-way stop, and how do two simultaneous arrivals break the tie?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Waving people out of legal turn order confuses the other two corners and triggers awkward mid-box lurches.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: What defines an uncontrolled intersection, and which car goes first when two reach it together?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Ease off the gas at residential corners lacking posts so you can yield cleanly if a car approaches from your right.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: What exact tie-breaker rule connects four-way stops and uncontrolled intersections?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Memorizing one left-yields-to-right rule covers every simultaneous corner arrival on the Colorado exam.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: Besides crosswalk walkers, which slim oncoming riders need careful speed-and-distance checks before a left turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Narrow single-headlight profiles look farther away and slower than wide cars, tricking left turners into pulling out.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: In what sole two intersection situations does a left-turning driver not yield to oncoming traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Outside a protected green arrow or arriving first at an all-way stop, turning left always waits on straight traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: How does a diverging diamond interchange make highway ramp turns safer?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Shifting traffic briefly to the left side lets ramp turners peel onto the freeway without crossing oncoming lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: Whom must you yield to when changing lanes or passing, and what brake test tells you the gap is too tight?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: If moving over makes a driver in that lane tap brakes or lift off the gas, you cut them off.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: Who holds priority when you merge onto a roadway, and when must you hold off merging?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Matching mainline speed before blending in keeps through-drivers from slamming brakes in fast traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: Which vehicles hold priority over you whenever your car is moving in reverse?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Drivers cruising down a street or parking aisle never expect a bumper backing out into their path.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: When two vehicles meet on a steep Colorado road too narrow to pass, which driver normally backs or yields, and when does that flip?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Backing uphill gives the descending driver better brake and gravity control than forcing an uphill car to reverse toward a drop-off.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: Between an uphill car and a downhill car on a single-lane mountain grade, who normally gives way?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Out-of-state visitors often guess backwards on mountain right-of-way, making downhill-yields a prime Colorado exam favorite.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: What warning sounds or four strobe colors require pulling right and stopping for an approaching emergency vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Clearing toward the right curb opens a predictable center corridor for ambulances, fire rigs, and patrol cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: If sirens and flashing lights close in while your car is already inside an intersection, what must you do?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Freezing mid-box corks up the exact turning lanes the fire truck or ambulance needs to get through.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: What is your first choice—and your backup move—when passing a stopped emergency vehicle along the shoulder?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: One open buffer lane shields troopers, paramedics, and tow operators working inches from highway mirrors.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: How does your legal duty change between an emergency vehicle closing from behind versus one parked on the shoulder?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Stopping dead in a live freeway lane beside a parked trooper invites a high-speed rear-end pileup.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: When traffic blocks you from vacating the lane beside a stopped responder, what exact speed drops apply at forty-five and below versus above forty-five?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Colorado sets hard numbers rather than vague slowdowns—twenty-five on slower roads and twenty under on faster highways.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: How does the forty-five-mile-per-hour posted limit split Colorado's move-over slowdown numbers?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: On a sixty-five-mile-per-hour interstate you drop to forty-five, whereas on a thirty-five arterial you drop to twenty-five.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: What two flashing light colors mark working service and maintenance trucks, and how must you treat them?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Road maintenance trucks stop, back, and swing wide unpredictably while patching asphalt or clearing drains.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: How does the light bar on a maintenance truck differ from the lights and sound on an emergency vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Spotting yellow-and-blue strobes warns you of slow utility or plow equipment ahead rather than a high-speed siren run.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: Why are working snowplows tough to see, and what passing move around diagonal plow formations is illegal?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Weaving between staggered plows drives blind into whiteout snow clouds and heavy steel wing blades.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: What two adjustments protect road crews and fellow drivers inside a construction zone?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Edging away from cone lines and dropping speed buys crucial inches next to workers on foot.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: At least how many feet away must you halt for a school bus flashing red lights, and when may you move?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Twenty feet creates a visible safety zone around the front bumper where small children cross below driver sightlines.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: Which approaching directions must stop for a flashing red school bus, and what sole roadway feature excuses opposite lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Painted center turn lanes never count as a barrier—opposite lanes must still halt twenty feet out.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: When a school bus flashes red across a multi-lane road, what is the sole separator that lets oncoming cars keep moving?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Permit tests love laying a five-lane painted turn-lane trap where every single lane in both directions must stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: Once a school bus switches off its flashing red lights, what check comes before touching the gas?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Kids who drop a backpack or dart back across at the last second ignore whether the overhead lamps stopped.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: When does Colorado law require yielding to a public transit bus pulling back out from the curb?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Colorado equips transit coaches with a rear electronic yield display that gives them legal merge priority back into traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: How should you pace your vehicle and focus your attention inside a construction zone?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Construction lanes shift without shoulders, where abrupt stops or equipment entries punish distracted tailgaters.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: What happens to posted speed limits and speeding ticket amounts inside Colorado work zones?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Speeding past clearly posted orange-zone reductions hits your wallet twice as hard while endangering exposed crews.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: What single factor drives crash severity more than any other on Colorado highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Kinetic impact force multiplies rapidly with velocity, turning survivable fender-benders into fatal highway wrecks.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: What weather do posted speed caps assume, and when does driving below a posted freeway minimum draw a ticket?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Crawling below a freeway minimum in clear weather creates dangerous closing-speed ambushes for seventy-five-mile-per-hour traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: Under what condition is driving slower than a posted minimum speed limit illegal versus legal?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Blizzards or gridlock justify dropping below the minimum, whereas creeping along dry sunny lanes violates the statute.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: Around what six hazards must you drop speed, and why is creeping way below normal flow dangerous?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Huge speed gaps in dry, clear lanes trigger frustrated passing waves and rear-end collisions.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: Even inside a marked reduced-speed zone, can safe driving require going slower than the sign?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Ice, glare, or crowded crosswalks override the metal number on the post every single time.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: When no speed post appears, what is Colorado's default limit on blind curves and narrow, winding mountain highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Hairpin canyon bends hide oncoming rigs and rockfall inside short sightlines that demand twenty miles per hour.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: With no sign posted, what default Colorado limits govern open mountain highways and commercial trash-hauling trucks?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Colorado's statutory forty-five-mile-per-hour cap on trash haulers is a unique handbook number test writers love asking.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: How do Colorado's two unposted mountain highway speed limits split between tight switchbacks and open stretches?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Doubling from twenty on blind narrow switchbacks to forty on open mountain grades rewards reading the road width accurately.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: When unposted, what default speed limits apply in Colorado business districts versus residential neighborhoods?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Dense storefront foot traffic and angled parking doors keep business districts five miles per hour slower than home streets.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: Many states set residential streets slower, so how do Colorado's twenty-five and thirty default limits pair up?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Guessing twenty-five for neighborhoods is the single biggest default-speed trap on the Colorado permit test.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: What default limits apply on Colorado urban highways versus designated rural interstates, and who can lower local limits?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Cities and towns can pass local speed ordinances, so watch city-limit posts carefully as rural highways enter town.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: How is total stopping distance defined, and which four factors add together to determine it?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Your car rolls dozens of feet while your eyes recognize danger and your foot moves before brake pads ever touch.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: How does keeping generous space behind traffic ahead make slowing or stopping safer?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Seeing three cars ahead brake lets you feather off the gas gently instead of spiking your brakes.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: What two driver mistakes cause most sudden stops, and what three bad outcomes follow hard panic braking?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Locking up late either slides your own tires sideways or invites the driver behind you straight into your trunk.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: Under ideal conditions, roughly how many feet does a light passenger car need to stop from fifty-five miles per hour?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Two hundred feet stretches past half a football field in dry sunshine—and heavy trucks or wet roads stretch far longer.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: What four steps from early blinker to exit throttle make up a textbook proper turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Dawdling after completing the corner surprises through-traffic behind you just as much as turning without a blinker.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: Is skipping your turn signal an actual traffic violation, and before which four maneuvers must it flash?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Pulling away from a curb or turning into a shopping plaza without blinking blindsides cyclists and trailing cars.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: How many continuous feet must your blinker run in urban zones versus four-lane highways posted above forty?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Faster multi-lane corridors cover one hundred feet in barely a blink, so doubling to two hundred gives real notice.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: Since judging exact footage on asphalt is tough, what everyday seconds rule guides pre-move signaling?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Counting three full flashes before moving your steering wheel gives surrounding eyes time to register the amber bulb.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: How do Colorado's urban footage, fast four-lane footage, and time rule of thumb fit together for signaling?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Knowing all three numbers guarantees points whether the exam asks city distance, highway distance, or seconds.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: What must you use if your electric blinkers burn out, and what do you do right before turning the wheel?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Bringing your left hand back inside before steering gives you full two-handed control through the corner.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: Where inside your lane do you set up for a right turn versus a left turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Tucking close to the right curb blocks impatient scooters or bikes from squeezing inside your right turn.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: How can you tell when turning from more than one parallel lane is legal at a busy junction?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Never invent a second turn lane on your own unless arrows or overhead signs explicitly mark dual turns.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: In which lane of the cross street should your car finish a standard turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Swinging directly into the far lane cuts across cars turning legally from the opposite approach.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: What painted guides steer multi-lane turns, and what four steering mistakes must you avoid?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Cutting inside or drifting wide across dotted turn guides sideswipes the vehicle turning centimeters from your mirror.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: In Colorado, where exact spot should you hold while waiting for a safe oncoming gap to turn left?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Colorado specifically teaches waiting behind the stop bar or crosswalk until a gap big enough to clear completely opens.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: What three hazards arise if you creep out into the middle of the intersection while waiting to turn left?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Stranding yourself mid-box leaves you exposed to late red-light runners when the signal flips.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: Why must your front tires stay pointed straight ahead while waiting to turn left?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: A distracted tap on your rear bumper pushes straight wheels harmlessly forward instead of sideways into sixty-mile-per-hour traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: What two habits combine for the safest possible left-turn wait in Colorado?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Pairing stop-bar patience with straight front wheels eliminates both mid-box stranding and head-on rear-end shoves.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: Where are U-turns illegal, and what safer alternative should you pick instead?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Even without a No U-turn sign, hills, curves, or heavy traffic make circling the next intersection far safer.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: What off-street spaces let you perform a two-point turnabout when circling the block will not work?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Tucking into an alley or driveway keeps you from swinging sideways across both lanes in a slow three-point block.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: Why is backing into a right-side driveway first—then signaling left forward—the preferred reverse two-point sequence?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: Backing off the road into an empty driveway lets you re-enter live traffic nose-first with clean windshield sightlines.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: How do you execute a forward two-point turnabout using a left-side driveway and backing right?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: Stop once your rear bumper clears the curb, signal right, and back slowly into the nearest lane before pulling ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: Under what strict road and routing conditions is a three-point turnabout justified?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Stopping perpendicular across an entire road exposes both doors, so save three-point turnarounds strictly as a last resort.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: How do you stop, signal early, check blind spots, and cut across to begin a three-point turnabout?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Signaling left for three seconds or two hundred feet after pulling right warns trailing cars before you swing across.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: How do you reverse across, pull forward into your new lane, and check your stalk to finish a three-point turnabout?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: Confirming your blinker clicked off once straightened prevents misleading drivers down the road in your new direction.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: What goal unites U-turns, two-point turnabouts, and three-point turnabouts, and which one sits last in priority?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Examiners reward picking circling the block, a clean U-turn, or a driveway two-point before blocking both lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.question_text: What gear, brake, and key habits secure automatic and manual vehicles when parked on uphill or downhill slopes?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.teaching_text: Using low gear uphill and reverse downhill locks manual engine compression against whichever way gravity tugs.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: How does securing a manual transmission uphill versus downhill differ from parking an automatic?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Leaving a stick-shift in neutral trusts a single cable brake on steep Colorado grades—always match opposing gear.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.question_text: Including runaway truck ramps, bridges, tunnels, tracks, and bike lanes, where is parking flatly prohibited?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.teaching_text: Stopping inside a runaway truck gravel bed in Colorado mountains puts your parked car directly in front of brake-failed semis.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.question_text: How many feet of clear curb must you leave near a stop post, signal, or rail crossing versus a fire hydrant?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.teaching_text: Thirty feet keeps corner traffic controls visible to approaching drivers while fifteen feet clears heavy fire-hose couplings.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: How do Colorado's thirty-foot and fifteen-foot no-parking buffers divide up roadside fixtures?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Pairing signals, stop posts, and rail crossings at thirty feet isolates fire hydrants cleanly at half that distance.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.question_text: What three steering cuts move you from beside the front car into the middle of a parallel parking space?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.teaching_text: Smooth S-curve steering tucks both tires near the curb without bumping bumpers ahead or behind.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.question_text: What three-step safety check is required before pulling out of a parallel parking spot into live traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.teaching_text: Parked cars hold zero right-of-way over approaching bikes or cars, so wait until the travel lane is completely clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: Within how many inches of the curb—or where on curbless shoulders—must you parallel park?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Leaving wide gaps pushes your driver-side doors and mirrors out into passing lanes and cyclists.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: Which way do your front wheels point when parked downhill beside a curb, and how do you set the tire?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Letting the front tire kiss the concrete chocks the vehicle immediately before momentum can build.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: Which way do your front wheels point when parked uphill beside a curb, and how does the tire catch?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Easing back until the rear of your front tire touches concrete anchors the car away from live lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: With no curb present, which way must your front wheels turn whether facing uphill or downhill, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Aiming right ensures a brake failure rolls your car off the shoulder instead of drifting across fast highway lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: How do the three hill-parking wheel directions line up across downhill curb, uphill curb, and no curb?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Grouping uphill-curb as the sole left-pointing setup keeps all three slope rules effortless under test pressure.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: What makes freeways inherently hazardous, and what mental habit must stay active there?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: At seventy miles per hour your car covers over one hundred feet every second, leaving zero margin for zoning out.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: What two traffic advantages are controlled-access freeways engineered to deliver over surface streets?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Eliminating traffic signals, driveways, and cross streets lets large traffic volumes flow smoothly when drivers merge cleanly.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: What is your main throttle job along a freeway acceleration ramp?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Entering seventy-mile-per-hour traffic at forty forces mainline semis and cars to slam brakes or swerve left.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: What four-step routine blends you cleanly from a side entrance ramp onto the freeway?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Picking your target gap early on the ramp lets you adjust throttle smoothly into that pocket.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: What painted ramp line must end before you merge, why avoid stopping, and who holds priority?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Cutting across the solid white gore stripe jumps prematurely into blind spots while freeway traffic holds right-of-way.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: How do you handle an entrance ramp controlled by an active ramp-metering signal?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Spacing incoming cars one green pulse at a time prevents clumps of mergers from choking mainline traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: Why is stopping on a normal acceleration lane a last resort, yet mandatory on a metered ramp?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Dead stops at the end of an open merge lane leave zero runway to rebuild freeway speed.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: Which freeway lane belongs to you whenever you are traveling slower than surrounding traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Camping slowly in center or left lanes forces faster traffic into risky right-side passes around you.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: For what three specific uses is the leftmost freeway lane reserved?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Treating the far-left passing lane like a casual cruise strip clogs highway flow and draws Colorado keep-right tickets.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: How do the rightmost and leftmost freeway lanes split duties by speed and maneuver?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Sorting traffic slowest-right to passing-left keeps speed differences predictable across multi-lane interstates.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: When cruising in the right freeway lane toward an upcoming on-ramp, what courteous move helps incoming drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Stepping into an open center lane clears the right lane completely for accelerating ramp cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: What directions, hidden zones, and overhead aids should guide your awareness while cruising a freeway?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Reading advance exit boards miles early prevents frantic last-second lane dives across fast traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: What blinker distance, weaving restraint, and median rule govern freeway lane changes?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Cutting across unpaved medians or gore islands blows tires and sends dirt-skidding cars head-on into opposing lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: How early do you signal for an exit lane, and at what exact point do you start braking?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Holding freeway speed until your tires enter the deceleration lane protects you from rear-end freeway impacts.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: Why must your braking wait until you have entered the deceleration lane rather than starting on the mainline?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Shedding thirty miles per hour in a live freeway lane catches seventy-five-mile-per-hour traffic behind you off guard.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: What three mistakes must you avoid when leaving a freeway onto an exit ramp?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Tight curved exit ramps flip fast vehicles that ignore yellow advisory ramp speeds after cruising seventy-five.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: Which four everyday maneuvers count legally as a lane change and demand full three-way checks?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Pulling away from a curb or blending off an on-ramp crosses lateral paths with the exact same crash risk.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: Where exact spot around your car sits a blind spot, and why do mirrors miss it?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Even wide-angle side glass leaves diagonal pockets beside your rear fenders where motorcycles and compacts disappear.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: Why is glancing at inside and outside mirrors never sufficient by itself before moving laterally?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: One quick chin glance over your shoulder spots the car pacing silently beside your rear quarter panel.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: What five-step sequence takes you safely from signaling to sliding into an adjacent lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Checking ahead first ensures traffic in front does not brake hard during the half-second you glance sideways.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: Once centered in your new lane, what mirror check and exact blinker cutoff finish the move?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Leaving a blinker ticking past three seconds misleads drivers into thinking another lane jump or turn is coming.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: How do the pre-move blinker minimum and post-move blinker shutoff frame every lane change?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Pairing three seconds or two hundred feet ahead with a three-second shutoff is a crisp Colorado test favorite.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: What roadway cues govern passing zones, and on which side does normal overtaking happen?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Left-side passing gives the overtaking driver a much clearer sightline down the center of the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: On which two multi-lane road layouts is passing on the right legal, and what shoulder move is banned?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Unlike states that allow paved-shoulder passes, Colorado strictly forbids driving off pavement or onto shoulders to pass.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: How does Colorado separate legal right-side overtaking from illegal shoulder bypassing?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Passing on a gravel or paved shoulder in Colorado draws an instant ticket and risks striking stopped cars or cyclists.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: Before overtaking any road user—including a cyclist—what must you evaluate ahead, beside, and behind?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Checking behind stops you from pulling left right as a faster car behind you has already started passing.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: How many vehicles should you commit to overtaking in a single passing move?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Counting on squeezing back between bunched cars fails fast when gaps close and an oncoming car appears.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: While completing a pass, what exact image in your inside rearview mirror signals safe clearance to return right?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Waiting until both front headlights show inside the center mirror ensures you never clip the passed bumper.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: At least how far from any oncoming vehicle—or oncoming cyclist—must you be tucked back into your right lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Remember that an oncoming cyclist on the opposite lane or shoulder counts identically to an oncoming truck.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: How does a solid yellow stripe starting ahead restrict starting a two-lane pass?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Crossing back right after no-passing paint begins means you lingered inside a blind hill or curve zone.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: What rear-mirror sight and forward-paint boundary together mark a textbook completed pass?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Cutting in before seeing both lamps crowds behind you, while running past solid yellow crowds blind oncoming road.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: What minimum side clearance must separate a cyclist from the widest sticking-out part of your rig?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Measuring from wide tow mirrors or trailer fenders—not your car door—prevents clipping handlebars as you pass.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: When does Colorado law allow briefly crossing a solid yellow center line to give a cyclist room?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Colorado explicitly legalizes straddling solid yellow on clear sightlines so drivers never squeeze cyclists inside three feet.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: Under what three road, vehicle, or weather conditions should you widen your buffer beyond three feet around cyclists?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Air wake from a tall rig, truck, or crosswind shoves light road bikes sideways toward gravel shoulders.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: Where do blind hills, curves, crossings, and structures make passing illegal in Colorado?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Pulling into the oncoming lane blind—or inside one hundred feet of crossings or sight-blocked structures—invites head-on collisions.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: Within what distance of an intersection or railroad crossing—and on which sight-limited features—is passing illegal?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Cars turning from cross streets or trains on tracks leave zero escape room inside one hundred feet.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: What single distance links Colorado's no-passing rule at intersections and rail crossings with sight-blocked bridges, viaducts, and tunnels?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Anchor one hundred feet across intersections, rail tracks, and sight-blocked bridges, viaducts, or tunnels alike.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: What side clearance—including mirrors—must you keep when passing a bicyclist, and when may you touch a solid yellow line?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Measure at least three feet from your widest mirror, crossing solid yellow briefly only with clear, empty sightlines.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: Even on an open road, which two passing actions break Colorado law every time?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Passing never grants extra speed allowance, and marked no-passing zones forbid overtaking regardless of empty pavement.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: May you ever pass a school bus displaying flashing red lights and an extended stop arm?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Extended stop arms and flashing red lamps protect boarding students crossing lanes right beside the bus.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: Why must you stay ready to stop at sight-blocking hills and curves even on routes you drive daily?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Knowing every bend by heart never tells you whether a stalled car or deer sits just beyond view.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: How should you manage your speed when approaching a hilltop you cannot see beyond?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Dropping to a safe pace before the crest gives you room to stop once the downhill lane appears.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: Why must you reduce speed before entering a curve, and at what point may you begin accelerating?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Carrying excess speed into a bend breaks tire traction into a skid, so hold throttle until past midway.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: Contrast your pedal timing at curve entry versus past the midpoint of the curve?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Adding gas while turning in unloads front grip, whereas gentle throttle past the apex stabilizes your exit.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: Which three visibility and lighting factors can make dawn and dusk riskier than midday driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Flat twilight shadows shrink sightlines while narrow headlamp pools and combined headlight-plus-fog glare strain your eyes.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: When does Colorado law mandate headlights, and what daytime lighting habit lowers crash risk?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Turn headlights on overnight or below one thousand feet visibility, and run low beams or DRLs anytime.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: When must a roadside-parked vehicle display parking lights, and what driving use is forbidden?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Parking lamps mark stationary shoulder cars in darkness or poor visibility, yet never illuminate lanes for moving vehicles.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: Contrast the legal purpose of parking lights at night against rolling down the street with only parking lights lit?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Use parking lamps strictly on parked roadside cars at night and switch full headlights on before rolling.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: Under which two conditions—lighting and route familiarity—should you stretch out your following distance?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Darkness and unfamiliar curves delay hazard recognition, demanding extra following cushion behind the taillights ahead.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: What unlit users, dark-zone movers, and single-lamp clues should you scan for after dark?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Slow through dark stretches for walkers or wildlife, watch for unlit bikes, and read single beams as two-wheelers.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: On which types of roadways should you use your high-beam headlights?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Away from city streetlights and traffic, high beams extend forward sightlines down dark rural stretches.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: Before reaching what distance from an approaching vehicle must you dim high beams or low-plus-fog lights?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Switching off brights and fog glare outside five hundred feet keeps oncoming drivers from losing night vision.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: Within what distance behind another vehicle must you switch to low beams and shut off fog lights?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: High beams or fog lamps inside two hundred feet bounce blinding glare off the lead driver's mirrors.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: Match Colorado's three key headlight distances—one thousand, five hundred, and two hundred feet—to each situation?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Pair one thousand with poor visibility, five hundred with meeting oncoming cars, and two hundred with following behind.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes to stay centered when oncoming headlights glare toward you?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Looking down toward the right pavement edge line preserves dark adaptation until the glaring vehicle passes.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: Which lights work best in nighttime fog, and why do high beams make visibility worse?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Suspended water droplets reflect upward-angled high beams right back into your eyes like a mirror.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: Contrast the driving setting where high beams shine against the weather condition where they backfire?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Save high beams for clear rural highways and drop immediately to lows or fog lamps when mist rolls in.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: Regardless of drivetrain, which two driving adjustments are essential in rain, fog, ice, high wind, or blowing dust?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Every drivetrain loses grip and visibility in foul weather, making lower speed and wider following gaps non-negotiable.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: Does driving a four-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive SUV let you skip slowing down and widening gaps in storms?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Powering all four wheels never shortens slick stopping distances or clears storm glare ahead.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: How should you set your headlights in poor storm visibility and your cruise control on wet or icy pavement?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Active cruise control can spin tires unexpectedly when hitting slick patches, while headlights help others spot you.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: How should you respond to large pools of standing water or a flooded roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Floodwater hides washed-out pavement, stalls engines, and floats cars away, so turn around for another route.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: How does the Colorado handbook rate the hazard level of snow, packed snow, and ice on roadways?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Fresh snow, hardpack, and glare ice slash tire friction dramatically, turning routine braking and turns into slides.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: What happens beneath your tires during hydroplaning, and what tire condition raises the danger?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Shallow, worn tire grooves cannot channel rain fast enough, floating rubber on water without steering or grip.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: Which pedal and steering inputs bring your vehicle back under control if hydroplaning begins?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Easing off throttle slows wheel spin while gentle steering with the slide realigns front tires as grip returns.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: Which abrupt steering or pedal reactions must you avoid while hydroplaning, and why?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Wrenching the wheel can roll the car when tires suddenly catch dry grip, and braking locks floating wheels.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: During a hydroplane, contrast the right steering direction and foot move against the wrong instincts?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Fight the urge to yank away or stomp brakes by guiding gently with the slide while lifting off throttle.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: At what stage are snow and ice slickest, and how do slippery surfaces change tire grip and stopping?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: A thin film of meltwater atop ice acts like grease, slashing tire friction and stretching braking room.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: Which four roadway locations can stay icy even when surrounding lanes look dry and clear?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Cold air circulating under bridges and overpasses or lingering inside tree and canyon shade keeps hidden ice frozen.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: Why shouldn't clear, dry-looking winter pavement trick you into letting your guard down?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Sun-warmed asphalt melts first while bridges, overpasses, and shaded bends right ahead remain sheeted in ice.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: What winter benefit does four-wheel drive deliver, and how does its stopping distance compare with a regular car's?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Four-wheel drive helps launch on snowy hills, yet all cars brake on four tires across identical ice.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: Separate what four-wheel drive adds on winter roads from the physics it cannot improve?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Confusing strong snow acceleration with stronger braking leads four-wheel-drive drivers to carry dangerous speed into stops.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: Which winter tire setups help or may be mandated on Colorado highways, and can they still slip?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Healthy tread, winter tires, and required highway chains boost winter grip, though slick glare ice still slides.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: How must your vehicle's braking system be maintained and adjusted ahead of slick driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Uneven brake pull grabs one corner harder on slick pavement and spins the vehicle sideways.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: When traction breaks into a skid, what is the baseline pedal and steering response?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Releasing both pedals restores rolling tire grip while pointing the front wheels guides recovery down your lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: In a vehicle equipped with anti-lock brakes, how do you respond if a skid starts?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Anti-lock sensors pulse brake pressure faster than human feet, letting you brake firmly while steering your line.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: Which braking technique applies on slippery roads or skids when your car lacks anti-lock brakes?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Squeezing the pedal right up to—without crossing—wheel lockup preserves maximum stopping force and steering control.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: Between threshold braking and anti-lock braking technique, which works in every car and which requires ABS?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Pressing hard through a skid locks wheels solid without ABS hardware, whereas threshold modulation works in any car.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: Contrast your brake-pedal action during a skid in an ABS-equipped car versus a car without ABS?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Know your car's brakes beforehand so you press and steer with ABS or modulate threshold pressure without it.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: How does the handbook's general skid rule differ on the pedals from its anti-lock skid rule, and what stays identical?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: General skid recovery lifts off both pedals whereas ABS presses brake, while both steer where you want to go.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: Before even a quick winter errand, how must you prep your glass and clear sudden cabin fogging?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Peephole scraping leaves huge blind zones, while cracking a window clears interior breath fog fast alongside working defrosters.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: Which two warning-light colors identify snowplows and sanding trucks, and how should you approach them?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Heavy plows kick up blinding snow clouds and travel well below highway pace behind yellow-and-blue beacons.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: When does Colorado law make passing a snowplow strictly illegal?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Government plows staggered in tandem formation span multiple lanes pushing heavy snow ridges with zero safe gap between.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: How should you adjust speed, following gap, and side clearance around pedestrians and cyclists in snow and ice?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Plowed snowbanks force walkers and cyclists closer to traffic just when icy roads stretch your stopping room.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: What hazards come with Colorado mountain driving, and how should you control speed down steep grades?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Using engine braking in a lower gear spares wheel brakes from overheating and fading down long mountain passes.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: Where on mountain two-lane roads is crossing into the oncoming lane to pass illegal?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Canyon walls, blind curves, and hillcrests hide fast downhill traffic until head-on impact is unavoidable.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: Beyond steep grades and fast weather shifts, what hidden road junctions and roadside movers appear in the mountains?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Pines and brush conceal side roads until the last second while deer or elk step onto mountain pavement.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: What should you do if your vehicle loses pace climbing a steep grade, and who holds mountain right-of-way?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Pulling off or hugging right lets faster climbers pass, while downhill drivers yield because backing uphill is far safer.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: Pair who gets right-of-way on a narrow mountain grade with the courtesy duty of a slow climbing vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Uphill vehicles beat oncoming downhill ones on tight grades, yet slow climbers still keep right for faster traffic behind.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: Which roadway category carries the highest fatality rate per mile driven across the United States?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: High speeds, unforgiving roadsides, and longer emergency response distances make rural highways America's deadliest miles.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: Which design features—from curves and hills to lane width and edges—make rural roads extra risky?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Tight lanes without paved shoulders or guardrails leave zero recovery room around blind curves and steep dips.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: What hidden entrances, unmarked tracks, debris, and slow traffic must you anticipate on rural roads?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Overgrown driveways, crossing farm machinery, unmarked train tracks, livestock, and cyclists appear abruptly at highway speeds.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: How do unpaved dirt or gravel rural surfaces—and washboard ripples—affect vehicle control?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Loose stones cut tire grip while corrugated washboard bumps chatter tires off the ground and destabilize steering.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: How can striking potholes upset your vehicle's grip on the road?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Sharp pothole impacts bounce suspension upward so tires momentarily lose road contact and steering bite.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.question_text: Why do many bicyclist fatalities happen on rural roads, and how should you adjust speed and buffer when passing?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.teaching_text: High-speed rural wind blasts can knock a rider sideways, so ease speed and give well beyond three feet.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.question_text: Why can yesterday's path through a construction zone look different today, and what guides you ahead?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.teaching_text: Crews realign lanes day by day around heavy equipment, using advance signs and cones to cue drivers early.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.question_text: Which three core driving habits keep you out of trouble inside any construction zone?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.teaching_text: Sudden flagger stops and lane tapers punish distracted tailgaters before they can touch the brake pedal.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.question_text: What traffic controls appear on major construction projects, and why are speed limits reduced there?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.teaching_text: Complex detours, concrete barriers, and flaggers take extra seconds to process, which lower work-zone speeds provide.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.question_text: Why must construction workers stay constantly on guard beside active travel lanes?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.teaching_text: Cones and barrels cannot stop a drifting car, leaving workers inches from live traffic without full wall separation.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.question_text: How do police presence and ticket fines change in Colorado work zones, and which other zone matches?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.teaching_text: Stepped-up patrols enforce doubled fines across both construction zones and school zones alike.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.question_text: Which crash type dominates construction zones, what causes it, and whom must you obey?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.teaching_text: Looking away as traffic bunches causes rear-end pileups, so watch the bumper ahead and obey flaggers and speed signs.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: Pair the two special zones that double traffic fines with the number-one collision inside work zones?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Both school and construction zones double ticket fines, while inattentive following drives most work-zone rear-enders.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.question_text: Why is calm, defensive driving necessary even when you follow every traffic rule yourself?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.teaching_text: Assuming other motorists might miss signs or drive aggressively keeps you calm, unprovoked, and ready with an out.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.question_text: Who inside your vehicle needs to wear a fastened seat belt?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.teaching_text: A single unbelted passenger risks fatal injury and endangers buckled riders during violent crash forces.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.question_text: Which three exceptions allow using a mobile device while driving under Colorado law?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.teaching_text: Outside calling police or fire, handling emergencies, or routing through hands-free gear, mobile phone use stays barred.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.question_text: When is texting while driving permitted in Colorado, and does a hands-free accessory excuse texting?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.teaching_text: Colorado's listed texting exceptions cover only police, fire, or emergency contact without adding any hands-free carve-out.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: How do Colorado's exceptions for general mobile-device use differ from its exceptions for texting?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Both rules allow police, fire, and emergency contact, yet only general phone use adds the hands-free accessory exception.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.question_text: Which clock positions and turning techniques belong on the steering wheel, and which two habits are unsafe?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.teaching_text: Holding nine-and-three or eight-and-four with hand-over-hand or push-pull-slide beats palming or letting rims spin loose.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.question_text: Which directions should you scan continuously, and what head-check pattern applies at intersections?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.teaching_text: Checking left, right, and left again catches fast motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians stepping off curbs.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.question_text: How many seconds ahead should you aim your gaze, and what distance is that in town versus open highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.teaching_text: Scanning a city block or open half-mile ahead spots brake lights early enough to prevent panic swerves.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.question_text: How frequently should you glance at your rearview mirror, and which maneuvers call for extra checks?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.teaching_text: Checking mirrors every five to eight seconds—plus before lane shifts, braking, backing, intersections, or steep descents—tracks tailgaters.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.question_text: How do you measure safe normal-weather following distance using a roadside fixed point?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.teaching_text: Reaching a shadow or signpost before finishing a three-second count behind the car ahead proves you are tailgating.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: Match ten seconds, five to eight seconds, and three seconds to forward gaze, mirrors, and following space?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Keep ten seconds scanning forward, five to eight checking mirrors, and three seconds cushioning the bumper ahead.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: Which four driving environment factors can dramatically lengthen the distance you need to stop?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Rainy pavement, heavy rush-hour congestion, or darkness stretches total stopping room well beyond dry midday baselines.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: Why should you stay within posted limits while matching surrounding flow instead of driving much faster or slower?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Weaving much faster forces constant passing while crawling far below pace creates backups and unpredictable braking.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: Where two lanes narrow into one, how does a proper Colorado zipper merge work?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Filling both lanes evenly right up to the taper and alternating one-by-one keeps traffic flowing smoothly.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: In a zipper merge, is riding the closing lane all the way to the taper rude cutting-in?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Abandoning the closing lane half a mile early wastes road capacity; merging cleanly at the taper is encouraged.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: Which eight busy locations or choke points count as slow zones needing lower speed and heightened focus?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Shopping lots, schools, parks, neighborhoods, rush hour, narrow bridges, toll plazas, and tracks pack sudden conflict points.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: What legal threshold allows law enforcement officers to initiate a traffic stop?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Officers pull vehicles over whenever observable facts establish reasonable suspicion of a traffic or criminal offense.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: How should you respond when police lights or a siren activate right behind your car?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Signaling calmly onto the right shoulder—and moving farther off traffic if asked—keeps both you and the officer safe.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: Once parked for a traffic stop, which five cabin actions set up a safe roadside interaction?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Shutting down engine and stereo, staying buckled inside, flipping dome lights at night, and showing hands calms the stop.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: Which window do you lower at a stop, and how do you handle weapons or reaching for paperwork?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Lower whichever window the officer approaches, calmly state any weapon upfront without touching it, and pause before reaching.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: What happens with identification when an officer making a stop is not wearing a uniform?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Non-uniformed officers normally display official credentials automatically, and you are entitled to request them politely.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: Which three documents do officers typically request, and how should you retrieve them if stored out of reach?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Tell the officer where your glovebox or bag holds your papers and get permission before lunging toward it.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: How should you behave if asked out of the vehicle, and what three stop outcomes can occur?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Keep your hands in plain sight where directed, and politely ask whether a warning, citation, or arrest applies.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: Where do ticket disputes belong instead of the shoulder, and how do you address improper officer conduct?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Roadside arguments never erase citations; save legal challenges for court and ask promptly for a supervisor if needed.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: What does your signature on a traffic ticket mean legally, and what happens if you refuse to sign?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Signing simply acknowledges receipt and court instructions, whereas refusing to sign can put you under arrest.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: Separate signing a citation, refusing to sign it, and disputing the charge?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Sign at the window without admitting fault to avoid arrest, then bring any disagreement before the judge.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: What shared rights, legal duties, and handling differences define sharing the road in Colorado?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Every traveler shares legal road rights and safety duties while respecting how bikes, motorcycles, buses, and trucks maneuver.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: Under what traffic-state, space, and speed conditions may a two-wheeled motorcycle lane-filter in Colorado?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: Two-wheeled motorcycles may roll past stopped cars at fifteen miles per hour maximum only when adjacent lanes are stopped.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: Which motorcycle type, surrounding traffic state, and top speed cap limit legal Colorado lane filtering?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Weaving between rolling cars is never filtering; adjacent traffic must sit completely stopped beneath a fifteen-mile-per-hour cap.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.question_text: Which driver maneuver causes most motorist-at-fault bicycle and motorcycle wrecks, and how do you prevent it?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.teaching_text: Drivers turning left misjudge narrow oncoming riders near lane edges or shoulders, so look twice and gauge approach speed.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.question_text: What legal status, full-lane and one-way street rights, and horn etiquette apply around bicyclists?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.teaching_text: Cyclists obey vehicle laws, claim full lanes at traffic speed or either side of multi-lane one-ways, and startle at horns.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: What makes the No Zones around large trucks and buses so hazardous to nearby cars?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: Disappearing from cab mirrors or crowding a heavy rig's braking cushion spikes collision danger immediately.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: Why must you never duck past or stop right behind a truck or bus preparing to back up?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: A long box trailer or transit coach creates a massive rear blind spot that hides cars directly behind.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: Which two visibility losses happen simultaneously when you tailgate a truck or bus?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: Riding a rear bumper hides your car from the rig's mirrors while filling your own windshield with metal.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: How do the side blind spots of trucks and buses compare with passenger cars, and what risk follows?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Camping alongside trailer wheels leaves you hidden if wind or road debris forces the rig sideways.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: Why is stopping behind white intersection stop bars especially helpful around turning trucks and buses?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: Engineers set white stop lines back so wide-turning trailers can sweep corners without clipping waiting hoods.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: On which side should you overtake a truck, and what mirror cue tells you it is safe to merge back?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: Cutting in before both truck headlamps appear in your inside mirror steals a heavy rig's long braking cushion.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: What visual mirror benchmark governs pulling back ahead of a semi-truck just like any regular pass?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Seeing the entire front grille and both headlamps inside your rearview mirror confirms safe clearance before merging right.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: Why do trucks and buses swing leftward before turning right, and where must you never squeeze?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: Rear trailer wheels track tighter than the cab, crushing any car that sneaks into the right-curb gap.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: What is a right-signaling truck or bus doing when it shifts left approaching a corner?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Mistaking that leftward swing for a lane opening lures impatient drivers right into a trailer pinch.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: What emergency role do mountain runaway truck ramps serve, and which three stops are illegal there?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: Blocking a gravel arrestor ramp to chain tires, fix a flat, or park leaves a brakeless rig nowhere to go.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: What visual sign warns of a runaway truck or bus, and where must you move immediately?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: Billowing brake smoke signals overheated, fading drums, so clear the lane fast and never pull ahead of it.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: Why must you stay extra alert behind transit buses and cautious when passing a stopped one?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Transit coaches brake at curb stops every few blocks and merge back into live lanes right after boarding.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: Who holds right-of-way when a bus pulls back into traffic from a drop-off zone, and whom should you watch for?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: Yield to transit buses re-entering lanes while scanning ahead of the bumper for riders loading front bike racks.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.question_text: In which two everyday settings must you use heightened caution around school buses and crossing students?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.teaching_text: Residential blocks and school zones concentrate excited kids boarding, stepping off, and darting across streets.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.question_text: What do overhead yellow warning lights on a school bus announce, and what triggers the switch to red?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.teaching_text: Overhead yellow warns you to brake early because opening the bus door immediately deploys red flashers and the stop arm.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: Contrast the meaning of overhead yellow school-bus lights against red lights paired with the STOP arm?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Never floor the gas on yellow warning flashers because red lamps and the extended arm follow when doors open.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.question_text: How far from a stopped school bus's front or rear bumper must you halt, and when may you move?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.teaching_text: Hold at least twenty feet clear until the driver retracts the stop arm and extinguishes red flashers.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.question_text: How must you respond to alternating flashing red lights on either end of a school bus?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.teaching_text: Brake to a complete stop at least twenty feet back and roll cautiously only once alternating reds cease.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.question_text: Compare which directions stop for a school bus on a four-plus-lane median-divided highway versus an undivided two- or four-lane road?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.teaching_text: Without a physical median even four-lane roads stop both directions, whereas a median-divided highway stops following lanes only.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.question_text: Who must stop for a school bus on a highway with five or more lanes including a shared center turn lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.teaching_text: Wide five-lane arterials with a shared center turn lane require stopping only in lanes traveling behind the bus.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: Across Colorado road layouts, sort where oncoming traffic stops for a school bus versus where oncoming keeps moving?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Oncoming stops on two-lane or undivided four-lane streets, and keeps rolling with a median or five-plus center-turn layout.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.question_text: How heavy can a light rail car be, and what rule governs turning across light rail tracks?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.teaching_text: Up to forty tons on steel wheels cannot stop quickly, so scan every direction and never turn ahead of one.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.question_text: What foot traffic and sightline traps require extra alertness around light rail corridors?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.teaching_text: Quiet electric trains emerge suddenly from behind urban buildings or landscaping right where transit riders cross.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.question_text: What do light-rail signals and gates command, and why must you never drive around a lowered gate after one train clears?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.teaching_text: Weaving around lowered gates right after one train clears puts you directly into an unseen opposite-direction train.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.question_text: How high do standard light-rail overhead wires hang, and how must you handle a downed wire or broken crossing gear?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.teaching_text: Overhead catenary wires sit eighteen feet six inches up, and any hanging wire is high-voltage—stay back and alert RTD.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.question_text: Which standard traffic control does a railroad crossbuck match, and what does a numbered plaque underneath indicate?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.teaching_text: Approach every crossbuck ready to yield to trains, checking any lower plaque to see if multiple tracks cross.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: Contrast your legal duty at a passive railroad crossbuck versus active flashing lights or crossing gates?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: A plain crossbuck works like a yield, whereas active signals or lowered gates demand a full stop without crossing.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.question_text: Which two large vehicle types must stop at most railroad crossings, and how should following drivers prepare?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.teaching_text: Following closely behind a commercial bus or hazmat tanker at clear tracks invites a rear-end crash when they stop.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: What non-driving financial court order can cost you your Colorado driving privilege if left unpaid?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Even a spotless driving record will not shield your license when court-ordered child support falls behind.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: What document must you carry whenever you drive, and what do you risk if you cannot show an officer?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Having an active policy at home does not save you at the curb if you cannot produce valid proof on request.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: How can a conviction for buying or holding alcohol under age twenty-one affect your driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Colorado links underage alcohol buying and possession directly to your driving privilege.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: In vehicles equipped with built-in belts, which three groups must wear a fastened seat belt on Colorado public roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Adults riding in the back row may not be covered under the general rule, though buckling every seat saves lives.
sec02-card-sec02-F04.must_match_memory_hook: Driver, front riders, kids under sixteen

visual_sync.text_span: Driver, front riders, kids under sixteen

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: Which five occupational, vehicle, or medical situations are exempt from Colorado's mandatory seat belt rule?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Notice a medical exemption requires carrying an actual physician statement covering physical or psychological grounds.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: When does a delivery-van driver qualify for the seat belt exemption versus have to buckle up like everyone else?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: Once the shift ends and that van heads home off the clock, the standard driver seat-belt law snaps right back on.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: How do Colorado's seat-belt and passenger-count rules tighten whenever the driver is younger than eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Unlike adult drivers, an under-eighteen driver must have back-seat riders of every age buckled with one belt per person.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: When a child's parent is not riding in the car, who is legally responsible for securing that child properly?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Giving a neighbor's kid a ride puts any missing booster or loose strap squarely on the driver's shoulders.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: How and where must a child younger than two weighing under forty pounds ride?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Combining rear-facing support with back-seat placement gives babies maximum protection away from front airbags.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: What restraint options apply to a child younger than two who already weighs forty pounds or more?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Hitting forty pounds before age two unlocks forward-facing seats alongside high-capacity rear-facing models.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: For children younger than two, what exact weight threshold separates rear-facing-only from facing either direction?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: Test questions pair a one-year-old with different weights to check whether you spot the forty-pound pivot.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: How must a child aged two to under four weighing at least twenty pounds be restrained and seated?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Toddlers in this band stay in harnessed rear- or forward-facing restraints rather than jumping early to boosters.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: What restraint and seating rule covers a child aged four to under nine weighing forty pounds or more?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: Boosters lift grade-schoolers until adult lap and shoulder belts rest across strong hip and collarbone structure.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: Match the twenty-pound weight floor and the forty-pound booster floor to their exact Colorado child age bands?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: Keeping twenty pounds with ages two-to-four and forty pounds with ages four-to-nine prevents mixing up booster eligibility.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: How must youths from age nine up to eighteen be secured inside a vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Older kids and teens must use a properly fitted seat belt or manufacturer-approved restraint in every row.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.question_text: Where does impairment from alcohol, drugs, or combined substances rank among traffic hazards?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.teaching_text: Mixing or using impairing substances sits near the very top of preventable highway deaths year after year.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.question_text: What drug classification does alcohol belong to, and how does it alter your brain, reflexes, and driving choices?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.teaching_text: People often mistake alcohol for a stimulant at parties, yet chemically it dulls reactions while encouraging reckless speed.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.question_text: Which two open substances are banned inside the passenger area of a vehicle on public roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.teaching_text: Colorado's open-container law covers broken-seal cannabis packaging in the cabin right alongside open booze.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.question_text: Which five personal and drinking factors explain why two people having the same drinks hit different BAC readings?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.teaching_text: Copying a heavier friend drink-for-drink can push your blood alcohol past legal cutoffs while theirs stays lower.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.question_text: Which serving sizes of beer, wine, and distilled spirits pack roughly the same amount of pure alcohol?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.teaching_text: A twelve-ounce can of beer hits your bloodstream with the same alcohol load as a shot of whiskey.
sec02-card-sec02-F21.must_match_memory_hook: Twelve beer, five wine, one-five spirits

visual_sync.text_span: Twelve beer, five wine, one-five spirits

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: Why doesn't sticking to beer or wine instead of liquor make driving any safer?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Your liver processes total ethyl alcohol, caring zero whether it arrived in fizz, grapes, or a shot glass.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.question_text: What is the sole cure for blood alcohol, and how fast does average BAC drop each hour?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.teaching_text: At roughly fifteen thousandths of a percent per hour, several evening drinks can leave you impaired the next morning.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.question_text: Why do black coffee, fresh air, or cold showers fail to lower your blood alcohol concentration?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.teaching_text: Caffeine only creates a wide-awake impaired driver while BAC crawls down at its fixed hourly pace.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.question_text: How does Colorado's definition of DWAI differ in impairment degree from DUI?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.teaching_text: You do not have to weave across lanes to get arrested when even slight impairment meets Colorado's DWAI standard.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.question_text: At what blood alcohol reading can a driver be convicted of DUI per se?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.teaching_text: Per se means the chemical reading itself proves the violation without needing extra proof of bad driving.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: Separate DWAI, standard DUI, and DUI per se in one clean comparison?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: Knowing two charges rest on driving ability while per se rests on the chemical number clears up tricky exam stems.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.question_text: Besides a chemical BAC reading, which three types of roadside evidence can convict an impaired driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.teaching_text: Staying under point zero eight will not block a conviction when swerving, slurred speech, and field tests show impairment.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.question_text: Alongside test refusal, which three BAC cutoffs for adults, under-twenty-one drivers, and CDL holders trigger license revocation?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.teaching_text: Underage drivers hit revocation at a fraction of the adult threshold—essentially one sip away from losing privileges.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: Match the revocation BAC thresholds of point zero two, point zero four, and point zero eight to each driver group?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: Notice each step doubles from youth at two hundredths to commercial at four hundredths to general adults at eight.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.question_text: For a driver twenty-one or older, what BAC benchmark, points, fine, jail, and service attach to a first DWAI?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.teaching_text: Even the lesser first offense brings up to five hundred dollars in fines, jail risk, public service, and eight points.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.question_text: For a driver twenty-one or older, what BAC benchmark, revocation length, fine, jail, and service follow a first DUI?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.teaching_text: Stepping from DWAI up to first DUI swaps points for an automatic nine-month loss of your license plus steeper penalties.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: How does the license hit on a first adult DWAI differ fundamentally from a first adult DUI?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: First DWAI is the lone impaired conviction scored as eight points rather than an immediate multi-month revocation.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.question_text: What revocation length, fine range, jail range, and public-service hours hit on a second DWAI or DUI?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.teaching_text: On offense two, Colorado merges DWAI and DUI into the same one-year revocation, higher fine ceiling, and ten-day jail floor.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.question_text: What revocation length, fine range, jail floor, and public service hit on a third or later DWAI or DUI?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.teaching_text: Repeat offenders face two full years off the road and at least sixty mandatory days behind bars.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: Trace how license revocation length climbs across a first DUI, a second offense, and a third or later offense?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: Memorizing nine months, twelve months, and twenty-four months nails the exact repeat-offender progression.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.question_text: When does a driver under twenty-one face revocation on a first DUI or DWAI versus on a second or third?
