sec02-card-sec02-F27.teaching_text: Completing every court-ordered evaluation and class is the only way a first-time minor avoids revocation, while strike two revokes automatically.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.question_text: Does an under-twenty-one alcohol purchase or possession conviction require a car to revoke your license?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.teaching_text: Getting cited on foot at a party or store parking lot can still strip your driver license.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.question_text: Contrast how revocation works on a first under-twenty-one DUI or DWAI against a repeat conviction?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.teaching_text: Second and third convictions offer zero program escape hatch—the license is revoked every single time.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.question_text: How do Colorado's penalties for driving impaired by cannabis, prescriptions, or cold medicine compare with alcohol?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.teaching_text: Buying a substance at a pharmacy or dispensary never softens the DUI charge once it impairs your driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.question_text: Does holding a medical prescription or using medical marijuana shield you from a DUI or DWAI charge?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.teaching_text: Judges look strictly at whether you could drive safely, not whether a doctor recommended the substance.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.question_text: Summarize why legal over-the-counter, prescription, and medical cannabis use can still trigger alcohol-style penalties?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.teaching_text: Legality at the counter ends at the driver's door whenever drowsiness or slowed reflexes set in.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.question_text: What determines how strongly a drug impairs someone, and which three everyday medication types can impair driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.teaching_text: An ordinary antihistamine or cough tablet taken before school or work can hit like a sedative behind the wheel.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.question_text: What two steps should you take before driving on any medication, especially when warning print is missing or unclear?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.teaching_text: Thirty seconds checking the bottle or asking the pharmacist beats discovering drowsiness in fast highway traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: When a five-plus-lane Colorado road includes a shared center turn lane, which directions stop for a school bus?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Wide five-lane corridors keep children crossing only on the bus's side, sparing oncoming lanes while locking lanes behind.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: What kind of legal exposure follows from violating Colorado's school bus traffic laws?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Passing a stopped school bus endangers kids stepping off the curb and brings heavy statutory penalties.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: Because trains run on unscheduled clocks day and night, how must you approach every railroad crossing?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Assuming a familiar track stays empty at night leads drivers straight past active bells, lights, or signs.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: How does a train's massive bulk distort your speed sense, and what stopping distance does a fifty-five-mile-per-hour freight train need?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Drivers try beating trains across tracks because giant locomotives look deceptively slow yet need a full mile to stop.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: Why is trying to eyeball whether you can beat an approaching fifty-five-mile-per-hour freight train so risky?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Once an engineer spots your car on the rails, physics prevents stopping inside a mile even under full emergency brakes.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: When you reach railroad tracks lacking flashing lights or gates, what precaution applies before crossing?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Passive rural crossings give zero automatic flash when a train nears, making your own stop-and-look check vital.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: What clearance must exist before entering railroad tracks, and what hidden danger lurks at multi-track crossings?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Getting boxed onto rails by traffic ahead, or rushing across behind one train into a second, turns fatal fast.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: Which sole traffic sign uses a circular outline, and why is it placed well ahead of the tracks?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Spotting the lone round sign on the road gives you braking distance before reaching the tracks themselves.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: What letters mark railroad pavement approaches, where must you wait without a painted line, and how far do trains overhang?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Locomotives and boxcars jut three feet past the steel rail, clipping any bumper crept closer than ten feet.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: Where no white stop line is painted before railroad tracks, what minimum setback protects you from train overhang?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Holding at least ten feet back leaves safe breathing room beyond the train's three-foot side overhang.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: How do you identify a designated railroad quiet zone, and what warns you instead of locomotive horns?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Rolling windows down to listen fails inside quiet zones where trains stay silent and rely on lights and gates.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: Which standard sign does a railroad crossbuck mirror, what plaque sits beneath multi-track posts, and when does it turn regulatory?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: Checking the track-count plaque below the X-shaped crossbuck warns you to scan more than one set of rails.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: Why must you leave stopping margin behind commercial buses or hazardous-materials trucks nearing railroad tracks?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Tailgating a hazmat tanker or transit bus into an open crossing causes rear-end hits when they stop by law.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: When red railroad crossing lights start flashing, what must you do and how long must you hold?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: Pulling out while red signals still flash after one train clears risks meeting a second train head-on.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: What is the legal status of the roadway while crossing gates sit lowered, and when may you proceed?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Weaving around lowered arms enters a legally closed crossing before both gates rise and red lights go dark.
sec13-card-sec13-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Road closed until gates, lights clear

visual_sync.text_span: Road closed until gates, lights clear

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: Contrast your legal duty at a lone crossbuck against your duty at flashing red lights or lowered gates?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Passive crossbucks act like yield signs until a train nears, whereas active lights or gates command an absolute stop.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: How does the job of the round advance railroad sign differ from the job of the crossbuck at the tracks?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: One sign alerts you down the block so you can brake, while the trackside crossbuck sets your actual yield point.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: If your engine dies straddling railroad tracks, what happens first even with empty rails, and whom do you call?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Cranking a dead starter wastes seconds before an unseen train arrives; clear every passenger first, then dial ENS or police.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: Where is the blue Emergency Notification System sign mounted at public rail crossings, and when is its line answered?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: Spotting the blue placard on the crossbuck post connects you directly to rail dispatch at any hour.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: Which emergencies belong on the ENS hotline, and what code on the blue sign lets dispatchers stop the right train?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: Street names can blur across rural miles, whereas reading the exact DOT crossing tag pinpoints your rails instantly.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: Why must phoning the ENS hotline or police always come second when a vehicle stalls on railroad tracks?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Making phone calls from inside a stalled cabin leaves everyone trapped if a silent fast train rounds the bend.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: Which directions can RTD light rail run along Denver-area streets, and what road rules apply to its operators?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: Because street light rail can run counter-flow as well as with traffic, one-way glances miss oncoming trains.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: How heavy can a single light rail car be, and what check is vital before turning across its tracks?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: Cutting across street rails like an ordinary lane turn puts a forty-ton railcar on your door with no quick stop.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: What pedestrian and sightline hazards cluster around RTD light rail stops and urban corridors?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: Passengers hurrying off platforms and trains masked behind buildings or landscaping create sudden urban conflicts.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.question_text: Which three types of control devices guard light rail crossings, and what single command do they share?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.teaching_text: Whether controlled by standard traffic signals, flashing rail lights, or gate arms, active signals forbid crossing.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.question_text: Why must you never weave around light rail gates even the moment one train clears the crossing?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.teaching_text: Gates stay down after the first train passes whenever a second train is closing fast from the other side.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.question_text: At what standard height do light rail overhead wires hang, and how must you treat any sagging or downed line?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.teaching_text: High-voltage catenary lines electrocute through anything touching them, and tall loads must respect eighteen-foot-six clearance.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.question_text: Whom should you contact immediately upon spotting a low-hanging light rail wire or broken crossing signal?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.teaching_text: Fast calls to nine-one-one or RTD let transit crews cut line power and flag approaching trains before someone gets hurt.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.question_text: How does Colorado roadway law classify bicycles, and what general rules govern riders?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.teaching_text: Recognizing cyclists as legal vehicle operators clarifies why they take turn lanes and obey traffic lights.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.question_text: How can city or town ordinances modify where bicyclists ride and which rights apply on sidewalks and crosswalks?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.teaching_text: Where municipalities allow sidewalk cycling, riders cross intersections carrying pedestrian priority and duties.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.question_text: Does one uniform Colorado statute decide whether bicycles may use sidewalks in every town?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.teaching_text: Assuming sidewalk bikes are banned, or permitted, everywhere ignores city-by-city local ordinances across Colorado.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.question_text: What size, protection, and rider-experience factors demand active visual scanning around bicyclists?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.teaching_text: Narrow bike silhouettes hide behind mirror posts, and young or novice riders may wobble unexpectedly.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.question_text: Where do cyclists normally position themselves, and what five conditions let them legally ride down the lane center?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.teaching_text: Swinging mid-lane avoids car-door openings, broken glass, storm grates, narrow squeeze points, and blind visibility.
sec13-card-sec13-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Right edge unless hazards require center

visual_sync.text_span: Right edge unless hazards require center

sec13-card-sec13-F30.question_text: Under what traffic condition may two cyclists ride side by side in Colorado, and how can that help passing?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.teaching_text: Two riders side by side create a wider visual target and shorten the lengthwise distance a passing car must clear.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: Why shouldn't a motorist assume a cyclist mid-lane or riding two abreast is breaking Colorado law?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Colorado explicitly permits lane-center hazard avoidance and side-by-side riding whenever normal traffic is unimpeded.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.question_text: From what point on your rig is Colorado's three-foot bicycle pass measured, does it apply beside bike lanes, and what if space is tight?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.teaching_text: Wide tow mirrors or trailers count as your outermost edge, so slow down and wait behind whenever three feet is missing.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.question_text: When does Colorado law allow crossing a solid double yellow centerline to pass a bicyclist?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.teaching_text: Giving cyclists a full three-foot safety buffer outweighs double-yellow restrictions once opposing lanes are verified clear.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: How do Colorado's double-yellow exception and tight-lane rule work together when overtaking a cyclist?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: If oncoming cars prevent straddling the yellow line for three full feet, patience behind the cyclist is mandatory.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.question_text: How must motorists yield to bicyclists inside intersections?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.teaching_text: Underestimating a bike's closing speed at an intersection causes classic right-of-way T-bone collisions.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.question_text: Who owns priority inside a bike lane, even across unpainted intersection gaps, and what three car actions are banned there?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.teaching_text: Stopping, parking, or cruising inside a bike lane forces unprotected cyclists out into fast motor traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.question_text: Before turning left across opposing lanes, where can oncoming cyclists hide and what must you judge?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.teaching_text: An oncoming bike tucked behind an SUV or hugging the shoulder moves fast enough to get cut off mid-turn.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.question_text: What two-stage sequence prevents stop-sign and traffic-signal collisions with cyclists?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.teaching_text: Rolling past the stop bar while glancing sideways puts your front bumper straight across bike and crosswalk lanes.

sec13-card-sec13-F35.question_text: Before swinging your street-side car door open, what rear check and hand switch help spot passing cyclists?
sec13-card-sec13-F35.teaching_text: Reaching across your body with your far hand naturally pivots your shoulders toward the mirror and blind spot.

sec13-card-sec13-F36.question_text: How should you position and time a right turn when a cyclist is riding straight toward the same corner?
sec13-card-sec13-F36.teaching_text: Waiting for through cyclists and turning snug to the curb blocks dangerous right-hook cutoffs.

sec13-card-sec13-F37.question_text: Which three paths and directions must you scan before nosing out of a driveway?
sec13-card-sec13-F37.teaching_text: Cyclists and scooters cross driveways along sidewalks and bike paths from either direction, not just street flow.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.question_text: Why is parking or stopping inside a bike lane dangerous, and when is crossing one legal?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.teaching_text: Parked cars force cyclists out into fast lanes, whereas brief crossings for turns, alleys, or driveways stay lawful.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: Contrast crossing across a bike lane for an alley or turn against stopping inside it?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: Moving cleanly across a bike lane after yielding is legal, while lingering or parking inside it is forbidden.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.question_text: Are cyclists required to stay inside a marked bike lane, and which sides work on a one-way multi-lane street?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.teaching_text: Left-hand turns or left-side hazards make riding on either edge of a multi-lane one-way street completely legal.
sec14-card-sec14-F02.must_match_memory_hook: May leave lane; either one-way side

visual_sync.text_span: May leave lane; either one-way side

sec14-card-sec14-F06.question_text: Under Colorado's two-thousand-twenty-two law, how may riders fifteen and older treat clear stop signs and red lights?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.teaching_text: Once an intersection is clear and priority is theirs, fifteen-plus cyclists conserve momentum safely under statutory rules.
sec14-card-sec14-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Stop as yield; red as stop

visual_sync.text_span: Stop as yield; red as stop

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: Which age cutoff and two intersection conditions limit Colorado's stop-as-yield bicycle rule?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: Younger kids under fifteen, or riders facing cross traffic with the right-of-way, still follow standard stop rules.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.question_text: Which direction does Colorado law require cyclists to travel, and why should drivers still scan every angle?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.teaching_text: Even though wrong-way riding breaks road rules, defensive drivers check both directions so mistakes never turn fatal.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.question_text: When must your turn signal be blinking, and what must you verify when driving straight?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.teaching_text: Leaving a forgotten blinker flashing while cruising straight tricks waiting cyclists and drivers into pulling out.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.question_text: How should you position your vehicle for a right turn, including where a green or dashed Conflict Zone is marked?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.teaching_text: Merging close to the curb through a marked Conflict Zone closes the gap that tempts cyclists to pass inside.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.question_text: As you set up for a right turn and spot a bicyclist riding alongside you, who goes first?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.teaching_text: Trying to beat a parallel cyclist around a right corner cuts straight across their front wheel.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.question_text: After stopping completely for a legal right turn on red, which three bicycle paths must you check?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.teaching_text: Focusing only on cars coming from your left misses cyclists rolling up your right flank or turning across.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.question_text: Before backing, changing lanes, or turning, especially turning left, where must you look for cyclists?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.teaching_text: Slim bike frames vanish behind roof pillars during lane shifts and blend into right shoulders on opposing approaches.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.question_text: How does Colorado law classify deliberately crowding or forcing a bicyclist off the roadway?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.teaching_text: Using a two-ton car to intimidate or push a cyclist off pavement brings serious aggressive-driving charges.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.question_text: What dual mindset should guide motorists whenever sharing lanes with bicyclists?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.teaching_text: Combining full right-of-way respect with extra care for unprotected riders prevents misjudged gaps.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.question_text: Which three vehicle, road, or weather situations call for giving a cyclist wider room than three feet?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.teaching_text: High-speed rural air wakes and side gusts from trucks or SUVs can shove a lightweight bike sideways.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.question_text: Why must you never cut in and brake hard or turn sharply right ahead of a moving bicyclist?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.teaching_text: Four wide car tires shed speed far quicker than skinny bike rims, leaving the cyclist nowhere to go.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.question_text: Why do wet asphalt, gravel, and road debris call for extra patience around bicyclists?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.teaching_text: Puddles or loose sand that a car barely feels can wash out a cyclist's front tire or force sudden swerves.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.question_text: Under what sole circumstance should you sound your horn near a bicyclist?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.teaching_text: A sudden loud blast right behind an open-air rider can startle them into wobbling straight into traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.question_text: What street-parking exit habit is called the Dutch Reach, and which hand opens the latch?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.teaching_text: Reaching across with the hand closer to the console turns your torso to spot bikes in the door zone.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.question_text: Why might a cyclist keep both hands gripping the bars instead of signaling, and what clues tip you off?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.teaching_text: Braking over bumps demands two-handed grip, so a quick over-the-shoulder glance often telegraphs an upcoming lane move.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.question_text: How does a cyclist hand-signal a right turn, a left turn, and slowing or stopping?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.teaching_text: Reading all four arm positions instantly tells you which way a rider ahead plans to turn or brake.
sec14-card-sec14-F18.must_match_memory_hook: Right out-or-up; left out; down stop

visual_sync.text_span: Right out-or-up; left out; down stop

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: When a cyclist ahead bends their left arm ninety degrees upward, which turn are they signaling?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: Test-takers often guess left because the left arm moves, forgetting an upward ninety-degree bend means right turn.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: Contrast a cyclist holding their left arm straight out horizontally against bending that left arm downward?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: Pointing horizontally left marks a turn, whereas dropping the forearm toward the pavement warns of braking.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.question_text: How do a motorcyclist's legal road rights compare with their physical protection in a crash?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.teaching_text: Without steel doors, airbags, or seat belts around the rider, minor car fender-benders become severe motorcycle trauma.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.question_text: How much lane width belongs to a motorcycle, why do riders weave inside it, and what can gusts do?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.teaching_text: Never crowd into a motorcycle's lane because riders adjust position for sightlines and crosswinds can shove them.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.question_text: Under what traffic state, space check, and speed cap may a two-wheeled motorcycle lane filter in Colorado?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.teaching_text: Filtering applies strictly past stopped cars when adjacent lanes are also stopped and bike speed stays at or under fifteen.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: Does Colorado's lane-filtering rule allow weaving between moving highway traffic or using three-wheeled trikes?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Separating low-speed filtering past stopped traffic on two wheels from high-speed lane splitting nails exam traps.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.question_text: Which visibility, braking, and road-surface traits call for leaving a longer following gap behind motorcycles?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.teaching_text: Light motorcycles shed speed fast and swerve around potholes, demanding extra seconds of following cushion.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.question_text: Which turning mistake ranks among top bicycle crashes, and where must your eyes sweep first?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.teaching_text: Drivers fixated on oncoming cars overlook fast oncoming cyclists hugging the right lane edge or shoulder.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.question_text: Beyond left turns, which four everyday mistakes commonly cause car-bicycle collisions?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.teaching_text: Checking behind before opening doors and looking both ways at driveways and stop bars eliminates classic urban crashes.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.question_text: Is sharing the road with bikes, motorcycles, and walkers merely polite advice or a legal mandate?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.teaching_text: Failing to yield or crowd vulnerable road users violates enforceable Colorado statutes, not optional etiquette.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.question_text: Who falls under Colorado's pedestrian definition across public and private pavement, and who bears watch duty?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.teaching_text: Whether someone walks, jogs, stands, or rolls in a wheelchair on a street or lot, motorists carry the duty of care.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.question_text: Why must you sometimes slow below the posted limit near foot traffic, especially around kids or wheelchair users?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.teaching_text: Small children and seated wheelchair users sit below SUV beltlines and parked trunks until you are close.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.question_text: At which intersections and crosswalks do pedestrians hold right-of-way, and what must drivers do?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.teaching_text: Waiting for white paint misses legal unmarked crosswalks at corners where drivers must yield or stop completely.
sec14-card-sec14-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Every intersection crosswalk, painted or not

visual_sync.text_span: Every intersection crosswalk, painted or not

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: Does missing crosswalk paint strip a pedestrian of right-of-way at a street intersection?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: Sidewalk extensions across any corner form legal crosswalks even without a single drop of white paint.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.question_text: Before edging forward to check vehicle gaps for a turn on red, what lane, stop, and walker steps come first?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.teaching_text: Rolling straight to the curb line to peek at cars blocks the exact crosswalk pedestrians step into.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.question_text: Put stopping for pedestrians and creeping forward for cross-traffic sightlines in the right order on a red turn?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.teaching_text: Reversing that sequence puts your bumper over the crosswalk before checking whether anyone is stepping off the curb.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.question_text: Why must you never stop across a crosswalk or whip around another car paused beside one?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.teaching_text: A stopped SUV in the next lane often screens a pedestrian walking straight into your passing lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.question_text: Around parked cars, busy gathering spots, and backing maneuvers, what pedestrian habits protect lives?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.teaching_text: Schools, parks, bus stops, lots, and parked doors produce unpredictable foot traffic from every blind angle.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.question_text: Which three driver faculties can a distraction pull away, and how do mental distractions compare with physical ones?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.teaching_text: Daydreaming or heated thoughts blind hazard recognition just like taking hands off the wheel or fiddling with dials.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.question_text: Which seven everyday eating, grooming, smoking, or audio habits does Colorado tell drivers to skip while moving?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.teaching_text: Unwrapping food, vaping, reading, or hunting playlists steals critical seconds of vision and steering grip.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.question_text: Why does a minor cabin distraction turn far deadlier when alcohol, cannabis, or drugs are involved?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.teaching_text: Impaired brains cannot divide attention across steering, speed, and sudden hazards when a distraction steals focus.

sec14-card-sec14-F35.question_text: When may adult Colorado drivers use a mobile electronic device, and what penalties follow careless manual texting?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.teaching_text: Pulling safely off the road beats risking fines or criminal misdemeanor careless-driving charges for manual phone use.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.question_text: What legal trouble can manual phone use or texting trigger if it makes your driving careless?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.teaching_text: Even though hands-free audio is permitted, manual screen tapping that causes erratic driving invites misdemeanor prosecution.

sec14-card-sec14-F36.question_text: How should you handle kids, pets, audio presets, cabin controls, and navigation before shifting into drive?
sec14-card-sec14-F36.teaching_text: Securing pets in carriers, learning switches, loading playlists, and mapping routes parked keeps your whole drive calm.

sec14-card-sec14-F37.question_text: What makes dangerous behavior behind the wheel count as aggressive driving in Colorado?
sec14-card-sec14-F37.teaching_text: Deliberate disregard for safety separates willful road aggression from an unintended mistake.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.question_text: How does Colorado define reckless driving, and must a driver intend harm to commit it?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.teaching_text: Saying you never meant to hurt anyone offers zero defense once your driving endangers people or property.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.question_text: When can a Colorado officer cite you for reckless driving, and how many record points can follow conviction?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.teaching_text: Stacking up to eight license points from one reckless conviction pushes a driver rapidly toward suspension.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.question_text: When do tailgating, shoulder passing, red-light running, or angry combinations count as aggressive driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.teaching_text: Combining speeding, weaving, honking, flashing lights, or rude gestures shows willful hostility rather than simple error.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.question_text: What mental state separates aggressive driving from reckless driving under Colorado's handbook?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.teaching_text: Careless speed without malice still triggers reckless charges, whereas willful acts define aggressive driving.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.question_text: Which three hostile acts toward another motorist escalate past traffic tickets into criminal charges?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.teaching_text: Brandishing a weapon, intentionally bumping a car, or pursuing someone fast triggers felony or criminal prosecution.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.question_text: What four non-engagement habits protect you when an aggressive driver targets your lane?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.teaching_text: Refusing eye contact, skipping retaliation, easing back, and letting them pass starves road rage of fuel.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.question_text: Which cabin behaviors, from muttering insults and blocking merges to confronting someone, warn of aggressive driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.teaching_text: Even everyday drivers slip into road aggression when frustration turns into blocking lanes, angry speeding, or yelling.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.question_text: Answering yes to how many aggressive-driving self-check questions signals real personal risk?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.teaching_text: You do not need every road-rage habit on the list before anger starts compromising your judgment.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.question_text: Which five pre-trip and on-road mindset choices prevent you from turning into an aggressive driver?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.teaching_text: Padding travel time, expecting human errors, parking outside stress, and letting rude mergers in keeps tempers cool.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.question_text: When a crash suddenly looks likely ahead, why is freezing in panic the worst response?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.teaching_text: Even in the final second before impact, steering or braking reduces crash energy far better than freezing.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.question_text: What are the three fundamental maneuvers for avoiding an impending collision?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.teaching_text: Knowing braking is only one of three options keeps your eyes open for open-lane steering or throttle escapes.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.question_text: Between stopping dead and steering around a sudden obstacle, which works faster and how do you hold the wheel?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.teaching_text: At highway speed a car swerves clear in far fewer feet than full braking needs when adjacent space is clear.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.question_text: If an oncoming car drifts into your lane, how does leaving the roadway compare with taking a head-on hit?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.teaching_text: Combined closing speeds make head-on collisions uniquely lethal compared with controlled off-road runoffs.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.question_text: In what crash-threat scenario is pressing the gas, followed by easing back down, your safest escape?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.teaching_text: Pulling forward into empty pavement clears the impact zone when someone is about to T-bone or rear-end you.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.question_text: Where and during what daily window do roughly ninety percent of Colorado deer and elk crashes happen?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.teaching_text: Twilight and nighttime wildlife movement makes slowing down at yellow animal-crossing signs critical in mountain corridors.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.question_text: Why can holding your lane and striking a deer or elk be safer than jerking the wheel sharply?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.teaching_text: Violent swerves launch cars into oncoming trucks, trees, or rollovers, whereas staying straight preserves control.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.question_text: Pair Colorado's two counter-intuitive survival choices for large animals on the road versus oncoming head-on threats?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.teaching_text: Avoiding wild swerves for wildlife while choosing shoulders over head-on steel picks the lower-energy outcome both times.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.question_text: How do you brake for a panic stop with anti-lock brakes, even when the pedal vibrates or pushes back?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.teaching_text: Lifting your foot when the ABS pedal pulses shuts off computer wheel-pumping and lengthens your stop.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.question_text: Without anti-lock brakes, how hard should you press the pedal, and how do you recover if wheels lock?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.teaching_text: Sliding locked tires lose stopping grip and steering, so easing off briefly lets tread bite again.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.question_text: Contrast your footwork during an emergency stop in an ABS car versus a car without ABS?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.teaching_text: Pumping ABS brakes wastes stopping power, whereas holding non-ABS brakes locked sends you skidding straight.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.question_text: What steering advantage do anti-lock brakes preserve during hard emergency braking?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.teaching_text: Keeping front tires rolling instead of skidding lets you steer around an obstacle while shedding speed.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.question_text: How do you execute an emergency turn in a vehicle without anti-lock brakes so it does not plow straight?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.teaching_text: Locked front tires or yanking the wheel too sharply makes a non-ABS car slide straight into the hazard.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.question_text: Put slowing, releasing the brake pedal, and steering away in exact sequence for a non-ABS evasive turn?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.teaching_text: Separating braking from turning gives non-ABS front tires 100 percent of their traction for steering clear.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.question_text: What simple ownership habit sharply cuts the odds of mechanical failure on the road?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.teaching_text: Routine fluid, belt, tire, and brake checks catch worn parts in the driveway rather than at seventy miles per hour.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.question_text: Walk through the step-by-step recovery if your service brakes fail, and may you keep driving afterward?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.teaching_text: Pumping may rebuild hydraulic pressure, while gradual parking-brake pull and lower gears bring you safely off-road for good.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.question_text: If your gas pedal sticks down at speed, what gear move comes before pulling off and shutting down?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.teaching_text: Shifting straight to neutral disconnects racing engine power while keeping power steering and brakes alive until parked.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.question_text: Contrast your immediate mechanical response to failed brakes against a jammed gas pedal?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.teaching_text: Failed brakes need pumping, gradual parking brake, and lower gears, whereas a runaway throttle needs instant neutral.
sec15-card-sec15-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Failed brakes pump; stuck gas neutral

visual_sync.text_span: Failed brakes pump; stuck gas neutral

sec15-card-sec15-F23.question_text: When a tire blows out at speed, how should you handle steering, gas, and brakes until off the road?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.teaching_text: Holding a firm straight line while easing off throttle and braking gently keeps a shredded tire from spinning the car.
sec15-card-sec15-F23.must_match_memory_hook: Grip straight, lift gas, light brake

visual_sync.text_span: Grip straight, lift gas, light brake

sec15-card-sec15-R05.question_text: Why must you resist slamming the brakes or stopping right in a travel lane during a tire blowout?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.teaching_text: Stomping the brake on a blown tire jerks steering violently sideways and risks getting rear-ended in live traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.question_text: If your engine stalls and power assist cuts out while rolling, do steering and brakes still work?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.teaching_text: Mechanical linkages stay connected without power boost, so pulling hard on the wheel and pressing firm stops you safely.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.question_text: If your headlights suddenly go dark at night, what steps help you see and get off the road?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.teaching_text: Flipping hazard flashers, turn signals, or fog lamps throws enough emergency glow to guide you onto the shoulder.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.question_text: Where must a driver involved in a Colorado crash present proof of insurance to law enforcement?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.teaching_text: Colorado requires verifying active liability coverage with officers either roadside after impact or later at the station.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.question_text: When an injured driver is physically unable to report a crash, whose legal duty steps in?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.teaching_text: Colorado shifts reporting responsibility onto an able passenger, including remaining at the scene if officers direct.
sec15-card-sec15-F28.must_match_memory_hook: Passenger reports and stays if told

visual_sync.text_span: Passenger reports and stays if told

sec15-card-sec15-F29.question_text: What immediate stop, aid, reporting, and information-exchange duties apply after any traffic crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F29.teaching_text: Fleeing turns an accident into a hit-and-run crime; stay put, render practical aid, call police, and trade records.

sec15-card-sec15-F31.question_text: If you bump an unattended parked car and cannot locate its owner, what two actions are required?
sec15-card-sec15-F31.teaching_text: Leaving a visible note alone falls short in Colorado unless you also notify law enforcement.

sec15-card-sec15-F30.question_text: During severe-weather Accident Alert Status, how do sober, uninjured drivers with drivable cars handle a crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F30.teaching_text: When storm calls overwhelm police, qualifying minor-crash drivers clear out after trading info and file within a day.

sec15-card-sec15-F32.question_text: After a minor divided-highway crash with drivable cars and zero injuries or impairment, what must drivers do?
sec15-card-sec15-F32.teaching_text: Leaving drivable cars parked in fast freeway lanes triggers deadly secondary pileups, and moving them carries zero fault penalty.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.question_text: With drivable cars and zero injuries or impairment, how does the Move It Law differ from Accident Alert Status?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.teaching_text: One rule clears divided-highway lanes immediately, while storm-time Accident Alert lets drivers swap info and report within twenty-four hours.
sec15-card-sec15-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Move It clears; Alert reports later

visual_sync.text_span: Move It clears; Alert reports later

sec15-card-sec15-F33.question_text: When passing any stopped highway vehicle flashing its hazards, what lane change or speed drop does Colorado require?
sec15-card-sec15-F33.teaching_text: Colorado protects every hazard-flashing roadside vehicle, not just police, with a lane buffer or twenty-mile-per-hour speed cut.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.question_text: Under Colorado's Move Over Law, when do you drop at least twenty miles per hour below the limit instead of changing lanes?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.teaching_text: Heavy adjacent traffic or a single lane each way triggers the mandatory twenty-below-posted slowdown past flashing hazards.

sec15-card-sec15-F34.question_text: What standard of care do Good Samaritan laws expect, and how do they shield everyday crash rescuers?
sec15-card-sec15-F34.teaching_text: Helping sensibly within your training protects good-faith bystanders from civil lawsuits and financial liability.

sec15-card-sec15-F35.question_text: When may a bystander move an injured crash victim, and what consent, check, call, and care rules apply?
sec15-card-sec15-F35.teaching_text: Unnecessary movement worsens spinal trauma, so ask conscious victims first, check life threats, dial emergency help, and stay.
sec15-card-sec15-F35.must_match_memory_hook: Move for danger; ask, call, stay

visual_sync.text_span: Move for danger; ask, call, stay

sec15-card-sec15-F36.question_text: What card mark and registry enrollment happen when you say yes to organ, eye, and tissue donation at licensing?
sec15-card-sec15-F36.teaching_text: Saying yes prints a small Y-heart emblem on your credential and keeps you on Donate Life Colorado until changed.

sec15-card-sec15-F37.question_text: Whose names honor Colorado's voluntary licensing donation fund, and what does that money support?
sec15-card-sec15-F37.teaching_text: Optional contributions at licensing finance statewide public outreach for the Emily Keyes and John W. Buckner fund.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: What minimum age and credential do you need to operate a car, motor-driven cycle, or moped on Colorado public roads?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Even low-powered mopeds and motor-driven cycles require full age-sixteen licensing once tires touch public pavement.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: Which three examples involving business, living stretch, or employment make Colorado count you as a state resident?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Taking a local job or opening a shop makes you a resident immediately without waiting out ninety days.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: How many days after becoming a Colorado resident do you have to obtain a Colorado driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Driving past that first month on an out-of-state card leaves a new resident unlicensed under state rules.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: Which three groups living in Colorado are exempt from the thirty-day new-resident licensing deadline?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Service members, their families, and out-of-state college students keep valid home-state licenses while stationed or studying here.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: Within how many days must you notify the DMV after changing your name or home address?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Missed renewal reminders or legal notices mailed to an old address never excuse driving on an expired record.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: How do Colorado's thirty-day licensing and record-update deadlines contrast with the ninety-day continuous-living rule?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Test questions swap thirty and ninety constantly, so pair ninety days with residency status and thirty days with DMV paperwork.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: Which handbook topics appear on the written knowledge exam, and where can you take official practice quizzes?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Studying only road signs leaves huge blind spots when DUI rules, safety habits, and legal questions hit your screen.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: How long before scheduled closing do offices stop starting written knowledge exams?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Walking through the door twenty minutes before closing means turning right back around without taking your test.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: How does the number thirty work differently for the written-test office cutoff than for residency and address rules?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Spotting the unit word separates a daily office cutoff before closing from a month-long legal filing window.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: What credential do you qualify for once you pass the written exam, and what does it grant?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Passing the computer test never lets you drive solo; it unlocks supervised practice under learner limits.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: What age, license status, and seating position are required for your supervising driver while you use an instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Having an adult in the back seat or someone holding an expired card leaves a learner driving illegally.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: How does Colorado's general minimum age to drive compare with the minimum age to supervise a permit holder?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: An eighteen-year-old friend can legally drive their own car yet still cannot supervise a learner beside them.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: Who administers most Colorado drive tests since state driver license offices do not currently schedule them?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Showing up at a state DMV counter expecting a road test wastes a trip when commercial schools and select counties run them.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: Which vehicle parts and documents does the examiner verify before your road test can roll?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: A burned-out brake bulb, stuck interior door handle, or expired registration cancels your drive test in the parking lot.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: Who is allowed inside the vehicle during a drive test, and what items or electronics must be removed, cleared, or turned off?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Phones buzzing, pets in the back, or charms swinging from the mirror all violate strict test-cabin rules.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: How soon may you take another shot at the drive test if you do not pass?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Same-day retests are off-limits, giving you overnight breathing room to fix whatever cost you points.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: What mandatory waiting rule applies to anyone who fails the driving skills test?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Friday afternoon failures mean waiting until Monday morning or the next open business day to retest.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: Will an examiner ever trick you into breaking a traffic law, and when should you ask questions?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Every second on the route is scored, so chatting mid-drive pulls focus right when you need sharp scanning.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: Which three AAMVA skill categories does Colorado's drive test evaluate, and what does each cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Smooth steering alone will not pass if you miss traffic gaps or fail to shift focus across hazards.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: Which six everyday traffic maneuvers combine to build your Colorado drive-test score?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Notice there are no trick stunts here; examiners grade routine intersections, lane changes, turns, and merges.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: At which three stages of driving does the examiner grade whether you picked the proper lane?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Drifting wide into an adjacent lane at the end of a turn loses lane-selection points immediately.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: What lane-tracking and steering-wheel habits are graded under lane management during turns?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Palming the wheel one-handed or letting tires drift across turn lines costs easy lane-management points.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: From which part of your lane should you initiate a right turn versus a left turn?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Tucking toward your turning edge blocks impatient bikes or cars from squeezing inside your turn path.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: Where in the receiving lane should your car settle after a turn, and what two contact errors must you avoid?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Clipping a corner curb or swinging across painted lane stripes signals poor speed and steering control.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: Put together the exact starting edge and finishing lane position expected on right and left turns?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Hugging your turn side going in and centering cleanly coming out earns full marks on every corner.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: For how many feet before turning or switching lanes must your blinker run in urban areas versus on four-lane highways?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Faster multi-lane traffic covers ground twice as fast, requiring double the advance warning distance.
sec01-card-sec01-F21.must_match_memory_hook: One hundred town, two hundred highway

visual_sync.text_span: One hundred town, two hundred highway

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: Within how many seconds after completing a turn or lane change must you cancel your turn signal?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Cruising down the block with a forgotten blinker tricks cross-street drivers into pulling out right in front of you.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: Combine Colorado's urban and four-lane highway signal distances with the post-move cancellation timer?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Locking those three numbers together covers both how early your blinker goes on and how fast it clicks off.
sec01-card-sec01-R06.must_match_memory_hook: One hundred, two hundred, three seconds

visual_sync.text_span: One hundred, two hundred, three seconds

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: What three smooth habits demonstrate proper speed control when slowing, changing lanes, and entering turns?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Stomping the brake halfway through a corner upsets tire grip and signals you entered the intersection too fast.
sec01-card-sec01-F23.must_match_memory_hook: Smooth slowing, steady lanes, slow entry

visual_sync.text_span: Smooth slowing, steady lanes, slow entry

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: What three checks define a proper stop regarding motion, pavement lines, and front-wheel angle?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: Pre-turning your front wheels while waiting for a gap can shove you straight into oncoming traffic if rear-ended.
sec01-card-sec01-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Full halt, behind lines, wheels straight

visual_sync.text_span: Full halt, behind lines, wheels straight

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: What visual cue tells you that you stopped far enough behind the vehicle ahead in traffic?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.teaching_text: Leaving that tire-to-asphalt buffer prevents a domino rear-end hit and gives room to steer around a stall.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.question_text: Which six rough or sluggish mistakes must you avoid while accelerating on the drive test?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.teaching_text: Jerky launches, coasting, gear grinding, or crawling below traffic flow all cost motor-control points.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.question_text: Which five scanning, mirror, shoulder, and intersection checks make up proper visual searching?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.teaching_text: Checking behind in your mirror after finishing every turn catches fast-closing traffic on your new road.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.question_text: How are backup cameras and blind-spot or lane alerts treated during the Colorado drive test?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.teaching_text: Staring only at a center screen without turning your head fails the physical searching requirement.
sec01-card-sec01-F28.must_match_memory_hook: Driver aids allowed, head checks required

visual_sync.text_span: Driver aids allowed, head checks required

sec01-card-sec01-F29.question_text: Which form must applicants under eighteen submit, and which adults are eligible to sign it?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.teaching_text: Colorado requires an eligible parent, guardian, adult spouse, or responsible adult to accept financial responsibility in writing.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.question_text: In front of whom is the liability affidavit signed, what happens if the signer withdraws, and who may be exempt?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.teaching_text: Because the signer backs your driving legally, pulling their signature immediately cancels your minor permit or license.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.question_text: What age requirement lets a spouse sign a minor's Affidavit of Liability, and what does withdrawing that signature do?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.teaching_text: Watch the wording carefully on test day because the spouse must be older than eighteen, not merely eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.question_text: For how many months must a minor hold an instruction permit before applying for a Colorado driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.teaching_text: Even if you finish all practice hours early, the full one-year calendar hold cannot be skipped.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.question_text: How many total and nighttime driving hours must appear on a minor applicant's signed driving log?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.teaching_text: Headlight glare and dark depth perception take dedicated practice before solo night privileges kick in.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: Do a minor's ten required night hours add on top of the fifty logged hours or count inside them?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Exam distractors try tricking you into picking sixty total hours, when fifty already includes the ten after dark.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.question_text: Which minor age bracket owes six instructor-led driving hours before licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.teaching_text: Waiting until sixteen and six months drops this instructor behind-the-wheel requirement, making the age cutoff critical.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.question_text: When may twelve extra supervised hours replace the six instructor hours, and what proof do you bring?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.teaching_text: Rural teens beyond thirty miles from a twenty-hour-a-week school swap in twelve family hours plus a printed route map.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: Tie together who owes the six behind-the-wheel instructor hours and when the twelve-hour substitute applies?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Pairing age sixteen-and-a-half with the thirty-mile rural school rule solves both halves of this licensing question.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.question_text: During the first six months with a minor license, what is the rule on carrying passengers under twenty-one?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.teaching_text: Without a parent or licensed adult riding along, peer passengers stay out during your riskiest first half year.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.question_text: How do minor passenger rules open up from six months to one year, and then after one full year?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.teaching_text: Siblings and medical emergencies are exempt during months six through twelve, before full seat-belt capacity unlocks at one year.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: Walk through all three passenger stages across a minor driver's first year and beyond?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: Gradually adding peers at six months and twelve months matches your growing real-world experience.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.question_text: Between which overnight hours is a first-year minor barred from solo driving, and which four exceptions apply?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.teaching_text: Without a parent, guardian, or instructor aboard, overnight drives require a signed school or work note, emergency, or emancipation.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: During the midnight-to-five curfew in year one, what exact proof makes a school or work drive legal?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Telling an officer you just clocked out is not enough without a signed statement from your boss or school.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.question_text: Which three point, impairment, or testing triggers can suspend, revoke, or cancel your driving privilege?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.teaching_text: Even without a conviction for impaired driving, racking up ticket points or refusing a chemical test pulls your license.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.question_text: Which two crash-scene or reporting failures can strip away your Colorado driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.teaching_text: Failing to stop, share details, and help, or ignoring Financial Responsibility reporting rules, costs your license directly.

sec01-card-sec01-F40.question_text: Which five application, judgment, misuse, re-exam, or felony grounds can also cost your license?
sec01-card-sec01-F40.teaching_text: Loaning your card to a friend or skipping a DMV re-exam jeopardizes your license just like court convictions.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.question_text: Why is it wrong to assume only points or impaired driving can cost your license after a collision?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.teaching_text: A completely sober driver with zero points still loses their license for fleeing or skipping required DMV crash reports.
